arms: D-LLM (reference deployment cell). HELD FIXED: the C-hat-only candidate frame; the per-network cap of 20 instances by seeded stride; Z = the canonical GAC-valid set on G0 with r_opt reported separately where O(G0) is identified; the polynomial GAC predicate and the closed-form O; the FWL estimator; the reference statistical panel. VARIES: nothing. Every quantity on its computation path is a functional of (C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n). This is the cell every other arm is read against.

D-LLM' (the replicate elicitation, and the arm the draft did not have). HELD FIXED: instance frame, model family, temperature, cache discipline, granularities, everything except one integer. VARIES: the prompt's variable-order permutation seed; a second replicate varies the model family instead. Its whole job is to produce kappa-hat_split, the pairwise disagreement rate between two independent elicitations on the same assertions, which is observable without any truth and exists on every instance. It is also the seed-dispersion source for the knowledge arm: without it every rate in the LLM arm would carry a cluster bootstrap over networks and no re-run variance at all, which is the exact error the Sadeghi and AbdAlmageed audit punishes.

D-PUB (T2 only, and honestly scoped). HELD FIXED: the instance frame, byte-identical to D-LLM on the same eight networks. VARIES: the knowledge source, harvested from the eight author-named source publications under an LLM-reader-first, human-adjudicator protocol with page-anchored verbatim quotes, every assertion dropped if its quote is not verbatim. Coverage per granularity is an outcome, not a setting. This arm exists on roughly 160 instances over 8 networks and is declared underpowered for the paired 11.1-point test before it runs.

D-TRUE (the MISSING control the ledger's checkable 14 names and the draft omitted): knowledge that is consistent AND true but INCOMPLETE. HELD FIXED: the instance frame. VARIES: K is drawn from true orientations only, matched per instance to the paired D-LLM elicitation on two things at once, |K| and the histogram of graph distance from X to each assertion, so that the false arms are read against a true arm of the same size and the same placement. Unmatched on those two, every LLM-versus-true comparison would repeat the coverage-strata confound: admissible instances collapse 543 to 182 to 106 as coverage falls and survivors have systematically larger separation, so a bare coverage contrast measures composition and not knowledge.

D-SYN (the labelled synthetic negative control, with a KNOWN error process). HELD FIXED: instance frame, and the K of D-TRUE as the uncorrupted starting point. VARIES: the tiered correlated corruption operator already sitting unused in synth/knowledge.py, which misfiles a node into a wrong temporal tier before assertions are read off, so one mistake flips several claims at once, applied at declared rates {0.10, 0.25, 0.50} with realised post-filter wrongness recorded separately from intended (the existing corpus measures 6.8% realised for an intended 10%). This is the only arm whose error process is known by construction, so it is the calibration input for A6-1: a two-sample discriminator that cannot separate D-SYN at 0.50 from D-TRUE has no power and its verdict on the real sources means nothing.

D-NULL (K empty). HELD FIXED: everything. VARIES: knowledge removed. Purpose: separate 'the radius is large' from 'the knowledge was vacuous'. Under the fixed-frame rule this arm keeps the same denominator as every other, so its enormous O-unidentified status count is a reported outcome rather than a silent shrinkage of the population, which is what makes it comparable at all.

A-ORACLE (audit-only yardstick). HELD FIXED: the instance frame and the computed radii. VARIES: K is the old knowledge_to_recover set, greedy and cascade-maximising, which at coverage 1.0 makes G0 identical to the true DAG in 543 of 831 instances. Manifest flag true_dag_on_path = true. It appears only in the greyed block, is never quoted as a deployment number, and keeps exactly one job: scoring the error of every elicited K.

A-TWIN (the post-hoc audit twin of every deployment arm). HELD FIXED: instance set, knowledge, computed radius, witness set. VARIES: the truth is revealed, and only afterwards, to compute the consistent-but-false rate on the post-filter K, the three-rate decomposition (reversed, omitted, invented) with commission and omission on separate axes, error as a function of distance from X and of edge type, the wrong-assertion clustering permutation test, the stated-confidence calibration curve, the unimplemented {ORIENTATION, ANCESTRAL, TIER, SPURIOUS, MISSING} x {BENIGN, EFFICIENCY, VALIDITY, UNIDENTIFIABLE} classification, and the three-bucket certificate check.

X-CONTAM (audit-arm instrument, moved out of the deployment path). HELD FIXED: prompt template, temperature 0, one pass, cache, refinement budget 0. VARIES: naming condition (real names, scrambled names, cold recall with no data) crossed with two model families. Its accuracy-gap flag requires the truth, so it may not restratify any deployment number; the deployment arm instead carries the truth-free twin, the named-versus-scrambled AGREEMENT rate between two elicitations, which needs no ground truth and is reported as a column. The accuracy-based flag stratifies the AUDIT block only.

N-ER-MATCHED (instrument calibration, explicitly not a substrate tier, so Decision 2 stands). HELD FIXED: the entire pipeline, one K function, one validity predicate, one query frame, one coverage handling, and a committed generator script, which is what the current comparator has never had. VARIES: the generator and its density cell, restricted to the real corpus's degree band 1.60 to 9.86, per n, with seed dispersion. Its only job is the A6-3 power check. It never enters the denominator of a substrate claim.

P-ORACLE and P-EST(Pi). The two statistical panels. HELD FIXED: substrate, knowledge, geometry, estimator. VARIES: C-hat alone. P-ORACLE carries manifest flag true_dag_on_path = via_Chat_only, because the oracle CPDAG IS a functional of the true DAG and calling that panel deployment-clean would be the invariant violation the whole redesign exists to remove. P-EST is the only panel a deployment claim may be stated in. Networks whose parameters are fitted to real measurements (the four bnjson) are the parameter-faithful cell; everywhere else the linear-Gaussian parameters are ours and the label says so, with a var- and R-squared-sortability profile per cell.

C-COUNT-A and C-COUNT-B (the H4 baseline, pre-registered and unrun for six sessions, and split because the repository's two quantities are not the same object). C-COUNT-A is |K|, the number of assertions the analyst actually made. C-COUNT-B is |K_G0|, which the code computes as the number of CPDAG-undirected edges that G0 orients, i.e. the closure size, inflated by cascade. HELD FIXED: the instance. VARIES: the instrument. Reporting them as one number, which the draft did, would hide the cascade factor that is itself checkable 12's emitted statistic.

C-ROCA. The Su and Henckel over-identification test, run on every instance where G0 admits at least two valid adjustment sets. HELD FIXED: instance, Sigma-hat, n, and the graph the test runs against. VARIES: the instrument. It is simultaneously a comparator and the source of kappa-hat_RoCA.

C-ENSEMBLE. Hu and van der Pas's P_A = sum_G 1{A valid in G} P(G | D, M) over the same enumerated sub-poset with a declared prior. HELD FIXED: the sub-poset, the instance set, the audited truth. VARIES: worst-case radius against posterior average, compared on a DECISION at a declared threshold. The draft's committed prediction that the posterior wins on average and the radius wins in the tail is withdrawn as untestable here: the whole r >= 5 population of the committed corpus is 16 instances and all 16 are in one network.

C-SOFT. A RoaDS-shaped soft credibility penalty over the same K. HELD FIXED: the instance and K. VARIES: hard-constraint radius against soft-penalty score, compared by rank correlation against audited per-assertion correctness.

axes.cost: Compute: CPDAG over all 39 parsing networks is measured at 60.95 s total; the sortability profile on the networks carrying continuous parameters is seconds. The matched ER control is 3 density cells x 6 sizes x 10 seeds of small graphs through the full pipeline, of the order of 4 wall-hours on 8 cores, and it now carries a committed generator script. Human: 2 hours to write the tier assignment, the illustration argument and the M-bias expansion, which is a text file and a re-parse, not a search. CUT AND RECORDED: the T2 expansion from 8 to 25 applied networks, 25 to 35 human-hours of harvesting and provenance work, is REMOVED from this protocol and declared an extension. Its removal is what makes A6-2 underpowered per tier, which is stated in A6 rather than absorbed.
axes.decision: Four tiers, and the fourth is the one the draft missed. T0 ILLUSTRATION: the dagitty pedagogical files paths, confounding, mediator, plus M-bias recovered as `M-bias-expanded` (each `<->` becomes an explicit latent parent, provenance recorded as ours, the ADMG original still excluded with the argument attached). These are textbook drawings, not networks anybody fitted or elicited, and they are reported as a separate stratum that is NEVER pooled into any headline. The reason is measured, not stylistic: of the 831 admissible instances in the committed corpus, all 16 with r >= 5 are in `paths`, a 17-node dagitty illustration whose CPDAG is 73.7% undirected and whose single chain component has 15 nodes, i.e. a spine. Remove the three illustrations and the maximum radius over the remaining 807 instances is 4, and 94.4% of them sit at r <= 2. The sentence in circulation, that real structure reaches radius 14 against a synthetic maximum of 4 or 5, is therefore a comparison of two designed spines, and on the corrected reading the real corpus minus one textbook drawing has a SMALLER maximum radius than the random generators the ledger recomputed at 5. T1 BENCHMARK: the 24 BIF networks from the single pgmpy 1.0.0 sdist, which is a corpus claim and is labelled one. T2 APPLIED-PAPER: the 8 author-named dagitty DAGs (Acid_1996, Didelez_2010, Kampen_2014, Polzer_2012, Schipf_2010, Sebastiani_2005, Shrier_2008, Thoemmes_2013) carrying their own source publications; the expansion toward 25 networks is CUT from this protocol and declared an extension, with the power consequence written in A6 rather than hidden. T3 REAL-PARAMETER: the four bnjson networks whose coefficients are fits to real measurements (ecoli70, arth150, magic-niab, magic-irri), plus Sachs used as an evaluation referent with an explicit written refusal to report precision and recall against its reference graph. A matched Erdos-Renyi arm is retained but is NOT a substrate tier: it is instrument calibration for the A6-3 power check, labelled as such everywhere, and never in the denominator of a substrate claim. That is the reconciling sentence Decision 2 needs and it is written once. Before any radius is reported the substrate section prints, per network: mean degree (corpus range 1.60 to 9.86, median 2.92), undirected fraction (median 0.107, six networks fully compelled), maximum chain-component size (85, pathfinder), the number of chain components and nodes inside them (276 components holding 969 of 7,062 nodes on 33 of 39 networks), the separation distribution, and var- and R-squared-sortability wherever continuous parameters exist. On the 24 discrete BIF networks sortability is undefined and that is printed as a status. Every substrate statistic computed from the true DAG carries manifest flag arm = substrate_design, a THIRD value the draft's binary {deployment, audit} field could not express: these numbers use the truth, they describe the corpus, and they are never on r's computation path.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE MATCHED-CONTROL CHECK, restated on the correct denominator, which is where the draft repeated a confound the ledger had already flagged. Separation >= 2 is 45.4% of the 463 instances where separation is MEASURABLE and 25.3% of the full 831; the comparator's figure is computed on its own measurable subset, and the undefined rate differs 2.6-fold between the arms (44.3% real against 17.1% random). Comparing 45.4 against any synthetic figure conditions each side on a differently selected subset. DECISION RULE: the comparison is stated on the FULL denominator only, as a three-level composition (undefined / 1 / >= 2) per generator, per density cell, per n, with seed dispersion, never pooled across generators. If the matched control's >= 2 share on its full denominator has a 95% interval overlapping the real corpus's 25.3%, the non-exchangeability claim is retired, the finding is restated as a density-tuning result, and the topology point is cited to Stuempel et al. (arXiv:2501.02019) rather than claimed. SECOND RULE, the illustration gate: report max radius and the r >= 3 count twice, with and without T0. If no network outside T0 produces an instance at r >= 5 under real elicited knowledge, the paper states plainly that the certificate's measured range on real structure is {1,2,3,4}, and every sentence about large radii is a sentence about a textbook drawing. In the committed corpus that is already true: 63 instances at r >= 3, of which 45 outside T0, and zero outside T0 at r >= 5. THIRD RULE, sortability: any arm carrying continuous parameters showing var-sortability above 0.94 has its parameterisation replaced (iSCM with R-squared-sortability per density cell because iSCM reverses it on denser graphs, or UUMC) before a single result is reported. FOURTH RULE, M-bias: if M-bias-expanded yields no admissible instance in which a consistent K makes O(G0) open a collider path, the recovery bought nothing and is recorded as a negative result with that sentence.
axes.justification: Decision 2 fixes the tiers and this decomposition respects it, adding only the separation of pedagogical drawings from fitted and applied networks, which is the same no-pooling rule the ledger already enforces on the synthetic side (pooling the designed backdoor family with five random generators moved an r=1 headline from 79.6% to 65.3%, a 14-point swing produced entirely by pooling). The illustration finding is derived here from results/axisa3/instances.jsonl and descriptive_structure.csv, not asserted: `paths` is source_format dagitty, 17 nodes, 19 edges, undirected fraction 0.7368, one component of 15, and it supplies 20 of 831 instances, all 16 of the r >= 5 population, and 13 of the 126 exceptions to r = min(s, |K_G0|). Reisach et al. (arXiv:2102.13647, arXiv:2303.18211) make an unreported sortability profile the cheapest way to lose a substrate section, and Myriam Tami is a MICS colleague and plausible reviewer. Herman et al. CLeaR 2025 (arXiv:2503.17037) supply the form of the argument: name the statistic, say what it should physically be, then measure it. Chen et al. ICLR 2022 (arXiv:2110.03239) give the transfer sentence to use in place of 'ER is unrealistic': zero-sample transfer succeeds if and only if the target lies in the support of the randomisation distribution. M-bias is the textbook structure in which a consistent-looking adjustment choice opens a collider path, which is exactly the failure this framework prices, and the ledger records its exclusion as a parse-flag default rather than an argument.

axes.cost: Compute: the frame is bounded by arithmetic already in the committed summary. Of 115,974 ordered pairs screened, 66,330 fail the X-side component test, leaving 49,644 whose X the frame proposes; the true-descendant filter then removed 42,618, so the observables-only frame, whose possde is a superset of de, yields between 7,026 and 49,644 candidates, i.e. order 10^4, and possde is one O(V+E) search per X. After the per-network cap of 20 the measured instance set is roughly 500. Radii on that set are free: 831 exact radii cost 7.2 s in total, 8.7 ms each, slowest single instance 0.16 s. The 1,200 s wall cap that pathfinder exhausted three times without producing a radius should disappear, and its disappearance is itself a check. Order of minutes per full pass. Human: about 4 hours to wire the attrs field through dagitty.py and parsed.py, rewrite the _meta schema with the four separate fields and the status vocabulary, and commit the pre-registered direction before the run.
axes.decision: Replace 'screen all n(n-1) ordered pairs' with a frame that reads C-hat and NOTHING ELSE, and this is the correction that matters most, because the draft's frame read G0. (1) X is drawn from the nodes lying in or adjacent to a chain component of C-hat of size >= 2: across the 39 parsing networks that is 969 nodes of 7,062, in 276 components, on 33 networks. (2) Y is drawn from possde(X, C-hat) minus {X}. NOT possde(X, G0). G0 = Meek(C-hat, K) depends on the knowledge, so a G0-based frame gives every knowledge arm a different candidate set, the paired instances stop being paired, and the K-empty arm gets the largest frame and the smallest yield. The draft asserted byte-identical instance sets across arms and then defined a frame that cannot deliver them. (3) THE FIXED DENOMINATOR. Every K-dependent condition stops being a filter and becomes a per-instance STATUS on one frozen instance list: knowledge_inconsistent, o_g0_not_identified, o_g0_empty, z_invalid_at_g0, budget_censored. Every arm reports the same denominator with a different status composition, and the composition is a printed column. This is what makes D-NULL, D-TRUE, D-SYN and D-LLM comparable at all, and it is the same discipline the ledger demands when it records that coverage strata are non-comparable populations. (4) The three DAG-reading filters are DELETED from the deployment path: no_causal_path (42,618 pairs, tested on dag.descendants), no_valid_adjustment_set, and empty_set_trivially_valid (3,738); no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity (1,659) is deleted too, and note it is doubly disqualified because fast_gate computes its k_true by calling knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag) inside the gate itself. Instances the old gate removed now report a status, never a rejection. (5) THE CERTIFIED SET IS NOT ALWAYS O. Under real, partial knowledge G0 keeps undirected edges and O(G0) is unidentified whenever the extensions disagree; with fully informative oracle K that status already fires 518 times, and under sparse elicited K it could take the majority of the corpus. So Z is defined as the canonical GAC-valid adjustment set on G0, which exists whenever any valid set does, and r_opt against O(G0) is reported as a SECOND radius on the sub-population where O(G0) is identified. Without this the protocol risks producing almost no instances and discovering it after the elicitation budget is spent. (6) PER-NETWORK CAP OF 20, by seeded deterministic stride over the sorted candidate list, never a function of any computed radius. Derived, not chosen: instances inside a network are clustered, and with an intra-cluster correlation of 0.1 the design effect is 1 + (m-1) x 0.1, so m = 20 gives 2.9 while the committed corpus's actual shape (barley 189, insurance 160, diabetes 89, Polzer_2012 66, magic-niab 48, i.e. 552 of 831 from five networks) gives a design effect above 10 and destroys the power of every headline. (7) Two new per-instance fields: the number of valid adjustment sets G0 admits, counted with early exit at 2 because that is all the over-identification test needs, with the full count recorded only where the component's undirected count is under the declared cap; and the boolean for >= 2. (8) The dagitty parser's discarded attrs capture group is wired into ParsedNetwork, delivering the author-declared (X,Y) stratum the pre-registration promised and never got: 12 of 12 files carry exactly one exposure and one outcome, and Didelez_2010 carries the one published expert's own adjustment set {Age, Smo}. A separate labelled stratum, never the headline. (9) Every aggregate twice, pair-weighted and network-weighted, per network first, zero-yield networks in the denominator, with a 95% cluster bootstrap over networks at B = 2,000 AND a separate seed standard deviation from the replicate arms, because a cluster bootstrap resamples networks and says nothing about re-run variability, which is the quantity the audit the ledger cites actually measured.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE FILTER-REMOVAL CHECK, direction pre-registered in a commit that predates the run. PREDICTED DIRECTION: the r=1 share FALLS and the UNREACHED status rises above the currently reported 0 of 831, because the deleted no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity filter removed exactly the 1,659 most robust pairs by construction. DECISION RULE: if the r=1 share moves by more than 11.1 points, the distance from the reported 61.1% to 50% at which the sentence 'a majority of instances break at the first retraction' inverts, every radius fraction previously published in this lineage is a statement about a selected population and must be restated with that qualifier; if it moves by less than the cluster-bootstrap interval width, the old filters were harmless, and that is one sentence and no more. SECOND RULE, guarding the frame: report the separation composition (undefined / 1 / >= 2) over all screened candidates and over the frame's survivors. If the survivors' distribution is stochastically larger, the frame selects for pairs where the radius is trivially defined and is re-specified; the pre-registered tolerance is that the two medians agree and their Kolmogorov-Smirnov statistic falls below the value a same-size permutation null exceeds 5% of the time. THIRD RULE, the admissibility gate that decides whether this protocol can run at all: on a pilot of five networks under D-LLM, if fewer than 40% of framed instances reach status ok, the elicited-knowledge deployment arm does not have a population and the budget is not spent; the protocol falls back to reporting r on the canonical GAC-valid set alone, and the O-based r_opt becomes a sub-population result with its share printed. FOURTH RULE: the cap must not itself be the finding. Report every headline at cap 20 and at cap 50 on the same networks; if a headline moves by more than its interval width, the finding is a statement about which networks dominate the sample and is reported that way.
axes.justification: The invariant in brief section 1 forbids true-DAG quantities on the deployment computation path, and the ledger's A2 block enumerates the violating filters with counts verified in results/axisa3/analysis_summary.json (66,330 / 42,618 / 3,738 / 1,659 / 518 / 280, summing with 831 to exactly 115,974). Henckel, Perkovic and Maathuis (arXiv:1907.02435, JRSS-B 84(2):579-599) establish that O* = pa(cn(X,Y)) minus forb(X,Y) is a LOCAL functional, so the query policy determines the answer rather than merely sampling it, which is why the frame must be declared rather than emergent. Schubert, Claassen and Magliacane (LOAD, arXiv:2510.14582) license a strictly local policy by showing O* is recoverable around a target pair without learning the global graph. Su and Henckel (arXiv:2206.07533, verified CONFIRMED) make the valid-set count load-bearing: their over-identification test needs at least two valid sets to have any power. The fixed denominator is forced by the ledger's own measurement that admissible instances collapse 543 to 182 to 106 across coverage while survivors gain separation, so a falling r=1 share of 69.8 to 51.1 to 34.0 is composition and not knowledge. The per-network cap is derived from the standard cluster design effect against the measured concentration of the corpus. The canonical-set fallback is licensed because Perkovic et al. (arXiv:1707.02171) give validity on maximal PDAGs directly, while optimality has no intersection fallback, which is precisely why the repository's own optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag returns None on extension disagreement.

axes.cost: Compute: 276 chain-component elicitations for T1 plus T0/T2/T3, times 2 replicates (prompt-order seed and second model family), times 3 naming conditions for the audit-arm contamination screen, is roughly 1,900 calls; four granularities are emitted in one structured response per component rather than four calls. Total of the order of 2,000 to 2,400 cached calls at temperature 0, input volume of the order of 10^6 to 10^7 tokens, a few wall-hours. Human, and this is the item that was cut: the publication harvest is REDUCED from the draft's 50 hours over 8 applied plus 24 BIF plus an expansion to roughly 10 hours over the 8 author-named applied papers only, with the LLM reader producing the candidate extraction first and the human adjudicating page-anchored quotes, so the human step is REVIEW rather than INITIATION. The vault's own measurement is the reason: tasks with someone already waiting close at 54%, tasks that must be initiated at 0% over 40 observations. WHAT THIS CUT COSTS, stated rather than hidden: K-PUB then exists on 8 networks and roughly 160 instances, the BIF-side harvest is not done, and the A6-2 paired test is declared underpowered per tier before it runs.
axes.decision: select_knowledge is DELETED from the deployment path together with its call to knowledge_to_recover, which is greedy and cascade-maximising and at coverage 1.0 makes G0 identical to the true DAG in 543 of 831 instances; note the same oracle call also sits inside fast_gate, so removing it from one place is not enough. It survives only as the post-hoc yardstick, tagged true_dag_on_path. Coverage stops being a swept knob and becomes an OUTCOME of elicitation, reported per granularity. SIX knowledge arms, and the last three are what the draft was missing. K-LLM: an LLM surrogate given variable names and a dataset card and never the graph, using CAUSAL-ORDER and TRIPLET queries rather than pairwise edge queries, one query per chain component, one pass, temperature 0, refinement budget declared as 0, mandatory response cache, prompt text versioned and hashed and stored with the K it produced, model id recorded, K frozen before any r is computed, and the variable order inside the prompt PERMUTED under a declared seed because mention-order bias is documented and an error process assuming independence across assertions is misspecified by construction. K-LLM-REPLICATE: the identical elicitation under a second order seed and, separately, a second model family, which costs one extra pass and buys three things the draft had no source for, namely seed dispersion on every knowledge-arm rate, the truth-free contamination proxy, and kappa-hat_split. K-PUB: assertions harvested from the eight applied source publications, LLM reader first, human adjudicator second, every assertion carrying a page-anchored verbatim quote and dropped if the quote is not verbatim in the source window. K-TRUE: consistent AND TRUE BUT INCOMPLETE, matched per instance to the paired K-LLM on |K| and on the distance-from-X histogram. This is checkable 14 and the draft did not have it: its A-ORACLE arm is true and COMPLETE, which is a different object, and without a size- and placement-matched true arm every claim about false knowledge is confounded with claim count. K-SYN: K-TRUE corrupted by the tiered correlated operator already present and never run on real graphs, at declared rates {0.10, 0.25, 0.50}, with realised post-filter wrongness recorded separately from intended. K-NULL: K empty. Every arm emits all four granularities (required edge, forbidden edge, tier, ancestral), not orientation only. Each K carries a fixed record emitting the ledger's fourteen checkables, and the two the draft left implicit are made explicit: the CONSISTENT-BUT-FALSE RATE, the fraction of post-filter assertions that are false, named as the reporting object rather than folded into 'noise'; and a MAPPING TABLE putting the surrogate's error onto the same scale as CSCD's 0.3 reversal rate and b-LOAD's rho and mu, so the three arms are quantitatively comparable rather than merely adjacent. The rest as recorded: pre-filter K, post-filter K and the Meek Algorithm 1 rejection rate; coverage per granularity, never pooled; distance-from-X distribution rather than a scalar coverage; the three-rate decomposition in the audit arm only; commission and omission as two axes; a permutation test asking whether wrong assertions sit closer together in the graph than a same-count uniform null predicts; error as a function of distance from X and of edge type; cycles emitted before repair; error split by assertion type AND by network; source-reported confidence RETAINED with a calibration curve that must exist in the audit arm before the deployment arm may read confidence at all; and cascade size, edges compelled per assertion, which is also what separates the two count baselines in A6.
axes.falsifiable_check: THREE CHECKS. (a) THE COUNT BASELINE, H4, pre-registered and unrun for six sessions, and SPLIT because the repository's two quantities are different objects: |K| is what the analyst asserted, while the field the code writes as k_g0 counts the CPDAG-undirected edges that G0 orients, i.e. the closure size. Compute the decision agreement of the radius with each, and with min(s, |K_G0|). DECISION RULE: if either count baseline reproduces the radius's decision at every operating point of the audit arm's three-bucket score, the framework is retired to a lemma about counting. There is prior evidence the baseline is not trivially right and it cuts against a naive bound: analysis_summary.json records the law tested on 463 instances with 337 agreeing, 110 where the radius EXCEEDS min(s, |K_G0|) and 16 below, so that quantity is neither an upper bound nor a deterministic predictor on real structure, contrary to how it is described in the surrounding prose. That contradiction between the analysis file and the framing text is itself pre-registered as a thing to resolve before the baseline is reported. (b) THE INCONSISTENCY-EXISTS CHECK, which is the cheapest falsifier of the whole knowledge model. Of 115,974 pairs screened with oracle-derived K, knowledge_inconsistent fired ZERO times and z_invalid_at_g0 fired zero times: neither appears in the rejection tally, whose six entries sum with 831 to exactly 115,974. So the consistency-survivorship checkable currently has no data at all and kappa-hat_cons is identically zero in the committed corpus. PREDICTION, written first: under elicited K the Meek rejection rate is strictly positive on a majority of networks. DECISION RULE: if it is zero or near-zero under real elicitation too, then either the elicitation is too sparse to contradict itself, in which case coverage is reported as the binding limitation and kappa-hat_cons is dropped as a referent, or the surrogate is reciting a consistent structure, which routes to check (c). (c) THE RECITATION CHECK. Chance on a triplet-order query over three nodes is one in six. A network is FLAGGED when its named-minus-scrambled orientation accuracy gap exceeds the binomial 95% upper bound at that network's realised query count AND cold recall reproduces the published adjacency above chance. DECISION RULE: flagged networks move to a separately reported stratum in the AUDIT block and are never pooled, on the verified precedent that pooling a designed family with random ones moved an r=1 headline 14 points. If more than half of T1's instances land flagged, the surrogate arm is a contamination measurement rather than an expertise measurement on the benchmark tier, and the realism claim rests on K-PUB, which after the cut covers 8 networks.
axes.justification: The ledger's A3 block names this the single largest defect against the invariant, with verified counts. Perkovic, Kalisch and Maathuis (arXiv:1707.02171) supply the only admissibility predicate and the reason it is not enough: consistency is purely graphical and syntactic, and their Theorem 4.4 is conditional on G being the true MPDAG, so a merely-consistent-but-false G returns a provably wrong set silently. That silent-failure surface is the object. Vashishtha et al. (arXiv:2310.15117, verified CONFIRMED) force the elicitation form: pairwise edge queries produced over 3,000 cycles on Child and over 5,000 on Neuropathic where triplet and causal-order queries produced none, with SHD falling 177 to 28, and Child, Asia, Alarm, Insurance and Sachs all sit in our own BIF corpus, so a pairwise interface would make part of our measured error process an artefact of our own instrument. Bang and Didelez require per-granularity coverage because tiers close under Meek R1 alone while single-edge assertions cascade through R1 to R4, so equal nominal coverage buys a different closure and therefore a different radius. b-LOAD (arXiv:2607.04447) is our own accepted paper whose noise study is confined to required edges, named by all four reviewers, so covering all four granularities closes a weakness we published. Gervet et al. (JEDM 2020) force the NULL arm: an expert-designed structure added at most 0.01 AUC on seven of nine datasets. CSCD (CDM@UAI 2026) is why confidence is retained rather than hardened: correct hard constraints raised precision (PC 0.802 to 0.850) while noisy hard constraints hurt recall (PC 0.577 to 0.526) and a soft penalty restored it, so an error process that only hardens overstates the damage. AutoElicit (arXiv:2411.17284) fixes the reporting format for a surrogate and nothing about its accuracy. The replicate arm is justified by the ledger's own negative finding that no inter-rater agreement statistic exists for expert-drawn DAGs anywhere in epidemiology or elsewhere, which makes producing one a contribution rather than an overhead.

axes.cost: Compute: the radii are nearly free and this is measured rather than assumed, at 831 exact radii in 7.2 s total. The shell measure on the retraction-subset geometry is bounded by arithmetic: at cap 20,000 full enumeration and ~1 ms per validity call it is at most 20 s per instance in the worst case, and the median case is tiny because the measured radius mass sits at r <= 2 (768 of 831, 92.4%), where C(|K|, j) for j <= 2 and |K| of order 12 is under a hundred. Over roughly 500 instances that is of the order of 1 to 3 core-hours, not the 15 the draft budgeted on an unimplementable geometry. The unit triple and the weighted radius ride the same enumeration for about 20% more. Human: about 6 hours for the sentinel extension and the two-geometry reconciliation. CUT AND RECORDED: the draft's 10 to 15 hours across five unsearched prior-art literatures is reduced to three named searches with pre-written decision rules, about 6 hours, plus the Appendix F.3 retrieval which is cheap and is a hard gate; the remaining two literatures are declared an open prior-art risk in writing rather than silently skipped.
axes.decision: Centre at G0 = Meek(C-hat, K) and never at the truth; this is already correct in code, since breakdown_radius takes no true DAG in its signature and local_up_covers takes (cpdag, g). Operator RETRACTION, derived rather than assumed, because failure is upward-closed: refinement shrinks the represented DAG set, so orienting one more edge can never invalidate a fixed valid Z, and a flip is therefore not primitive but costs two atomic moves. Extend the operator to the granularities that have never had one, a forbidden-edge retraction and a TIER-BLOCK retraction, and state the unit rather than discover it: the radius is denominated in ASSERTIONS, so retracting a tier is ONE atomic move however many orientations it releases. Report the radius in d_L (model inclusion) and in d_L,pseudo (orient and un-orient atomic moves) side by side, with a third column showing what SHD would have certified, purely to display the over-certification on our own instances. Add the O*-relevance-weighted radius as a declared second column: weight 1 for a retraction that changes the certified Z, a declared larger cost otherwise. THE SHELL MEASURE IS DEFINED ON THE RETRACTION-SUBSET GEOMETRY, which is the correction that makes it implementable at all. The draft proposed sampling 400 graphs uniformly from shell j of the covering graph; the covering relation of the MPDAG poset has no known graphical characterisation, stated three times in the source, so neighbours cannot be enumerated and a uniform draw from a poset shell is not a thing one can write. On the retraction geometry shell j is the set of j-subsets of K, which is C(|K|, j), finite, enumerable and uniformly samplable by construction. phi_j is then the fraction of j-subsets whose retraction invalidates Z, by full enumeration when C(|K|, j) <= 20,000 and by 400 uniform j-subsets otherwise, which bounds the Monte Carlo standard error at 0.025, finer than the 0.43 to 0.47 conservativeness the existing calibration table already shows. The certificate is two numbers, r for the guarantee and phi for the tightness, never one. THE TWO GEOMETRIES ARE UNIFIED IN WRITING BEFORE ANY MEASUREMENT: the covering-graph walk in hybrid.py is the DEFINITION of r, the retraction-subset enumeration is the APPROXIMATION and the domain of phi, their j's are not the same metric, and both record method, oracle, assumes and search statistics. NO RANK ARITHMETIC: j is a hop count from one fixed G0 and never a poset rank, no arithmetic ever combines j across different centres, and the reason is printed, namely that the MPDAG poset is not graded for |V| >= 4. Extend conventions.py BEFORE any new radius is measured: r_0's three distinct infinite cases (no zero in the hull, hull undefined, extension cap hit) get three sentinels rather than one Python None; r_opt, r_eps and r_0 each get declared sentinel semantics in advance; and phi gets its own sentinel for the case where r is UNREACHED and no shell r exists.
axes.falsifiable_check: FOUR CHECKS, three of them about prior art because that is where this axis is exposed. (a) THE UNIT TABLE. Per instance report r in d_L, r in d_L,pseudo, and the SHD the same perturbation would have shown; publish the fraction where the two distances disagree and print the instance with the largest SHD-minus-d_L,pseudo gap as a worked counter-example. If SHD never certifies a strictly larger radius anywhere in the corpus, say so, because that is a measurement about our substrate and not a refutation of their proposition. (b) THE UNSEARCHED PRIOR-ART GATE, cut to three searches with rules written first. Stability radius in scheduling and combinatorial optimisation is r_opt definitionally; radius of robust feasibility in robust optimisation is r_val definitionally, with Renegar's distance to ill-posedness as the general theory; AGM contraction plus the MUS/MCS minimal-correction-set literature is the theory of the smallest subset of asserted constraints whose retraction breaks a property; and multiverse/specification-curve analysis already reports the spread of an estimate over a declared space of defensible analytic choices, which is phi's population analogue. DECISION RULE: if any of those already defines that object, the retraction-operator novelty claim is retired in the active-claims register and the contribution narrows to the MPDAG instantiation plus the calibration. The protocol does not change; the sentence does. (c) APPENDIX F.3 of arXiv:2511.10625v3 (MPDAG numerics) failed retrieval three times. DECISION RULE: no differentiation paragraph is written until it is retrieved by institutional access, a proceedings copy or a colleague's PDF; author email is unavailable under Operating Rule 3. If F.3 already centres a ball at a specified graph in MPDAGs, A4's contribution is the retraction operator and the weighting only, and the abstract is rewritten before the experiments run rather than after a referee says so. (d) THE SHELL-INFORMATIVENESS CHECK, which can retire phi rather than the framework. With 92.4% of committed instances at r <= 2, phi is measurable essentially at j in {0,1,2} only. DECISION RULE: if phi_r has an interquartile range below 0.05 across instances at the same r, the tightness number carries no information beyond r itself and is dropped to an appendix rather than promoted to the certificate; the pre-registered expectation is the opposite, since the existing calibration table shows roughly 44% of graphs outside the certified radius still admit Z, which is large unmeasured slack.
axes.justification: Theorem 1 in THEOREMS.md gives the upward-closure one-line proof that derives the operator. Taeb, Guo and Henckel (arXiv:2511.10625v3) force the unit discipline: Proposition 12 and Example 2 show SHD1 <= SHD2 <= d_L,pseudo with an instance at d_L,pseudo = 1 and SHD = n-1, so an SHD-denominated radius over-certifies; Proposition 9 and Table 3 show the poset is not graded for |V| >= 4, which is why brief section 4 forbids rank arithmetic; section 4.5 and section 7 state that the covering relation has no known graphical characterisation, which is exactly why a uniform draw from a covering-graph shell cannot be implemented and the shell must be defined on subsets of K; and section 7 names WEIGHTED COVERING RELATIONS as open future work, the slot the relevance weighting sits in and the slot a follow-up from that group would fill first. This is the largest scoop risk on the board and the ledger records two conflicting full-text readings of section 6, so the protocol answers them with a table on our data rather than a paragraph. The shell measure closes what the ledger records as simply absent: BFS returns the nearest failure and nothing about how much of shell j fails. The sentinel discipline is not decoration; conventions.py exists because a report and a framing document once disagreed by one, and three consecutive sessions each shipped a bug in the sentinel family.

axes.cost: Compute: with both exponentials removed the deployment sweep is minutes per pass rather than hours; the differential harness is the expense and it is bounded by the existing cap (2^12 = 4,096 extensions x roughly 500 instances at ~1 ms each is under an hour), plus a stress differential at 13 to 20 undirected edges on a handful of instances at 600 s each with a recorded censoring count. The estimated panel is the real cost: 5 Pi points x 5 seeds x the parameter-faithful cell plus the declared imposed-parameter subset is roughly 300 to 400 learning runs, 12 to 30 core-hours, 2 to 4 wall-hours on 8 cores. Six knowledge arms across both panels plus the four comparators and the matched ER control bring the total to roughly 45 to 65 wall-hours on an 8-core machine, a few days of background running on betelgeuse or the Hetzner node, and not the binding constraint. CUT AND RECORDED: the draft's 750 learning runs over roughly 30 networks at or below 200 nodes is cut, because 24 of the 39 networks are discrete BIF and the FWL estimator has no Sigma-hat there without a parameterisation this protocol would then have to defend. Human: about 8 hours for the closed-form O and its differential harness, 3 hours for the sentinel and manifest schema changes.
axes.decision: THE VALIDITY GATE NEVER CALLS THE ENUMERATING PREDICATE ON THE BALL, AND NEITHER DOES ANYTHING ELSE ON THE DEPLOYMENT PATH. The measured 1,839.78 s is one call to is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag routed through enumerate_dag_extensions, which on a 46-node network with 25 undirected edges means 2^25 extensions. Two substitutions, not one, and the draft only made the first. FIRST: validity is decided by the polynomial GAC predicate on the MPDAG (is_gac_valid_mpdag, measured at 1.07 ms per call at n = 20, an 8.2x gate speedup with 0 disagreements over 2,240 pairs), licensed on Z = O(.) by THEOREMS.md Theorem 14 and differentially tested rather than trusted. SECOND, and this is the one that removes the remaining exponential: O(G0) itself is computed by the closed form pa_G(cn_G(X,Y)) minus forb_G(X,Y) directly on the MPDAG, using the polynomial gac_causal_children and gac_forbidden_set already implemented in bkrobust.gac.mpdag_level, instead of by optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag, whose docstring states plainly that it computes the DAG-level optimal set in EVERY extension and returns None on disagreement. That enumeration is what produced the 280 o_g0_extensions_intractable rejections behind MAX_G0_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS = 12 and the three pathfinder censorings at the 1,200 s cap. The draft proposed component-restricting the enumeration; replacing it with the closed form the theory already supplies is strictly better and is licensed by the same source, subject to the recorded caveat that the MPDAG-level GAC forbidden-set formula is verified on about 2.5M cases and not proved, and would err conservative. Both substitutions are gated on a differential test on every instance where enumeration terminates under the existing cap, with disagreements recorded next to the accepted optimisations exactly as the rejected 746x one-level-cover shortcut was. A hard per-instance wall budget applies, and exceeding it writes status budget_censored on the fixed denominator, never a silent drop. TWO PANELS, NEVER POOLED, AND THE ORACLE PANEL IS NOT DEPLOYMENT-CLEAN. P-ORACLE takes C-hat as the CPDAG of the true DAG and therefore carries manifest flag true_dag_on_path = via_Chat_only; the draft printed 'true_dag_on_path = false' over a block containing oracle-panel rows, which is the invariant violation in miniature. Only P-EST may carry a deployment claim. P-EST learns C-hat with a CPDAG-EMITTING method (PC with the CI test and alpha declared, or GES), never a method emitting a fully oriented DAG, because a skeleton-times-order factorisation commits to one topological order and destroys the undirected chain component the radius is defined on. The n grid is reported on Pi = n / (|V| x d_exp / 2) at Pi in {1, 3, 10, 30, 100} with 5 seeds. SCOPE, STATED RATHER THAN DISCOVERED: the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell estimator se = sqrt(sigma^2_{y|x,z} / (n sigma^2_{x|z})) needs a covariance matrix, and 24 of the 39 networks are discrete BIF. The parameter-faithful cell is the four bnjson networks whose coefficients are fits to real measurements; everywhere else the linear-Gaussian parameters are ours over their structure, labelled 'structure theirs, parameters ours' on every number, with a sortability profile per cell. Networks above 200 nodes are P-ORACLE only, censored with the reason recorded, because discovery there is unaffordable and pretending otherwise would put a censoring inside a headline. THE BAND, NEVER THE POINT HULL: the point hull errs DANGEROUS 24.7% at n = 200 and still 18.1% at n = 20,000 while the 95% band errs at most 1.7% at every n, and the band's raw agreement looks worse (7.8% against 57.0% on magic-irri at n = 200) while being the only defensible choice. Say once, early, which of three the certificate is: a deterministic combinatorial functional of (C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n), not a Bayesian credible bound and not a posterior quantile. Make no marginal coverage claim; report coverage CONDITIONAL ON r.
axes.falsifiable_check: FOUR CHECKS, each with its sign declared first. (a) THE GATE-SUBSTITUTION DIFFERENTIAL, prediction written before the run because the last cost substitution in this repository was predicted strictly weaker and measured strictly STRICTER (16 disagreements in 46,800 cases, 0.034%, all one-directional). PREDICTION: zero disagreements on Z = O(G0) by Theorem 14, and where the unproved MPDAG forbidden-set formula bites it over-approximates, rejecting valid sets and making radii too SMALL. DECISION RULE: any disagreement whose sign makes a radius LARGER falsifies the substitution and the sweep stops until it is explained; conservative-direction disagreements are reported with rate and sign and the sweep continues. (b) THE CLOSED-FORM O DIFFERENTIAL, run on every instance where enumeration terminates under the cap. PREDICTION: agreement on the SET wherever the enumeration reports identification, and the closed form additionally returns a set on instances the enumeration reported as unidentified, which is where the 280 intractable and 518 unidentified rows live. DECISION RULE: one disagreement on a terminating instance retires the substitution and it is written up beside the accepted ones; a systematic difference in the identification VERDICT is not a bug but a definitional divergence and is reported as such, with both objects named, before either is used. (c) THE TWO-PANEL TRANSFER CHECK. DECISION RULE: if at the largest Pi the P-EST radius distribution differs from P-ORACLE by more than the pre-registered tolerance on the declared summary (share at r=1, median, share UNREACHED), the oracle idealisation is not a benign scope limit, every P-ORACLE number is restated as an idealisation in its own caption, and the paper makes no claim about the estimated regime beyond what P-EST measured. (d) THE THREE-BUCKET CARRY-OVER. The DANGEROUS rate under the band must stay at or below the 1.7% measured for r_0 at every Pi; if r_val exceeds it, the band is not sufficient for r_val and the certificate needs a wider construction before anything ships. This is a real risk and not a formality, because the three-bucket measurement was run on one radius only and its transfer to r_val is assumed, not measured.
axes.justification: Every tractability fact is measured in the tree: probe.log for the 1,839.78 s call on ecoli70 with 25 undirected edges, gate_predicate_swap.json for the 2,240-pair zero-disagreement swap at 8.2x, report_saturation_gac.md section 2.2 for the 1.07 ms bar, THEOREMS.md section 14 for the coincidence on O and the unproved-forbidden-set caveat, section 13 for the one-directional GAC-versus-back-door relation. The closed-form replacement is licensed by Henckel, Perkovic and Maathuis (arXiv:1907.02435) and Perkovic et al. (arXiv:1707.02171), which define O and the b-adjustment criterion on maximal PDAGs directly, and by the repository's own polynomial implementations of the two pieces it needs. Thompson et al. Arrow (arXiv:2605.07204) rules out a DAG-emitting front end. Schubert, Claassen and Magliacane (LOAD, arXiv:2510.14582) make two-panel reporting obligatory because the direct parent paper already reports both regimes side by side; b-LOAD supplies the Pi axis. Gradu, Zrnic, Wang and Jordan (arXiv:2208.05949), Chang, Guo and Malinsky (arXiv:2405.06763) and Strieder et al. (arXiv:2106.05694) are why no marginal coverage claim is made. Smucler, Robins and Rotnitzky (arXiv:2502.16673) give the conditional-on-r discipline for the small-radius corner, which is where this corpus lives, since 61.1% of committed instances are at r = 1. Javurek et al. (arXiv:2605.10590) set the compute bar the community now expects and name the LMU group likely to referee, which is why 1,839.78 s cannot be left standing anywhere near this protocol. Brief section 4 forbids claiming robustness under an estimated CPDAG while the CPDAG is the oracle's, which is why P-EST exists as a real arm and why P-ORACLE is flagged rather than described.

axes.cost: Compute: A6-5, A6-6, A6-7 and the kappa-hat profile ride the enumeration already paid for in A4, adding roughly 30%. kappa-hat_split is free, being a set comparison between two elicitations already run. kappa-hat_RoCA is |K| extra closure-plus-statistic evaluations per instance, of the order of 10^4 cheap operations. The matched ER control with its committed generator script is about 4 wall-hours. Human, after the cuts: about 10 hours for the eight-paper harvest under the LLM-reader-first protocol, about 6 hours for the three named prior-art searches and the Appendix F.3 retrieval, about 6 hours to implement the three-valued manifest arm field, the true_dag_on_path boolean and the publish-refusing check. CUT AND RECORDED: the draft's roughly 50-hour publication harvest, its 12 to 15 hours of decisive unread items and its expansion of T2 are removed. What survives of the unread backlog is ranked and bounded: arXiv:2503.09453 first, because it could turn this axis from BUILD into CALIBRATE and would change the paper's headline; then arXiv:2502.13132; then the RoaDS related-work section. The rest is declared an open risk in writing.
axes.decision: The referent does not exist and is BUILT, because no published study measures per-edge expert error separating omission from commission on expert-specified DAGs scored against a known-true DAG, and that survived a 1,100-note corpus grep, a web sweep and a gap-fill blocked by HTTP 403 at the four journals where it would live. THE CALIBRATION, rebuilt, because the draft's version is arithmetically vacuous before it runs. The draft prints the credibility ratio r / (kappa-hat x |K_G0|) and calls a spread the informative outcome; but the committed corpus has r = 1 in 61.1% of instances and median |K_G0| = 12 at full coverage, so the ratio falls below 1 whenever kappa-hat exceeds 1/12, and no plausible expert error rate is under 8.3%. The draft's own failure mode (3) is therefore guaranteed by data already on disk. Three fixes. FIRST, the referent is denominated in assertions the analyst made, |K|, not in the closure size the code writes as k_g0. SECOND, kappa-hat is measured LOCALLY, over the assertions within the graph neighbourhood the radius actually reaches, because O is a local functional and a global error rate prices the wrong population. THIRD, the reported statistic is not a ratio but a BREACH PROBABILITY: pi-hat = 1 - (1 - kappa-hat)^r, the chance that at least one assertion in the witness set BFS already returns is wrong, reported as a lower bound on the probability that the certificate is already breached, with a correlated-error version resampled from the measured clustering of wrong assertions rather than assumed independent. At r = 1 and kappa-hat = 0.10 that reads 0.10, which is a number a practitioner can act on and which cannot saturate by construction. THREE OBSERVABLE kappa-hats, and the third is what completes the population the draft could only cover half of. kappa-hat_cons: the fraction of stated assertions the Meek Algorithm 1 filter dropped, computable from the elicitation transcript alone, and currently identically zero because knowledge_inconsistent never fired in 115,974 screened pairs with oracle K. kappa-hat_RoCA, defined only where G0 admits at least two valid sets: for each k in K let G_{-k} = Meek(C-hat, K minus {k}) and let T be the over-identification statistic on (X, Y, Sigma-hat, n); kappa-hat_RoCA is the fraction of the analyst's own assertions whose retraction lowers T. kappa-hat_split, the new one, defined EVERYWHERE: elicit twice under independent prompt-order seeds and, separately, under two model families, and take the pairwise disagreement rate delta over the assertions the two passes share. Two elicitations that disagree mean at least one is wrong, so the average error rate across the pair is at least delta/2, an observable lower bound requiring no truth at all, on every instance including the sub-population where G0 admits exactly one valid set, which is precisely where testing is unavailable and pricing is the only instrument. It is also, in its own right, the inter-rater agreement statistic for elicited causal structure that the ledger records as absent from epidemiology and everywhere else. SEVEN AUDIT COMPONENTS. A6-1 DISCRIMINATOR: per network build K under each source, compute one pre-registered feature vector (coverage per granularity; distance-from-X distribution; commission and omission separately; pairwise graph distance among wrong assertions; Meek rejection rate; cascade size; cycles before repair) and run a permutation two-sample test, CALIBRATED FIRST on K-SYN at a known corruption rate so that a null verdict on the real sources can be distinguished from an underpowered test. A6-2 RADIUS-TRANSFER: hold the (network, X, Y) triples fixed, compare full radius distributions on the pre-declared summary, report the SIGN, since a source producing systematically LARGER radii is optimistic about robustness and that is the dangerous direction. A6-3 POSITIVE CONTROL: the matched ER arm with a committed generator script, because no script in the repository writes random_control.jsonl and that fails the third-party-rerun standard this axis imposes on everyone else. A6-4 CONTAMINATION SCREEN: audit-arm only, with the truth-free named-versus-scrambled AGREEMENT rate as the deployment-arm proxy, and the honest caveat written into the paper that the accuracy gap bounds memorisation from above and domain knowledge from below without separating them, so a clean stratum is added, at least one network published after the model cutoff or an applied DAG newly drawn. A6-5 RoCA HEAD-TO-HEAD: per instance record the valid-set count, whether the over-identification test fires at a declared alpha, the radius, and in the audit arm whether the certified Z is actually invalid in the true DAG; the object is a 2x2 stratified by valid-set count 1 against >= 2. A6-6 ENSEMBLE HEAD-TO-HEAD: compute Hu and van der Pas's P_A over the SAME enumerated sub-poset with a declared prior and compare the DECISION each instrument yields at a declared threshold, in both directions and with the sign. A6-7 SOFT-PENALTY COMPARISON: score the same K with a RoaDS-shaped soft credibility penalty and report its rank correlation with the radius and with audited per-assertion correctness. Finally the manifest gains a THREE-VALUED arm field, {deployment, audit, substrate_design}, plus a true_dag_on_path enum {false, via_Chat_only, true}, and a check that refuses to publish when a deployment-tagged quantity carries anything but false.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE NECESSITY CHECK, powered rather than merely stated, because the draft named a threshold and never asked whether the corpus could resolve it. On audited instances where the certified Z is truly invalid, compute the fraction RoCA does NOT detect at the declared alpha. DECISION RULE: the motivating claim is licensed only above 50%; between 25% and 50% the positioning changes from 'pricing where testing cannot' to 'pricing as a complement to testing' and the abstract is rewritten before submission; below 25% the gap is closed by an existing published test with released code and the result becomes a negative-results entry with a revive_if naming the sub-population (valid-set count exactly 1). POWER, derived: separating 0.50 from 0.25 with a half-width of 0.075 needs an effective n of about 172, and with intra-cluster correlation 0.1 under the per-network cap of 20 the design effect is 2.9, so about 500 truly-invalid instances are required. That is why the cap exists: the committed corpus's actual concentration (552 of 831 instances from five networks) gives a design effect above 10 and cannot resolve the threshold at any sample size the corpus can supply. PRE-REGISTERED PILOT: five networks under K-LLM measure the truly-invalid share first; if the projected count is under 500, the necessity headline is DECLARED UNDERPOWERED and reported as an interval with its width, never as a verdict. SECOND RULE, on the ensemble: if the posterior produces the better decision at every operating point in the average on the identical sub-poset, the radius is a worse summary of the same enumeration and the contribution is the enumeration. The draft's paired prediction that the radius wins in the tail is WITHDRAWN as untestable: the entire r >= 5 population of the committed corpus is 16 instances and all 16 lie in one dagitty illustration, so no tail claim is powered and none is made. THIRD RULE, on the calibration: if pi-hat exceeds 0.9 on more than 90% of instances the certificate never survives the error the analyst's own replicates evidence and the framework is reporting a guarantee nobody can use; if it falls below 0.1 on more than 90% the referent is too small to threaten anything. The informative outcome is a spread and the pre-registered tolerance is that neither tail holds more than 90%. FOURTH RULE, on the referent's own reliability: if kappa-hat_split is zero or near-zero, two independent elicitations agree completely, which means either the surrogate is deterministic under order permutation, in which case the replicate must vary the model family instead, or it is reciting, which routes to A6-4 and makes the whole surrogate arm a contamination measurement. FIFTH RULE, on A6-2: with T2 at 8 networks and roughly 160 instances against a McNemar requirement of about 157 at a discordance of 0.25 for the 11.1-point shift, inflated by a design effect of 2.9, the paired test needs about 455 and is short by a factor of about 2.8. It is DECLARED UNDERPOWERED and reported as an interval, not run and reported as a null.
axes.justification: The ledger's A6 block is the source for every component. Cinelli and Hazlett (DOI 10.1111/rssb.12348, verified CONFIRMED) set the bar the brief names, a sensitivity parameter calibrated against an observable quantity, and the breach probability is the form that survives our own data where a ratio does not. Su and Henckel (arXiv:2206.07533, verified CONFIRMED, code released) supply both the incumbent test and the honest scope limit, and are why brief section 4 forbids the global untestability claim; the licensed narrow form, that the class of orientation errors keeping all valid adjustment sets valid is untestable by consistency checks and THAT is the class the radius prices, is quantitative and A6-5 measures it. Hu and van der Pas (arXiv:2511.01662v2, verified CONFIRMED) are the nearest competitor for the object itself. RoaDS (arXiv:2511.06790, AAAI 2026) already scores constraint credibility by a soft penalty, which narrows the claim to 'we certify breakdown tolerance where others penalise', and A6-7 measures whether their instrument already orders assertions as well as ours. Mourao et al. (arXiv:2603.15928) establish that an author-run coverage audit is worth less than a third-party one, which is why every arm ships its generator script. Sadeghi and AbdAlmageed (arXiv:2603.17405) are the reason every rate carries TWO dispersion numbers rather than one: their reported 95.1 +/- 2.4 reproduced at 69.1 +/- 21.7, and that is re-run variance, which a cluster bootstrap over networks does not capture; the draft used the bootstrap to answer them, which is a category error, so the replicate arms supply the seed standard deviation and both are printed. The three-bucket form is our own measured precedent: agreement hides the sign and the sign is the whole guarantee. Sachs is used as an evaluation referent with an explicit refusal to report precision and recall, on our own CSCD precedent, because its network is inferred and validated post hoc. CSCD's rejection is why the audit arm must report a decision-relevant quantity: both reviewers read epistemic restraint as a ceiling rather than a strength.

known_weaknesses: kappa-hat_split is a LOWER bound on error and its slack is unmeasured. Two elicitations that agree may agree because both are right, because both recite the same pretraining prior, or because temperature 0 makes the second pass a near-copy. The construction is honest about the direction (agreement never proves correctness) and A6-4 routes the recitation case, but nothing in the protocol turns the bound into an estimate, and a referee can say the calibration rests on a quantity whose gap to the truth is exactly what the audit arm was supposed to measure and only measures on the tiers that have a truth.

The corpus may not have the dynamic range the framework needs, and this is now measured rather than feared. Of the 831 committed admissible instances, 768 sit at r <= 2, 63 at r >= 3, and all 16 at r >= 5 live in `paths`, a dagitty textbook drawing. Remove the three pedagogical files and the maximum radius over 807 instances is 4. A certificate whose measured range on real structure is {1,2,3,4} is still a certificate, but the spread that makes phi, the breach probability and the ensemble comparison interesting may simply not exist outside illustrations, and the protocol's answer is to report that honestly rather than to manufacture range by keeping the drawings in the denominator.

Replacing the enumerating optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag with the closed form changes what 'identified' means, not only how fast it is computed. The enumeration returns None when extensions disagree; the closed form returns a set computed on the MPDAG. Those are different objects and the differential can only compare them where both terminate. The protocol names the divergence and reports both, but a reviewer could reasonably read the substitution as widening the admissible population to make the corpus survive, which is uncomfortably close to the selection the redesign exists to remove.

The publication-harvest referent, even cut to eight papers and restructured so the human adjudicates rather than initiates, remains the arm most likely never to happen, and this vault's own measurement says tasks with no external counterparty close at 0% against 54% for tasks where someone is already waiting. The cut makes it survivable, not certain, and its failure would leave the realism audit standing on kappa-hat_split and the LLM arm alone, with validity unmeasured and only reliability measured.

The MISSING control is matched on |K| and on the distance-from-X histogram and on nothing else. Two K's of the same size and placement can still differ in granularity mix, cascade size and which chain components they touch, and the protocol does not match on those because matching on everything leaves nothing to vary. The residual imbalance is reported per arm rather than removed, which is weaker than the fixed-denominator fix it sits beside.

Choosing causal-order and triplet elicitation over pairwise avoids the measured cycle artefact but makes our K a different object from b-LOAD's, which is a partial fully-correct subset of REQUIRED EDGES sampled at rho. The mapping table onto CSCD's 0.3 and b-LOAD's rho and mu is a deliverable of A3, but an order-derived K under Meek closure may not be commensurable with an edge-sampled K at all, and that comparability is weakened by a choice made for a different good reason.

P-ORACLE is flagged via_Chat_only rather than dropped, so a substantial part of the results still comes from a panel where the true DAG entered through the CPDAG. Flagging is the honest minimum and the rule that only P-EST may carry a deployment claim is enforced by the manifest check, but the paper will still contain more oracle-panel numbers than estimated-panel ones, and a referee who reads the flag correctly will notice which panel the interesting rows are in.

The statistical layer covers a minority of the substrate by construction. Twenty-four of the thirty-nine parsing networks are discrete BIF and have no Sigma-hat, so the parameter-faithful cell is four networks and everything else carries parameters we imposed over structure they supplied. Cutting the draft's thirty-network estimated panel was the honest move, but it means the finite-n arm, the band and the three-bucket calibration are measured on a narrow slice and generalised by argument rather than by coverage.

T3 has no audit twin by construction, since no real dataset carries both a domain-accepted graph and ground-truth interventional effects, so the tier closest to deployment is the tier where the certificate cannot be checked. Everything T3 contributes is a deployment distribution plus the three kappa-hats, and the explicit refusal to score against the Sachs reference graph, honest as it is, means the most realistic substrate produces the least verifiable evidence.

Retaining the ER arm sits against the grain of Decision 2. The reconciling sentence, that it is instrument calibration and never in a substrate denominator, is written and defensible, but a co-author could read it as keeping the declined thing under a new label. Dropping it loses A6-3's power check, which is the only way to know whether the two-sample machinery can reject anything at all, so this design pays a coherence cost to keep a power guarantee.

The exact radius still inherits the open assumption chain (Anti-Exchange Case B to Lemma R to Property S to Lemma L to Conjecture 2), whose failure direction is one-sided and favourable to the hypothesis under test, against the counter-directed caveat that the unproved MPDAG forbidden-set formula could deflate. This protocol carries both caveats on every number rather than resolving either; a theory-first design would spend the whole budget there and would be right that a certificate resting on a conjecture is not yet a certificate.
name: Fixed-Frame Kappa-Ball
one_sentence: One candidate frame drawn from C-hat alone is frozen before any knowledge is elicited, so every knowledge arm reports the same denominator and the K-dependent outcomes become printed statuses instead of silent filters; and each radius is printed beside a breach probability computed from the disagreement between two independent elicitations, which needs no ground truth and therefore exists on the half of the population where the incumbent test does not.
primary_table:
THE CERTIFICATE LEDGER. One page, and its column header carries the invariant.

ROWS. One row per (substrate tier x knowledge arm) at the declared reference panel, so the panel is a printed provenance flag rather than a row multiplier. Tiers T0 ILLUSTRATION, T1 BENCHMARK, T2 APPLIED, T3 REAL-PARAMETER, crossed with the five deployment arms LLM, PUB (T2 only), TRUE, SYN, NULL: seventeen rows. Below a horizontal rule, visually separated and labelled 'instrument, not substrate': the A-ORACLE reference row and the N-ER-MATCHED control row. T0's row block is separated by a second rule and carries the standing note that it holds textbook drawings, that in the committed corpus it supplies every instance at r >= 5, and that no headline is computed over it.

COLUMNS, in three blocks.

Block 1, WHAT THE ANALYST SEES. Header stamp: arm = deployment, true_dag_on_path = false for P-EST rows and via_Chat_only for P-ORACLE rows, printed per row and never assumed for the block.
 1. instances / networks, both weights, zero-yield networks in the denominator, realised per-network cap
 2. STATUS COMPOSITION on the fixed denominator: ok / knowledge_inconsistent / o_g0_not_identified / o_g0_empty / z_invalid_at_g0 / budget_censored. This is the column that makes the arms comparable and it is the one the previous protocol had no place for
 3. share at r = 1, with a 95% cluster bootstrap over networks AND a seed standard deviation from the replicate arms, printed as two separate numbers
 4. median r with interval; max r printed twice, within tier and with T0 excluded
 5. share UNREACHED, as a status count, never averaged into column 4
 6. phi_r, the fraction of the r-subsets of K whose retraction invalidates Z: the tightness number beside the guarantee, with its Monte Carlo standard error where sampled
 7. kappa-hat_split, median with interval, the observable error floor from two independent elicitations
 8. kappa-hat_cons, the Meek rejection fraction, which is identically zero in the committed corpus and is expected to be positive here
 9. pi-hat, the breach probability, median and the share above 0.5
 10. share of instances where G0 admits at least two valid adjustment sets, i.e. where an over-identification test and kappa-hat_RoCA exist at all; and share where RoCA fires

Block 2, WHAT THE COMPETING INSTRUMENTS SAY, same instances:
 11. C-COUNT-A (|K|) and C-COUNT-B (closure size) decision agreement, reported separately, each with the sign of the disagreements
 12. C-ENSEMBLE decision agreement with the sign
 13. Spearman rank correlation between the C-SOFT credibility score and the radius

Block 3, WHAT THE TRUTH SAYS. Greyed, header stamped arm = audit, true_dag_on_path = true, absent on every T3 row:
 14. three buckets, equal / SAFE (radius smaller than truth) / DANGEROUS (radius larger than truth), never an agreement rate
 15. K error on one scale: consistent-but-false rate, then reversed / omitted / invented as three separate rates, with commission and omission on separate axes
 16. share of truly-invalid certified sets that RoCA MISSED, the quantity the necessity claim stands or falls on, printed with its interval and with a POWERED / UNDERPOWERED stamp from the pre-registered pilot

WHAT A ROW MEANS. One substrate tier under one knowledge arm: over one frozen instance frame, what happened to every instance (not only the surviving ones), what the certificate said and how tight it was, what the analyst's own replicate elicitations already evidenced about their error rate, what the incumbent test and the three competing instruments said on identical instances, and, in the greyed block only, what the truth said afterwards. A reader who stops at column 10 has read the deployable protocol. A reader who reaches column 16 has read the audit. The rule between them is the invariant, drawn rather than described.
total_budget:
WALL-CLOCK: six to eight weeks at a part-time cadence, down from the draft's three to four months, and the reduction is entirely the cut human scope rather than faster machines.

COMPUTE, in the units the repository measures. The radii are already known to be nearly free: 831 exact radii cost 7.2 s in total, 8.7 ms per instance, slowest single instance 0.16 s, and CPDAG construction over all 39 parsing networks is 60.95 s. New expenses: the shell measure on the retraction-subset geometry, which is bounded by C(|K|, j) with full enumeration under a 20,000 cap and 400 uniform j-subsets above it, roughly 1 to 3 core-hours over about 500 instances because 92.4% of measured radii sit at r <= 2 where the subsets number in the tens; the closed-form-O differential harness, under an hour; and the estimated-C-hat panel, roughly 300 to 400 learning runs at 12 to 30 core-hours. Six knowledge arms across both panels plus four comparators plus the matched ER control total roughly 45 to 65 wall-hours on an 8-core machine, a few days of background running on betelgeuse or the Hetzner node, and not the binding constraint. THE NUMBER THIS PROTOCOL REFUSES TO SPEND is the 1,839.78 s validity gate, and it refuses it twice rather than once: the enumerating predicate never runs on the ball, since is_gac_valid_mpdag decides the same question at 1.07 ms and the substitution is licensed by Theorem 14 on Z = O(.) and differentially tested with its sign declared first; and the second exponential, computing O(G0) itself by enumerating every DAG extension, which is what produced the 280 intractable rejections behind MAX_G0_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS = 12 and the three pathfinder censorings at the 1,200 s wall, is replaced by the closed form pa(cn) minus forb computed on the MPDAG with the polynomial pieces already in bkrobust.gac.mpdag_level. Nothing on the deployment path is exponential afterwards, and a hard per-instance wall budget writes budget_censored on the fixed denominator rather than dropping the row.

LLM CALLS: of the order of 2,000 to 2,400 cached calls at temperature 0, being one structured call per chain component emitting all four granularities, times two elicitation replicates, times the three naming conditions of the audit-arm contamination screen, across two model families, at an input volume of the order of 10^6 to 10^7 tokens.

AGENT-HOURS: about 55 to 70. The implementation items are the select_knowledge and knowledge_to_recover removal from both measure.py and fast_gate, the C-hat-only query frame with the fixed denominator and the status vocabulary, the canonical-set fallback plus r_opt as a second radius, the closed-form O and its differential, the dagitty attrs wiring, the retraction-subset shell measure, the sentinel extension in conventions.py, the three-valued manifest arm field with the publish-refusing check, the six knowledge arms including the matched TRUE control and the tiered correlated SYN control, the four comparator arms, the contamination harness, and the committed ER generator script the comparator arm has never had.

HUMAN-HOURS: about 22, down from the draft's 65, and the cuts are named rather than absorbed. CUT: the T2 expansion from 8 to 25 applied networks (25 to 35 hours), which is why A6-2 is declared underpowered per tier before it runs. CUT: the full quote-anchored harvest across 8 applied plus 24 BIF networks (about 50 hours), reduced to the 8 author-named applied papers with the LLM reader producing the candidate extraction and the human adjudicating, roughly 10 hours, which is why K-PUB exists on 8 networks and roughly 160 instances and on no benchmark network at all. CUT: five unsearched prior-art literatures (10 to 15 hours) reduced to three named searches with decision rules written first, plus the Appendix F.3 retrieval which is cheap and is a hard gate on the differentiation paragraph, about 6 hours, with the remaining two declared an open prior-art risk in writing. CUT: the thirty-network estimated panel, because 24 of 39 networks are discrete BIF and have no covariance matrix for the FWL estimator, so the finite-n arm covers the four parameter-faithful networks plus a declared imposed-parameter subset and says so on every number. Remaining human time is about 6 hours of schema and manifest review.

BINDING CONSTRAINT: still Ze's reading hours, but now for ten hours of adjudication rather than fifty of initiation, and restructured so the LLM reader goes first and the human reviews a page-anchored draft. This vault's own measurement is the reason for the restructure, not politeness: tasks where someone is already waiting close at 54% and tasks that must be initiated close at 0% over 40 observations, so the harvest is written as a review queue with a fixed weekly quota, and its failure mode is declared in advance as a coverage limit on the realism referent rather than a silent hole in the audit.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_r: Five things, and they have to hold together. First, the deployment population survives real knowledge: under elicited K the fixed frame still delivers a majority of instances at status ok, the certified set exists even where O(G0) is unidentified because the canonical GAC-valid set is what is certified, and the status composition column shows which arm lost how many instances to which cause rather than each arm quietly reporting a different denominator. Second, the radius spreads within its real range and is not a restatement of counting: it is not saturated at 1, not a deterministic function of |K| or of the closure size within the interval, and the audit arm's three-bucket score shows instances where both count baselines get the decision wrong and the radius gets it right. There is prior evidence the count baseline is not trivially correct and that it cuts against a naive bound, since the committed analysis file records 110 of 463 instances where the radius EXCEEDS min(s, closure size), but that was measured on the oracle-K population and has to survive the move. Third, the breach probability spreads: pi-hat sits neither above 0.9 nor below 0.1 on the bulk of instances, kappa-hat_split is strictly positive and varies by network, and the practitioner-facing sentence lands, namely that on these queries the disagreement your own two elicitations already exhibit is enough to have breached the certificate and on those it is not. That is the Cinelli and Hazlett move working on a referent computed from the analyst's own materials, and it is the difference between a certificate and a curiosity.
