Fourth, the certificate is conservative in the direction it claims: DANGEROUS at or below the 1.7% the band achieved for r_0 at every Pi, with the SAFE excess visible as slack rather than hidden inside an agreement rate, and phi_r printing that slack as a number rather than leaving the 0.43 to 0.47 conservativeness an unremarked property. Fifth, the necessity result: a majority of the audited invalidities are invisible to RoCA, concentrated where G0 admits exactly one valid set, the radius fires on them, and the pilot showed the corpus had enough truly-invalid instances to resolve the 50% threshold at the declared half-width. The paper that comes out of that says: here is a deterministic combinatorial certificate priced in units of an error rate the analyst can compute from two elicitations and a regression, on the class of graph errors an existing test provably cannot see, with the size of that class measured on a corpus whose textbook drawings are reported separately from its networks.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_w: Seven concrete outcomes, any one of which the protocol produces on its own data, and two of them are already partly visible in the committed files. (1) THE POPULATION DISAPPEARS. Under real, partial elicited K, G0 keeps undirected edges and the certified set is not identified on most framed instances; the pilot gate on five networks reports an ok share under 40% and the elicitation budget is not spent. This is the most likely failure and neither the draft nor the ledger named it: the current corpus is admissible largely because oracle knowledge orients everything, and o_g0_not_identified already fires 518 times with fully informative K. (2) THE RANGE WAS AN ILLUSTRATION. No network outside the dagitty pedagogical files produces r >= 5, which is already true of the committed corpus, where all 16 such instances lie in `paths` and the maximum over the remaining 807 is 4. Then every sentence about large radii is a sentence about a textbook drawing, the founding contrast against a synthetic maximum inverts, and the certificate's honest measured range on real structure is {1,2,3,4}. (3) THE COUNT BASELINE WINS. |K| or the closure size reproduces the radius's decision at every operating point of the three-bucket score within the interval. Then the framework is a lemma about counting your own claims, and six sessions of not running H4 will have been the reason nobody noticed. (4) THE CALIBRATION IS VACUOUS. pi-hat sits above 0.9 on more than 90% of instances, meaning no certificate survives the disagreement the analyst's own replicates already exhibit, or below 0.1 on more than 90%, meaning the referent is too small to threaten anything; or kappa-hat_split comes back at zero, meaning two independent elicitations agree completely and the referent measures determinism rather than reliability. (5) NECESSITY FAILS. Fewer than a quarter of audited invalidities escape RoCA, and the one-valid-set sub-population is a thin corner. Then the motivating gap is closed by an existing published test with released code, and the honest output is a negative-results entry whose revive_if names that corner. Or the pilot says the corpus cannot resolve the threshold at all, in which case the headline is stamped UNDERPOWERED and reported as an interval rather than dressed as a null. (6) THE SURROGATE IS RECITATION. More than half of T1's instances land in the contamination-flagged stratum, with the named-minus-scrambled gap past the binomial bound and cold recall reproducing the published adjacency. Then the LLM arm measures pretraining rather than expertise on the benchmark tier, and after the harvest cut the realism referent rests on eight applied networks. (7) THE PRIOR ART ALREADY OWNS IT. Appendix F.3 of arXiv:2511.10625v3, once retrieved, already centres a ball at a specified graph in MPDAGs; or the radius of robust feasibility, Renegar's distance to ill-posedness, AGM contraction, the MUS/MCS minimal-correction-set literature or the specification-curve tradition already defines the smallest subset of asserted constraints whose retraction breaks a property, or already reports phi as the fraction of defensible specifications that fail. Then the geometry contribution retires to an instantiation, and the protocol is built so that this is discovered before the differentiation paragraph is written rather than by a referee who has read the paper we did not.

name: Oracle Meter v2 — taint-propagated deployment with a masked-compelled-edge bridge
one_sentence: Instead of asserting the invariant in a paragraph, every record carries an `oracle_on_path` bit that PROPAGATES TRANSITIVELY over provenance — so the true-DAG-derived knowledge arms (K-MISS, K-CORR, K* ) are mechanically forced out of the deployment arm even though the radius computation itself never reads a DAG — and the one number the whole design rests on, the surrogate's error rate, is measured oracle-free by un-orienting an edge the DATA compelled in the ESTIMATED CPDAG and asking the surrogate to re-derive it blind, which is Veitch and Zaveri's "delete an observed quantity and check whether predicted harm tracks realised harm" transposed from confounding to structure.

axes.axis: A1 SUBSTRATE — population of true structures, and which statistics a substrate must match for a claim about r to transfer
axes.decision:
Five labelled tiers, never pooled, each with a fixed instance set and its own dispersion convention.

T0-CONTROL: the five random generators kept as a LABELLED NEGATIVE CONTROL, re-run through ONE pipeline (same K construction, same polynomial GAC gate, same coverage handling, same sampling frame, same reporting schema), on a grid REPARAMETERISED ON EXPECTED DEGREE rather than edge probability, because ER's expected degree (n-1)p grows with n and no single edge-probability cell holds density constant across a size sweep. Densities: the instance-weighted min / median / max mean degree of the admissible sub-corpus, recomputed from descriptive_structure.csv as 2.00 / 3.50 / 9.86 (all-39-network band 1.60-9.86, median 2.92). Sizes: the instance-weighted octiles of the admissible corpus's node counts, which recompute to 4 / 14 / 20 / 27 / 36 / 48 / 48 / 76, deduped and closed at the top to {5, 14, 20, 27, 36, 48, 76, 109}. THE SIZE CAP IS THE CORRECTION THAT MATTERS: the existing ER sweep tops out at n=30, which covers 384 of 831 admissible instances (46.2%); n<=50 covers 687 (82.7%), n<=110 covers 736 (88.6%). A control that stops at 30 cannot be matched to more than half the instance mass. Grid = 3 densities x 8 sizes x S seeds; the generator script is COMMITTED (its absence is the one place the current audit apparatus fails its own third-party-rerun standard).

T0-FIXTURE: the designed backdoor family plus M-bias, always reported separately. M-bias is recovered CORRECTLY, not as a parse fix: the file is `D <-> Z`, `E <-> Z`, `E -> D`, i.e. two BIDIRECTED edges, which is why is_dag=False — it is a latent-variable ADMG, not a broken DAG. The recovery is the explicit latent expansion E <- U1 -> Z <- U2 -> D plus E -> D on five observed nodes, entered as a named single-instance regression fixture for the forbidden-set machinery. This matters because it is the textbook structure where a consistent-looking adjustment choice opens a collider path, and because the corpus otherwise contains 6 networks with nothing to orient at all.

T1-BENCH: 24 BIF plus 4 bnjson networks. T2-APPLIED: the 11 dagitty DAGs, with `ParsedNetwork` gaining an `annotations` field so the exposure/outcome/adjusted/latent attributes that `dagitty.py:44` matches into a named capture group and discards are retained.

T3-REAL: datasets carrying a domain-accepted graph, Sachs first, used as an evaluation referent with precision and recall against it explicitly REFUSED in writing. T3 REPORTS PER-INSTANCE ROWS, NOT FRACTIONS. Sachs is 11 nodes and yields 13 admissible instances under the oracle CPDAG; any proportion on <=13 instances carries SE >= sqrt(0.25/13) = 0.139, so a T3 rate is not a measurement and the table prints the instances verbatim, one line each.

MATCHING STATISTIC for transfer: the JOINT distribution of (chain-component size, separation s, |K_G0|), never a marginal, because the only relation that survived out of sample is the BOUND r <= min(s, |K_G0|); the equality did not (337 of 463 = 72.8%, 110 exceptions above and 16 below).

TWO DISPERSIONS, never interchanged and always named in the cell: SEED dispersion, over simulated draws, exists only where there is a seed (T0-CONTROL and every C-hat_E cell); BETWEEN-NETWORK dispersion, over the corpus, is the only dispersion a fixed-corpus C-hat_O cell has. Every reported rate says which one it carries.
axes.justification: Decision 2 fixes benchmarks plus applied-paper DAGs plus real datasets with a domain-accepted graph and declines structure-matched synthetic generators; the ledger's A1 CONVENTION nonetheless requires the ER arm to survive LABELLED, because Test A6-3's power check depends on it, and its open question 'should the ER arm survive at all' is answered by keeping it as a control rather than deleting it. The one-pipeline requirement and the density band are the ledger's own stated replacement for the current comparison, which is unmatched on size, coverage, search method, gate provenance and pipeline. The size cap is derived here rather than inherited: the draft's 'sizes overlapped where the real corpus permits' is unfalsifiable until someone computes the coverage, and the computation says the current sweep reaches 46.2% of the instance mass. The M-bias correction is load-bearing: the draft proposed to 're-enter it as a DAG', which the file's two bidirected edges make impossible — the exclusion was not a technicality and the honest recovery is the latent expansion. T3-as-rows follows from arithmetic, not taste: the draft's Table 1 put fractions in the T3 deployment block, and a fraction over 13 instances has a standard error wider than most of the effects the protocol is trying to see. Seed dispersion is mandated by Sadeghi & AbdAlmageed arXiv:2603.17405, where a reported 95.1 +/- 2.4 reproduced at 69.1 +/- 21.7; separating it from between-network dispersion is required because the fixed-corpus tiers have no seed and reporting a between-network SD under the seed-dispersion label would be a category error a reviewer of that audit will catch.
axes.falsifiable_check:
MATCHED-CONTROL TEST, pre-registered before the matched run is looked at. Two-stage seed rule, not a stipulated S: pilot 5 seeds per cell, estimate the per-seed SD sigma-hat of the separation>=2 rate, then set S >= 18*sigma-hat^2 / Delta^2 with Delta the planning gap 21.3 pp (real 45.4% pair-weighted against the ER arm's own sparse cell at 24.1%). That constant is derived, not chosen: the SE of a difference of two S-seed means is sqrt(2 sigma^2/S), and setting it to Delta/3 gives S = 18 sigma^2/Delta^2. DECISION RULE: if the matched ER separation>=2 rate and the real rate differ by less than three seed-dispersion standard errors of their difference AS REALISED IN THAT RUN, the non-exchangeability premise is WITHDRAWN in writing, the finding is restated as 'the edge probability was set wrong' rather than 'ER is not exchangeable with real structure', and Decision 2 is re-opened for Ze rather than silently retained.

DENOMINATOR-SELECTION RULE, generalised from the ledger's 2.6x finding rather than applied only to it. Every rate prints its own denominator's selection rate as a paired number. Verified selection rates that already differ: separation is undefined for 368 of 831 real admissible instances (44.3%, status `no_z_member_in_component`) against 17.1% of random-generator instances; the r=1 column has denominator 831 while the bound-agreement column has denominator 463 (55.7% of the same rows); 280 pairs are dropped as measurement-limited and 518 as structurally unidentified. DECISION RULE: no cross-arm statement about a rate may be made unless the two arms' denominator-selection rates fall within a band pre-registered before the arms are compared; outside the band the comparison is reported as within-arm only, with the selection gap printed as the reason.

SIZE-COVERAGE CHECK: report, before any matched claim, the fraction of admissible instance mass whose network size lies inside the control's size grid. DECISION RULE: below 80% the matched claim is stated as conditional on the sub-corpus and the excluded networks are named with their instance counts (currently diabetes 89 and munin1 6, together 95 of 831 = 11.4% above n=109).
axes.cost: Compute: the T0-CONTROL grid is 24 cells x S seeds, against the previous unmatched arm's 2,880 draws (480 per generator, 2,334 accepted) — at S=20 it is 480 draws, i.e. one sixth of the arm it replaces, so the size extension to n=109 is paid for by the grid shrinking. Hours, not days, on one machine. The T1/T2 re-screen is bounded above by the repo's own caps: 39 networks x 1,200 s cap_per_network_run_s x 3 deployment knowledge arms + 39 x 1,200 for K-CORR + 9 x 1,200 for K-PUB (only 9 dagitty networks yield admissible instances) = 198,000 s = 55 h worst case, and the observed slowest instance is 0.16 s, so the realised figure will be far under the cap. Human: 3 h for the M-bias latent-expansion fixture and its written argument, 3 h for the refusal-to-score-Sachs paragraph, 4 h for the `annotations` field and its parser test. Agent: ~20 h, of which the committed matched-generator script is the majority.

axes.axis: A2 QUERY POLICY — how (X,Y) is drawn non-adaptively, and what the filters do to the population
axes.decision:
Replace 'screen all n(n-1) ordered pairs and reject post hoc' with a declared OBSERVABLES-ONLY sampling frame, applied in this fixed order, non-adaptively:
(1) X lies in, or is adjacent to, an undirected component of C-hat of size >= 2. Already observable, already first, and the largest rejection bucket at 66,330 of 115,974 verified screens.
(2) Y in possible_descendants(G0, X) \ {X}, computed in polynomial time on the analyst's own graph. This REPLACES `y not in dag.descendants(x)`, 42,618 true-DAG reads.
(3) O*(G0) identified, i.e. the extensions agree. Observable; 518 rejections.
(4) Z = O*(G0) GAC-valid at G0. Observable, holds by construction, fires 0 times.
(5) The empty set is NOT GAC-valid at G0. REPLACES `is_valid_adjustment_set_dag(dag, x, y, frozenset())`, 3,738 true-DAG reads. It changes the population, because triviality at the analyst's graph is not triviality at the truth.
(6) Some single retraction from the ANALYST'S OWN K changes GAC validity at the re-closure. REPLACES the `knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag)` loop, 1,659 true-DAG reads, and unlike the current version it is the very perturbation the radius walks.
`no_valid_adjustment_set` is DELETED: it reads the true DAG and fired 0 times in 115,974 screens.

Sampling inside the frame is a seeded deterministic stride over the sorted frame, never a function of any computed radius. The per-network _meta row records frame_size, target_fraction, stride and realised_count as FOUR SEPARATE FIELDS, ending the disagreement where `sampling_rate` reports the target while `sampled_pairs` reports the stride realisation.

RECORD PER PAIR, additionally: the NUMBER of valid adjustment sets (this decides whether the incumbent test has power on that instance, and is currently unrecorded), and the RoCA verdict.

FIXED INSTANCE SETS, declared before anything is compared. The corpus's 831 admissible instances are 543 UNIQUE (X,Y) pairs measured at three coverage levels (543 / 182 / 106, recounted); every paired comparison across knowledge sources runs on the unique-pair set, and every comparison ACROSS COVERAGE runs on the 106 instances admissible at coverage 0.25, with the full-set numbers printed beside and the composition delta named. This is the ledger's non-comparable-strata rule turned into a specific integer instead of a principle.

HEADLINE WEIGHT: NETWORK-weighted, with the pair-weighted figure printed beside it in every table; zero-yield networks stay in the denominator. Deliver the population-shaping report the pre-registration promised: the (component size, separation, |K_G0|) distribution before and after each filter. Run H4, the naive |K|-count baseline, pre-registered and unrun for six sessions and fully observable.
axes.justification: The ledger's A2 measurement enumerates exactly five filters that read the true DAG and names the four rejection reasons the deployment arm may keep. The oracle arithmetic that motivates the redesign, recomputed and verified in-tree: 42,618 + 3,738 + 1,659 = 48,015 screening decisions, 41.4% of every screen ever run, are made by a true-DAG read, and the top two rejection buckets together (66,330 + 42,618 = 108,948) are 93.9% of all screens, which is why 'the budget sits on the wrong side of the filter' and pathfinder spent its whole 1,200 s wall cap screening and produced no radius. Locality licenses the frame: Henckel, Perkovic & Maathuis (arXiv:1907.02435) prove O* = pa(cn(X,Y)) \ forb(X,Y) is LOCAL, and Schubert, Claassen & Magliacane (LOAD, arXiv:2510.14582) recover O* around a target pair without learning the global graph. Recording the count of valid adjustment sets is Su & Henckel's requirement (arXiv:2206.07533, verify CONFIRMED): a robustness test needs at least two valid sets to have power. Network-weighting as the headline is derived: 969 of the corpus's 7,062 nodes lie in a chain component at all, and the admissible pair count is dominated by a handful of networks (barley 189, insurance 160, diabetes 89 of 831), so a pair-weighted corpus statistic is largely a statement about three networks; the pair-weighted number stays visible because the two differ materially (45.4% against 35.6% for separation>=2; 61.1% against 71.3% for r=1). The 543/106 fixed sets are the ledger's coverage-confound constraint made executable — 'condition on a FIXED instance set' is unenforceable until the set is an integer. Non-adaptivity is the pre-registration's own ban, defended here rather than lifted.
axes.falsifiable_check:
FRAME-BIAS TEST. On the same networks, the same C-hat and the same K, run the observable frame and the current oracle gate side by side and compare the separation distributions of the two admitted sets with a one-sided two-sample KS test at a level pre-registered from the realised n. DECISION RULE: if the observable frame's admitted separations are stochastically SMALLER than the oracle gate's, the frame selects for the corner where the radius is trivially defined; the population-shaping report then LEADS the results section instead of sitting in an appendix, and the headline is restated as conditional on the frame. Separately, the 3,738 pairs the oracle triviality test excluded are re-screened observably and the SIGN of the population change is reported, never absorbed.

POWER FLOOR, pre-registered per column so that no cell is read as a measurement when it cannot be one. For a proportion at the corpus-measured r=1 rate of 0.611, SE = sqrt(0.611*0.389/m): SE <= 0.05 needs m >= 96 instances, SE <= 0.02 needs m >= 594. The corpus at 831 gives SE = 0.017; the MEDIAN network yields 11 admissible instances, giving SE = 0.147. DECISION RULE: no per-network rate is printed as a rate. Per-network numbers are printed as counts with their denominator; only tier-level and corpus-level rates carry a percentage, and each carries its dispersion (between-network SD for fixed-corpus cells, seed SD for simulated ones).

CONTRIBUTION CHECK, which can narrow the paper. Run H4 on the same instance set. DECISION RULE: if r's three-bucket calibration (equal / SAFE / DANGEROUS) is not better than |K|'s on those instances, report in the paper that pricing does not beat counting your own claims on this population, and narrow the contribution to the geometry rather than the number.
axes.cost: Compute: the frame cuts X candidates to the 969 nodes lying in chain components plus their neighbours, against 7,062 nodes in the corpus, so the screen falls by roughly an order of magnitude from 115,974 pairs; at the observable filters' cost (polynomial possde plus a polynomial GAC call at ~1.07 ms at n=20) the whole screen is minutes, not the 1,200 s cap pathfinder burned. The RoCA co-report adds one chi-squared over stacked OLS coefficients per instance. Human: 6 h to write the frame into `measure.py` and re-derive the _meta schema (4 fields), 4 h for the population-shaping report, 3 h to port and validate RoCA (code at github.com/zehaosu/RoCA) and to record IN WRITING that its transfer from linear-SEM DAGs to MPDAGs is UNVERIFIED. Agent: ~30 h.

axes.axis: A3 KNOWLEDGE MODEL — source, coverage, granularity, and above all the error process
axes.decision:
`select_knowledge` and `knowledge_to_recover` leave the deployment path entirely. `knowledge_to_recover` is not deleted: it moves to the audit arm as the SCORING YARDSTICK K*, the minimal true recovering set against which an elicited K's omission, commission and invention rates are computed.

THE INVARIANT FIX THAT THE DRAFT MISSED. `oracle_on_path` is not a per-quantity flag; it is a TRANSITIVE PROVENANCE TAINT over every input to a record. Verified: `select_knowledge(dag, cpdag, coverage)` reads the DAG, and `synth/knowledge.py#tiered(dag, cpdag, rng, ...)` reads it too. So a knowledge set that is TRUE-but-incomplete, or that is corrupted RELATIVE TO the true temporal order, is oracle-derived even though `breakdown_radius` itself takes no DAG in its signature. The harness therefore propagates the taint through K's provenance, and a record whose K is oracle-derived cannot carry taint=false; the test matrix asserts exactly that, so the invariant is enforced instead of asserted.

DEPLOYMENT-ARM KNOWLEDGE SOURCES (taint false) — three:
K-SUR: an LLM surrogate, elicited in TRIPLET / causal-order form and never pairwise, on a LOCAL neighbourhood window of C-hat around the query (munin at 1,041 nodes does not fit in a prompt, and locality is what O* licenses), temperature 0, one pass, zero refinement passes in v1 as a declared and reported protocol parameter, prompt template versioned and hashed, mandatory response cache, model id and prompt hash in provenance, K frozen and hashed BEFORE r is computed. Cycles-emitted-before-repair is an EMITTED PROPERTY of K-SUR itself, not only a feature inside a downstream test.
K-PUB: knowledge harvested from each network's source publication — the retained dagitty annotations plus a coded read of the applied papers.
K-NULL, REDEFINED, because the draft's version is unrunnable. 'K contributes nothing' means K = empty, and `search/exact.py:85-94` returns as retractable exactly those edges directed in g and undirected in the CPDAG, so an empty K gives zero retractable edges, zero upper covers, and r = UNREACHED on 100% of instances by construction — a column of sentinels that may never be averaged and that carries no information. The correct vacuous null is a SIZE- AND PLACEMENT-MATCHED RANDOM CONSISTENT K: same |K| and same distance-from-X distribution as the K-SUR draw on that instance, orientations of C-hat's undirected edges drawn by fair coin, passed through Meek Algorithm 1, redrawn on FAIL up to a declared retry cap, with cap-exceeding instances recorded under their own status and never silently dropped. This is chance-level correctness, not zero information, which is the right null: it separates 'the radius is large because K is big' from 'the radius is large because K is right', and it is the natural anchor for Guess2Graph's better-than-random threshold.

AUDIT-ARM SIMULATED KNOWLEDGE (taint true) — two, and they stay controls rather than certificates:
K-MISS: consistent AND TRUE but incomplete. This is CHECKABLE #14's missing control arm; it exists, it is required, and it is read against the deployment rows on the fixed instance set — but it is oracle-derived and its radii are audit-arm quantities, never deployment certificates.
K-CORR: the tiered misfiling operator already sitting deterministic and unrun in `synth/knowledge.py`, where one wrong temporal-tier placement flips several claims at once.

WHAT EVERY K MUST EMIT, closing the A3 checkable list item by item:
#1 The reported error object is the POST-MEEK-FILTER fraction of CONSISTENT-BUT-FALSE assertions, and it is never called 'noise'. Consistency is syntactic and says nothing about truth; the silent-failure surface is the thing being priced.
#2 Coverage SEPARATELY per granularity — required edge, forbidden edge, tier, ancestral — never pooled, because tiers close under Meek R1 alone while single-edge assertions cascade through R1-R4.
#3 Coverage as a DISTRIBUTION of graph distance from X to each asserted claim, not a scalar.
#4 Error on ONE common scale across all sources as three separate rates — fraction reversed, fraction omitted, fraction invented — AND reported on the same scale as CSCD's 0.3 reversal rate and b-LOAD's rho and mu, so the three arms in this lineage are quantitatively comparable rather than merely adjacent.
#5 Commission and omission as separate axes with separate biases; a scalar error rate is inadmissible output.
#6 Error correlation, tested rather than assumed (see the check).
#7 ERROR RATE AS A FUNCTION OF GRAPH POSITION — by distance from X, and by edge type (data-compelled against assertable). The draft omitted this and it is the item the ledger marks UNSUPPORTED and calls the most load-bearing unmeasured quantity in the design, because O* is local and the radius equalled the separation in 792 of 792 designed instances. It costs nothing extra here: it is a by-product of A6-0's per-edge probes.
#8 Pre-filter K, post-filter K, and the Meek Algorithm-1 rejection rate, all three; the deployment object is the post-filter K, because that is what a practitioner ends up using.
#9 Elicitation form declared; triplet, never pairwise.
#10 Error split by assertion type AND by network AND by contamination stratum.
#11 Prompt versioned and hashed with the K it produced; independence across assertions is treated as misspecified by construction.
#12 Provenance: model id, prompt hash, mandatory response cache, K frozen before r.
#13 Confidence RETAINED in the record and NOT READ by the deployment arm until the audit arm has produced a calibration curve of stated confidence against measured correctness.
#14 K-MISS, above.

All four granularities are exercised. The perturbation operator on a tier is a BLOCK retraction costing one move in the assertion metric, reported on its own axis and never added to the edge metric.
axes.justification: The ledger's A3 names the current construction 'the single largest defect against the invariant': at coverage 1.0 — 543 of 831 admissible instances, 65% — G0 IS the true DAG exactly with zero undirected edges, and the greedy rule asserts whichever true orientation cascades furthest, biasing |K_G0| downward in a way no expert does. The taint-propagation fix is the ledger's own A6 recommendation ('a machine-checkable field recording, per quantity, whether the true DAG was on its computation path') taken one step further, because a per-quantity flag would have passed K-MISS and K-CORR as clean: the radius routine is oracle-free, its INPUT is not. Getting this wrong is how the current defect arose in the first place. The K-NULL redefinition is forced by verified code, not preference: `retractable_edges` freezes data-compelled edges, so nothing is retractable when K is empty; the draft's null would have produced a table column of -1 sentinels and been read as 'no failure found anywhere', the opposite of what a null is for. Triplet elicitation is forced by Vashishtha et al. arXiv:2310.15117 (verify CONFIRMED): pairwise edge queries to an imperfect expert produced >3k cycles on Child and >5k on Neuropathic against 0 under triplet, with SHD falling 177 -> 28, and Child, Asia, Alarm, Insurance and Sachs are all inside our own BIF corpus, so pairwise would make part of the measured error an artefact of the interface. Per-granularity coverage is CHECKABLE #2; placement as a distribution is CHECKABLE #3, licensed by b-LOAD arXiv:2607.04447's measured local-beats-global result; three separate error rates is CHECKABLE #5 (arXiv:2601.08258, PMC13281103, where laboratory elicitation shows omission dominating commission — the effect is 1.3-1.4x, not the 2.6x the ledger corrected). K-NULL and K-MISS together are the ledger's 'MISSING control arm', without which a large radius is confounded with vacuous knowledge — the Gervet et al. JEDM 2020 precedent, where an expert-designed structure adds <= +0.01 AUC on seven of nine real datasets. Refusing to read confidence follows from the ledger's correction on PMC9222732: stated confidence is data about the expert, not evidence about the edge, and the specific overconfidence figures did not survive verification. b-LOAD's premise that coverage rather than correctness is the binding limitation is that paper's ASSUMPTION and may not be cited as evidence about practitioners.
axes.falsifiable_check:
(i) CORRELATION OF ERROR IN GRAPH SPACE. Permutation test on whether the WRONG assertions of an elicited K are closer together in C-hat than a same-count uniform null predicts. DECISION RULE: if the test does not reject on K-SUR, the uniform symmetric-flip model that b-LOAD and our own CSCD both used is VINDICATED, the K-CORR arm's contribution is withdrawn in writing, and the paper says so. This is the check that can kill a component we want.

(ii) CASCADE-SIZE DISTRIBUTION (edges compelled per assertion), computed on all three candidate generators and on the referent. DECISION RULE: any generator whose cascade-size distribution differs from the referent's beyond the pre-registered tolerance is not the referent's generator and may not carry a claim about real knowledge. The statistic is cheap and has never been computed on any of the three.

(iii) DIRECTION PRESERVATION. Over 2,746 rows on 12 networks the measured direction is that WRONG knowledge INCREASES the radius (r=1 share 57.8 -> 56.8 -> 50.2 -> 42.1% as the flip rate rises 0 -> 0.1 -> 0.25 -> 0.5, median 1 -> 2, s>=2 share 40.6 -> 49.5%, max radius 14 and max separation 7 unchanged), which makes every true-knowledge-centred headline CONSERVATIVE. DECISION RULE: recompute the direction under the elicited error process; if it reverses, every existing headline loses its conservativeness argument and must be restated, and the reversal is the finding, not a footnote.

(iv) NULL SEPARATION, the check that decides whether the knowledge model is doing anything. On the fixed 543-pair set, compare K-SUR against K-NULL on the r distribution with a paired sign test. POWER, derived: for H0 p=0.5 against p=0.65 at alpha=0.05 two-sided and power 0.80, n_discordant = [1.96*0.5 + 0.8416*sqrt(0.65*0.35)]^2 / 0.15^2 = 85 discordant pairs. The measured discordance floor from wrong_knowledge.jsonl is the largest marginal bucket shift, ~0.16, so 85/0.16 = 531 paired instances are needed and the corpus supplies 543 unique pairs. DECISION RULE: this comparison is made at CORPUS level only; it is not powered on any single tier (T2-APPLIED holds 184 instances on 9 networks, short by a factor of ~2.9), and a per-tier non-rejection may never be read as 'the surrogate matches the null'.

(v) COVERAGE COMPARISON ON THE FIXED SET. Run it on the 106 instances admissible at coverage 0.25 and print the full-set numbers beside. The measured full-set coverage effect is 35.8 pp (r=1 at 69.8% -> 34.0%), which a paired test on 106 instances detects comfortably; anything below roughly 15 pp is not detectable on that set. DECISION RULE: state the 15 pp floor in the table caption, and never state a coverage difference smaller than it.
axes.cost: LLM calls, all cached at temperature 0, after the scope cut described in A6: K-SUR over 767 assertable edges in 33 networks at four granularities is roughly 2,400 calls; A6-0's held-out probes 1,808 plus a scrambled replicate 1,808; cold-recall 39 per model x 2 models = 78; a second model on the flagged contamination stratum, bounded by 1,808. Total ~7,900 cached calls, roughly 20M input plus 5M output tokens. Named in currency because the draft never was: ~EUR 650-900 across two model families, the only cash line in the protocol. Human, after the cut: the K-PUB prose harvest is 7 papers (Thoemmes_2013 is dropped — see A6 — because it yields zero admissible instances) x ~3 h = 21 h, plus a time-separated re-code of 3 papers at 1 h = 3 h, total 24 h, against the draft's 56 h. Plus 8 h to implement `LLMElicitor` and `to_background_knowledge`, both of which currently raise NotImplementedError, without letting a network call reach a test. Agent: ~50 h.

axes.axis: A4 PERTURBATION GEOMETRY — centre, distance, operator, reference measure
axes.decision:
Centre at Meek(C-hat, K) and never at the truth — already correct in code, since `breakdown_radius` takes no true DAG in its signature and `local_up_covers` takes (cpdag, g). Declare the unit as BFS hop count on the covering-relation neighbour graph RESTRICTED TO THE FIXED-SKELETON SUB-POSET G_{C-hat}, with the pseudo-rank reading (#directed + 2 x #undirected) reported alongside on every instance where the two are separately computable, because they provably differ off polytrees. Never SHD, and never the sentence 'tolerates k structural errors' with SHD as k. No rank arithmetic on the MPDAG poset.

The operator is RETRACTION, derived from upward-closure of failure rather than assumed; a flip is two atomic moves; a TIER retraction is one move in the ASSERTION metric and is never added to the edge metric; a FORBIDDEN-EDGE retraction is defined for the first time as the symmetric un-forbid move.

ADD THE REFERENCE MEASURE the geometry currently lacks: the shell failure fraction phi_j = (covers at shell j where Z fails) / (covers at shell j), uniform over covers, computed on top of the existing cover generation, with the O*-relevance-weighted version reported as a secondary. The certificate is then TWO numbers, r and phi, never one.

UNIFY the two geometries in circulation: the covering-graph BFS hop count is THE definition, and the r_0 probe's raw retraction-subset enumeration (sum over r <= j of C(|K|, r)) is an approximation, relabelled j_sub, with a measured disagreement rate against d on every instance where both terminate.

EXTEND SENTINEL DISCIPLINE BEFORE any new radius is measured. `conventions.py` currently defines UNREACHED = -1 and DEGENERATE = 0 and nothing else. It gains: declared semantics for r_opt, r_eps and r_0; three distinct sentinels for r_0's three infinite cases (no zero in the hull / hull undefined / extension cap hit), currently collapsed into one Python None; and — new, and forced by the K-NULL finding — a FOURTH sentinel NO_RETRACTABLE_EDGES, distinct from UNREACHED, because 'K asserts nothing that could be taken back' and 'nothing in the enumerated space fails' are different facts that today both print as -1 and would make a vacuous-knowledge arm indistinguishable from a maximally robust one.

THE PRIOR-ART GATE MOVES TO WEEK 1 AS A GO / NO-GO, before any compute is spent. It can kill the contribution, so it runs first, not last.
axes.justification: The ledger's A4 records SHD's over-certification as MEASURED (Taeb et al. Proposition 12 and Example 2: an explicit case with d_L,pseudo = 1 while SHD = n-1), the poset's non-gradedness for |V| >= 4 (Proposition 9, Table 3), and — stated three times in the source — that the MPDAG covering relation has NO known graphical characterisation, so neighbours cannot be enumerated and the poset cannot be searched in general. That is why the radius must condition on a fixed estimated skeleton, and why gradedness on G_{C-hat} is carried as a CONJECTURE in the `assumes` field, not asserted. The missing shell measure is a MEASURED gap: BFS returns the nearest failure and nothing about how much of shell j fails, while the calibration table already measures conservativeness at 0.43-0.47, i.e. roughly 44% of graphs outside the certified radius still admit Z — a guarantee that is right 100% of the time and tight 56% of the time is two numbers, not one. The O*-relevance weighting occupies the slot Taeb et al. section 7 declares empty (weighted covering relations as future work), which is also the slot a follow-up by that group would fill first. The two-geometry unification closes the ledger's finding that `breakdown_radius` walks the covering graph while the r_0 probe enumerates retraction subsets and 'its j is not the same metric as d'. The fourth sentinel is not decoration: it is the direct consequence of the verified fact that `retractable_edges` freezes data-compelled edges, and without it the null arm and the maximally robust arm are the same row. Moving the gate to week 1 is a scheduling decision with a cost argument: the vault's own record shows arXiv:2511.10625v3 was named 51 days before anyone read it in full, and the full read then RESHAPED the differentiation paragraph (their section 6 is one paragraph and one figure, in ADMGs, supergraphs only, no background knowledge, no Meek closure, no guarantee). Spending 245 agent-hours before checking whether the operator is AGM contraction under another name is the same mistake with a larger bill.
axes.falsifiable_check:
(i) UNIT DISAGREEMENT. Compute d_L and d_L,pseudo on the fixed-skeleton sub-poset for every instance where both terminate. DECISION RULE: a single instance where they differ forces every reported radius to name its unit and carry the polytree-equality caveat; the 48-element demo collapses them only coincidentally.

(ii) GRADEDNESS ON G_{C-hat}. Check computationally on every instance whose sub-poset is enumerable. DECISION RULE: one violation kills the conjecture, the exactness argument falls back to the pseudo-rank, and the paper says the sub-poset does not restore gradedness.

(iii) IS phi INFORMATIVE? phi at shell r is a ratio of integers whose resolution is 1/(covers at shell r). DECISION RULE: keep phi only if its within-r variance across instances exceeds that resolution, i.e. only if phi is not a deterministic function of r on the observed data. If it is, drop phi and report r alone; a second number that carries no second bit is decoration.

(iv) THE PRIOR-ART GATE, WEEK 1, GO / NO-GO. One recorded written verdict on each of eight units: stability radius (Sotskov, Emelichev); radius of robust feasibility (Goberna, Jeyakumar, Li, Vicente-Perez); Renegar's distance to ill-posedness; AGM contraction and epistemic entrenchment; minimal correction sets (Liffiton & Sakallah); inconsistency measures for knowledge bases (Hunter & Konieczny); specification-curve and multiverse analysis (Steegen et al.; Simonsohn, Simmons & Nelson; Patel, Burford & Ioannidis); and the two unresolved retrievals — arXiv:2511.10625v3 Appendix F.3, which failed retrieval three times, and the arXiv:2010.08611 identity conflict, where the same id returned two different titles across three passes. All eight return zero corpus hits and were never queried. DECISION RULE: if retraction is contraction under another name, or 'the smallest subset of asserted constraints whose retraction breaks a property' is a minimal correction set, or the fraction of specifications crossing zero is r_0's established population analogue in the specification-curve tradition, the operator claim is WITHDRAWN, the contribution narrows to the Meek-closure-plus-background-knowledge instantiation, and the remaining 240 agent-hours are re-scoped before they are spent rather than after.
axes.cost: Compute: phi is a by-product of cover generation already performed by the BFS, so its marginal cost is the validity call per cover — at ~1.07 ms per polynomial GAC call at n=20, phi over one shell of a 12-undirected-edge G0 is ~13 ms, and over all 831 instances ~11 s; across 3 deployment knowledge arms and 3 n-levels, under 3 minutes. The d_L versus d_L,pseudo differential and the gradedness check run only on enumerable sub-posets, minutes. The j_sub-versus-d differential runs on the instance intersection of the two current arms, which the split forbids today and which becomes possible once the gate is polynomial. Human: 16 h for the prior-art gate, derived as 8 units x 2 h and not an estimate; 4 h for the sentinel extension in `conventions.py` including the fourth sentinel and its test; 3 h for the tier and forbidden-edge move definitions. Agent: ~35 h.

axes.axis: A5 STATISTICAL LAYER — oracle CPDAG against an estimated one, sample sizes, estimator, and the tractability wall
axes.decision:
TWO CPDAG TIERS, never pooled, side by side. C-hat_O, computed from the true DAG, is a true-DAG quantity ON the computation path, so under the invariant every number computed on it belongs to the AUDIT arm — including every number the project currently holds. C-hat_E, estimated at finite n by a CPDAG-EMITTING method (PC or GES; never a front end that emits a fully oriented DAG, because a skeleton-times-order factorisation commits to one topological order and destroys the undirected chain component the radius is defined on), is the only CPDAG the deployment arm sees. Both regimes plot on Pi = n / (|V| * d_exp/2).

The estimator stays the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell standard error from Sigma alone, the same formula serving population Sigma and sample Sigma-hat; the true DAG enters only to generate the sample by ancestral simulation, which is nature's licensed role.

Say once and early which of three the certificate is: a DETERMINISTIC COMBINATORIAL CERTIFICATE, a deterministic functional of (C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n) — not a Bayesian credible bound, not a distribution-free conformal set. The deployment arm reports r and phi and ISSUES NO COVERAGE STATEMENT; any coverage statement lives in the audit arm, carries a resampling or test-inversion correction, and is reported CONDITIONAL ON r rather than marginally.

THE TRACTABILITY WALL, answered directly. The 1,839.78 s call is `is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag`, the extension-ENUMERATING validity predicate, on a 46-node network with 25 undirected edges, i.e. a 2^25 global enumeration. THIS PROTOCOL NEVER CALLS IT. Validity is decided everywhere by the polynomial `is_gac_valid_mpdag` (`src/bkrobust/gac/mpdag_level.py:298`), verdict-identical on Z = O(.) by Theorem 14 and verified rather than assumed on 2,240 pairs across child, insurance, asia, sachs and water with 0 disagreements at 8.2x (20.22 s -> 2.47 s). The arithmetic that shapes the whole design: 831 instances x 12 covers in one shell x 1,839.78 s = 18.35M s = 212 DAYS for a single shell of the corpus, and 6.13 h for one shell of ONE instance; the same 9,972 calls with the polynomial predicate at ~1.07 ms is 10.7 s. A protocol that calls the enumerating gate once per graph in a ball is a wish; this one calls it zero times.

The remaining exponential is `optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag` (`demo/evaluate.py:288`), which calls `enumerate_dag_extensions(g)` GLOBALLY and is what forces MAX_G0_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS = 12 and drops 280 pairs. It is COMPONENT-RESTRICTED, exactly as `theta`/`sub_component` already does for pa_D(x) in `output/2026-09-09_rnull-real/rnull_real.py:92-124`: pa_D(x) depends only on x's chain component and O* = pa(cn(X,Y)) \ forb(X,Y), so the enumeration factorises over the components cn(X,Y) touches. On ecoli70 that replaces 2^25 by 2^(edges inside the touched components), whose node sizes are at most 10; corpus-wide, 33 of 39 networks have max_component_size <= 12, so most of the corpus becomes fully tractable and the 280 dropped pairs are recovered.

EVERY RECORD IN EVERY ARM carries one schema: method, oracle, exact, assumes, stats, plus the transitive `oracle_on_path` boolean and an `arm` field. Censored runs keep `wall_until_timeout_s` on a _meta row and are never counted as measurements; measurement limits stay distinct from structural rejections.

SCOPE CUT, stated rather than discovered. The finite-n arm runs on the 30 corpus networks with n <= 109 at THREE sample sizes, not 33 networks at four. Sizes derived from Pi: on the median admissible network (|V| = 32, mean degree 3.04, denominator 48.7), n in {500, 5000, 50000} gives Pi = 10.3 / 102.7 / 1026.8, spanning two decades, which is what a two-panel Pi plot needs. The 9 networks above n = 109 are dropped and NAMED with their yield: munin1 (6 admissible), andes (0), diabetes (89), pigs (0), link (0), munin2 (0), munin4 (0), munin (0), munin3 (0) — together 95 of 831 admissible instances, 11.4%, of which 89 are diabetes alone. The per-network wall cap stays at the repo's own 1,200 s rather than being raised to a round 3,600, so the censoring behaviour is comparable with the existing runs; raising it is a separate, argued decision.
axes.justification: The repo's own manifest names the oracle-CI idealisation as its largest scope limit, and the ledger holds 'robust under an ESTIMATED CPDAG' FORBIDDEN until the discovery arm runs. Two-panel reporting is licensed and obligatory because the direct parent paper (LOAD, arXiv:2510.14582) already reports both regimes side by side, and Pi is the group's published reporting axis. The CPDAG-emitting requirement is Thompson et al. Arrow arXiv:2605.07204, whose G = A tensor M(pi) is acyclic by construction and cannot ingest required or forbidden orientations. No coverage statement in the deployment arm follows from Gradu/Zrnic/Wang/Jordan, Chang/Guo/Malinsky and Strieder et al.: naive two-step inference after discovery inflates miscoverage, and the certificate's determinism does not sidestep it. Conditional-on-r reporting is Smucler/Robins/Rotnitzky's scope discipline for the small-radius corner. The component restriction is the ledger's 'highest-leverage change in the repo', and the ledger is explicit that it needs a theorem plus a differential test rather than just a speedup, which is why the check below is written as it is. Cost-substitution discipline comes from the fast_gate precedent, where the author predicted the substitution was strictly weaker and the differential showed it strictly STRICTER: 16 disagreements in 46,800 cases (0.034%), all one-directional, all excluding instances where r_val(O) = UNREACHED, i.e. biased AGAINST our own hypothesis. The scope cut is derived, not chosen: the excluded networks hold 11.4% of the admissible instance mass and 89 of those 95 instances come from one network, so the cost of the cut is a single named network rather than a diffuse loss, and saying so is cheaper than discovering at week 9 that PC on 1,041 nodes at four sample sizes did not finish.
axes.falsifiable_check:
(i) THE COMPONENT-RESTRICTION DIFFERENTIAL. Pre-register the predicted direction as 'verdict-identical', then run the component-restricted O* against the global enumeration on EVERY pair where the global version terminates (|G0 undirected| <= 12) and publish the disagreement rate WITH ITS SIGN. DECISION RULE: any disagreement at all kills the substitution, the 280-pair intractable stratum stays intractable, and the restriction is reported as a rejected optimisation next to the accepted ones — the repo already records one such rejection (testing G0's one-level upper covers is 746x faster on pathfinder and WRONG, because retracting a knowledge edge and re-closing can land strictly above a cover).

(ii) THE C-hat_E STRUCTURE TEST, TWO-SIDED, and this is the one that can kill the framework. The draft anticipated only collapse; both directions are live and must be pre-registered, because PC's missed weak edges remove v-structures and can INCREASE the undirected fraction rather than shrink it. Measure the undirected fraction and the chain-component-size distribution of C-hat_E at each n against the descriptive table committed for C-hat_O (assertable pool 767 undirected against 9,004 compelled, 7.85% of 9,771 edges, median undirected fraction 0.107, 6 of 39 networks fully compelled, 25 of 39 yielding any admissible instance). DECISION RULE, DOWN: if at the largest n the median undirected fraction falls below half the oracle's 7.85% assertable share, the headline changes from 'the breakdown radius on real structure' to 'the radius is defined on a vanishing fraction of a discovered graph', and that becomes the paper's finding rather than a limitation. DECISION RULE, UP: if the undirected fraction rises materially, every oracle-CPDAG number in the project is a LOWER bound on applicability and the scope sentence must be rewritten in the opposite direction — the 6 fully compelled networks and the 14 zero-yield networks are then re-run rather than excluded, which is why none of them is dropped from the finite-n arm's denominator.

(iii) THREE-BUCKET CALIBRATION UNDER C-hat_E, never an agreement rate, because agreement hides the sign. Measured precedent from r_0: the point hull errs DANGEROUS 24.7% at n = 200 and still 18.1% at n = 20,000, while the 95% band errs dangerous <= 1.7% at every n even though the band's raw agreement looks worse (7.8% against 57.0% on magic-irri at n = 200). DECISION RULE: if the point version of r errs dangerous at a rate that does not fall materially between the smallest and largest n on the Pi grid, the point certificate is abandoned for a band version, exactly as r_0 was — a danger rate barely improving over a hundredfold sample increase is the argument that this is a coverage problem and not a sample-size problem.
axes.cost: Zero seconds on `is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag`, by construction. The polynomial gate over the whole design is seconds (9,972 cover-validity calls at ~1.07 ms = 10.7 s), against 212 days for the enumerating one; that ratio is the single most important cost fact in the protocol and belongs in the paper. Component restriction recovers the 280 dropped pairs and lifts MAX_G0_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS from 12 toward the largest touched component, with 33 of 39 networks at max_component_size <= 12. The finite-n arm after the cut is bounded by 30 networks x 3 sample sizes x 1,200 s cap = 108,000 s = 30 h, against the draft's 132 h — a 77% reduction bought by dropping 11.4% of the instance mass, concentrated in one network. Human: 8 h for the factorisation lemma and its differential harness, 4 h for the transitive `oracle_on_path` field and the manifest checker, 4 h for the discovery-arm configuration (CI test, alpha, n grid) written down before it runs. Agent: ~55 h.

axes.axis: A6 REALISM AUDIT — the external referent, built rather than cited, and the calibration of the certificate
axes.decision:
Eight components. A6-0 is the centrepiece and everything else hangs off it.

A6-0, THE HELD-OUT COMPELLED-EDGE PROBE. Take an edge that the DATA compelled IN C-hat_E — the estimated CPDAG, stated explicitly, because scoring against C-hat_O would put the oracle back on the path — un-orient it to form C-hat_E-minus, elicit the surrogate blind on C-hat_E-minus in a local window, and score its answer against what the data compelled. This measures the surrogate's per-edge error rate, split into reversed / omitted / invented, by assertion type, by network, AND BY GRAPH DISTANCE FROM X and by edge type, which is how CHECKABLE #7 gets measured for free. No true DAG is read, so it runs unchanged on T3 where no truth exists. On T1 and T2 the same edges are also scored against the truth, and the CORRECTION FACTOR between error-on-compelled-edges and error-on-assertable-edges is measured there and carried to T3.
A6-0b, THE PLACEBO LEG, new: run the same masked probes with SCRAMBLED node names. The named-minus-scrambled gap on masked edges is a contamination read that requires no truth at all, so unlike A6-4 it is available on T3. It bounds memorisation from above and domain knowledge from below and does not separate them; that limitation is written down rather than glossed.

A6-1, THE DISCRIMINATOR. Per network, build K from the generator and from the referent and run a permutation two-sample test on a pre-registered feature vector (coverage per granularity; distance-from-X distribution; false-assertion and false-omission rates separately; pairwise graph distance among the wrong assertions; Meek Algorithm-1 rejection rate; cascade size; cycles emitted before repair), tolerance pre-registered BEFORE the referent is looked at.

A6-2, THE RADIUS-TRANSFER TEST, the one with teeth because the reported quantity is r and not K: hold the instance set FIXED at the 543 unique (X,Y) pairs and compare full radius distributions on pre-declared summaries (r = 1 share, median, max, agreement with r <= min(s, |K_G0|)), reporting the SIGN.

A6-3, THE POSITIVE CONTROL, rebuilt on the MATCHED T0-CONTROL of A1 — and rebuilt correctly, which the draft got wrong: K-SUR CANNOT RUN ON A RANDOM GRAPH, because an ER draw has no variable semantics for a surrogate to reason about. On T0-CONTROL the only admissible surrogate arm is the SCRAMBLED-NAME one, which doubles as A6-0b's semantics-free floor; the structural arms K-NULL and K-CORR run there unchanged. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: A6-3 validates the power of the two-sample machinery on structural knowledge features, not on the K-SUR-versus-K-PUB contrast specifically.

A6-4, THE CONTAMINATION SCREEN: named elicitation, scrambled elicitation, and a cold-recall probe; flagged networks move to a separately reported stratum and are NEVER pooled. Threshold derived per network as the upper 99th percentile of a label-shuffling permutation null on adjacency recall, not stipulated.

A6-5, CALIBRATION IN THREE BUCKETS — equal / SAFE / DANGEROUS — never an agreement rate.

A6-6, EVPPI over assertions, with loss = absolute bias of the adjusted estimate against the estimand at the true DAG, RESTRICTED to T1-BENCH and to instances where the recorded number of valid adjustment sets is >= 2, because on a single-valid-set instance there is no alternative decision for information to improve. That restriction is a scope cut with a reason, not a convenience.

A6-7, THE INCUMBENT CO-REPORT: for every instance where r fires, report whether Su & Henckel's RoCA test would have fired. RoCA is itself oracle-free, so it runs in the DEPLOYMENT arm.

The manifest declares `analysis_summary.json` canonical and every report reads from it, ending the situation where four committed files carry different headline figures for the same quantity.

SCOPE CUTS, named. (a) The full-corpus scrambled replicate of the main K-SUR elicitation is CUT; scrambling moves to the 1,808 masked probes, which is the right instrument anyway and halves ~2,400 duplicated calls. (b) The K-PUB prose harvest drops Thoemmes_2013: it yields ZERO admissible instances (verified), so harvesting its prose buys no rows, and the harvest is 7 papers ordered by yield — Polzer_2012 (66 instances), Kampen_2014 (42), Schipf_2010 (13), Sebastiani_2005 (11), Shrier_2008 (10), Acid_1996 (10), Didelez_2010 (8). (c) The SECOND CODER is cut unless a named second human takes it. There is one person on this project. A kappa computed by one person is not an inter-coder kappa; the fallback is a time-separated re-code of 3 of the 7 papers reported explicitly as INTRA-coder agreement, with the sentence 'every A6-1 result is conditioned on one coder's reading' printed in the limitations. The mitigation is to assign the second read to the named collaborator on this line, which also changes the completion odds: this vault's own measurement says a task where someone is already waiting closes at 54% and a task Ze must initiate alone closes at 0% (n = 40).
axes.justification: The ledger's A6 headline is MEASURED: no published study measures a domain expert's per-edge error rate, separating omission from commission, on expert-specified causal DAGs scored against a known-true DAG. This survived a 1,100-note corpus grep, a seven-dimension web sweep and a gap-fill that exhausted a 200-call budget and was blocked by HTTP 403 at Reliability Engineering & System Safety, Risk Analysis, IJAR and Knowledge-Based Systems, the four journals where the measurement would most plausibly live. So the referent must be BUILT. A6-0 is the ledger's own named template made concrete: Veitch & Zaveri arXiv:2003.01747, corrected in the ledger from 'oracle-requiring' to its true form — delete an OBSERVED quantity from the baseline data and check whether predicted harm tracks realised harm, explicitly without ground truth. The transposition is exact: 'observed' becomes 'compelled by the data', and the holdout pool is 9,004 compelled edges against 767 assertable ones, 11.7x larger, so power is not the constraint. Specifying C-hat_E rather than C-hat is not pedantry: masking an edge of the ORACLE CPDAG and scoring against it would reintroduce the oracle on the very path the protocol exists to clear. Refusing an LLM as validator is mandatory (arXiv:2606.12071: judges and domain experts reach opposite conclusions on the same pairs, and pairwise comparison, the standard remedy, is worse); scoring is mechanical, against the truth in the audit arm or against the data in A6-0. A6-4 is forced because ASIA, ALARM, CHILD, INSURANCE and SACHS all sit in our 24-network BIF corpus and in published LLM-plus-SCM evaluation sets; the pooling precedent is verified (pooling the designed family with the random ones moved a headline 14 points, 79.6% -> 65.3%). A6-5's three buckets and the refusal of agreement rates are our own measured precedent. A6-6 exists because epistemic restraint reads as under-delivery: both reviewers of our restrained CSCD paper read 'stability not correctness' as its ceiling rather than its strength. A6-7 licenses the narrow claim and refutes the forbidden broad one — RoCA characterises which graph errors are detectable, so the licensed sentence is that the class of orientation errors keeping all valid adjustment sets valid is untestable by consistency checks, and THAT is the class the radius prices.
axes.falsifiable_check:
(i) THE BRIDGE CHECK, which decides whether the protocol's central idea works. In the audit arm on T1 and T2, compute the surrogate's error rate on masked compelled edges and on assertable chain-component edges. DECISION RULE: extrapolation to T3 is admissible only if |error_compelled - error_assertable| is smaller than the between-network dispersion of either rate. If it is not, the correction factor is unstable, the T3 numbers are uninterpretable, and the paper states in writing that the oracle-free bridge FAILED and that the surrogate's error rate on a real dataset cannot be estimated by this route. The bias is real and known a priori — compelled edges are compelled because they sit in v-structures or Meek cascades, so they are not exchangeable with the edges an analyst must assert — and the check converts a caveat into a measured, reportable quantity. SECOND LEG, new: the bridge is usable only if the compelled-edge error rate VARIES across networks. DECISION RULE: if its between-network variance does not exceed the sampling variance implied by each network's probe count, the rate is a constant, carries no per-network information, and the correction factor is a single global scalar that must be reported as such rather than as a per-network adjustment.

(ii) A6-3 MUST REJECT on the matched control. DECISION RULE: if the two-sample machinery does not separate matched-ER structural knowledge from real-substrate structural knowledge on the pre-registered feature vector, the machinery has no power and every A6-1 and A6-2 result is uninterpretable and is withdrawn.

(iii) A6-2's SIGN. DECISION RULE: a surrogate producing systematically LARGER radii than the harvested referent on the fixed instance set is optimistic about robustness — the dangerous direction — and that is printed as the headline of the surrogate arm, not reported as a difference. A certificate computed on surrogate knowledge would then overstate safety exactly where the framework is most likely to be used.

(iv) POWER, PRE-REGISTERED AND REPORTED NEXT TO EVERY VERDICT, because the draft's 'the power is UNKNOWN' is not a protocol. A6-1 compares n1 = 9 dagitty networks that yield admissible instances against n2 = 25; the effective per-group n is 2*n1*n2/(n1+n2) = 13.2, and 80% power at alpha = 0.05 needs n_eff = 16/d^2, so d = 1.10 — one full between-network SD. Reaching d = 0.8 requires n_eff = 25, i.e. n1 ~ 25 applied DAGs. DECISION RULE: A6-1 prints 'powered only against d >= 1.10' beside its verdict, a non-rejection is NEVER read as agreement, and the derived target for the dagitty public model repository and Tennant et al. (IJE 2021) forward citations is 25 applied DAGs, not 'more'. A6-2's paired sign test needs 85 discordant pairs for 80% power at p = 0.65, and at the measured discordance floor of ~0.16 that is 531 paired instances against the corpus's 543 unique pairs. DECISION RULE: A6-2 is a corpus-level test only; on T2-APPLIED (184 instances, 9 networks) it is short by a factor of ~2.9 and no per-tier verdict is issued.

(v) SAMPLE-SIZE HONESTY ON THE REFERENT, stated with the verified integer. Of the 12 dagitty files, exactly ONE — Didelez_2010 — carries an adjusted-node annotation AND yields admissible instances, with 2 adjusted nodes and 8 instances. Thoemmes_2013 carries the only other adjusted node and yields zero instances; its 4 latent markers are SEM error terms. So the published-expert adjustment sets that reach the pipeline are 2 assertions on 8 instances from 1 paper. DECISION RULE: that sentence is printed verbatim in the limitations and no A6-1 or A6-2 claim about 'what applied authors assert' is made from the annotation channel alone; it must come from the 7-paper prose harvest or not at all.
axes.cost: A6-0: min(84, n_compelled) masked probes per network across all 39 networks = 1,808 probes, VERIFIED by recomputation from descriptive_structure.csv. The 84 is derived: a per-network error rate near the only anchor we have (0.3, our own CSCD flip rate) carries SE <= 0.05 when 0.3*0.7/0.05^2 = 84; 26 of 39 networks have fewer than 84 compelled edges and are capped by availability, so their rates are reported with their realised SE and pooled only by tier. The corpus-level rate at 1,808 probes carries SE <= 0.02 (the requirement is 525). Cached LLM calls: 1,808 plus the scrambled replicate 1,808, plus 39 cold-recall probes per model x 2 models, plus a second model on the flagged stratum. A6-3 rides the matched control from A1 at no extra cost. A6-6 EVPPI is one loss evaluation per assertion per instance, cheap once the estimator is the Sigma-hat formula, and it runs only on the T1 instances with >= 2 valid adjustment sets. Human: 6 h to pre-register the A6-1 tolerance and derive the A6-4 threshold; 4 h to write the EVPPI loss down; 3 h to make every report read from `analysis_summary.json`. Agent: ~55 h. Every arm must be rerunnable by a third party from committed artefacts, which means committing a generator script for the control arm — the one place the existing audit apparatus fails the standard it sets for everyone else.

arms: ARM D — DEPLOYMENT. Computes the reported certificate from analyst-observable quantities only: r, phi, the RoCA verdict, the H4 |K|-count baseline, the number of valid adjustment sets, and the assertable-edge fraction, all as functionals of (C-hat_E, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n). HELD FIXED: `oracle_on_path = false` on every record, checked by TRANSITIVE PROVENANCE TAINT over every input and not by a per-quantity flag, asserted by the harness before any record is written; the observables-only sampling frame; the polynomial GAC validity predicate; the deterministic seeded stride; K frozen and hashed before r is computed; no coverage statement issued; confidence retained but not read. VARIES: substrate tier (T0-CONTROL, T0-FIXTURE, T1-BENCH, T2-APPLIED, T3-REAL), deployment knowledge source (K-SUR, K-PUB, K-NULL), granularity (required / forbidden / tier / ancestral), n on the C-hat_E grid at Pi = 10.3 / 102.7 / 1026.8. Runs identically on all five tiers INCLUDING T3, where no true DAG exists; that completion is the protocol's principal claim.

ARM A — POST-HOC AUDIT. Opened only after the ARM D record for an instance is written and hashed. Reveals the truth to score, never to compute: the elicited K against K* = knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag); r against the true failure distance in three buckets (equal / SAFE / DANGEROUS, never an agreement rate); the contamination decomposition; the EVPPI loss; and every number computed on the oracle CPDAG C-hat_O, which under the strict reading of the invariant belongs here in its entirety. IT ALSO HOLDS THE TWO SIMULATED KNOWLEDGE SOURCES, K-MISS and K-CORR, because both read the true DAG (verified: `select_knowledge(dag, cpdag, coverage)` and `synth/knowledge.py#tiered(dag, cpdag, rng, ...)`) — their radii are controls for reading the deployment rows, never certificates. HELD FIXED: the instance set, the same 543 unique (X,Y) triples ARM D used, so the two arms join row by row; the hash, checked before the truth is opened. VARIES: the same factors as ARM D, minus T3, where this arm is EMPTY BY CONSTRUCTION and the emptiness is reported rather than hidden.

K-SUR (deployment knowledge sub-arm). LLM surrogate, triplet / causal-order elicitation on a local window of C-hat. FIXED: temperature 0, one pass, zero refinement passes, prompt template hash, model id, mandatory response cache, no LLM ever used as validator, cycles-before-repair emitted as a property of the arm. VARIES: assertion granularity, network, contamination stratum (named / scrambled / cold-recall), and, for A6-4 only, model identity across two model families.

K-PUB (deployment knowledge sub-arm). Knowledge harvested from each network's source publication: the retained dagitty exposure/outcome/adjusted/latent annotations plus a coded prose read of SEVEN applied papers, ordered by admissible-instance yield — Polzer_2012 (66), Kampen_2014 (42), Schipf_2010 (13), Sebastiani_2005 (11), Shrier_2008 (10), Acid_1996 (10), Didelez_2010 (8). Thoemmes_2013 is dropped: it yields zero admissible instances. FIXED: the coding scheme, the four granularities, adjudication before use. VARIES: paper, coder, granularity. This is the referent A6-1 and A6-2 test against, and it is the arm whose sample size binds the whole design.

K-NULL (deployment control, REDEFINED). A size- and placement-matched random consistent K: same |K| and same distance-from-X distribution as the K-SUR draw on that instance, orientations of C-hat's undirected edges drawn by fair coin, passed through Meek Algorithm 1, redrawn on FAIL up to a declared retry cap. FIXED: everything else in the cell, and the matching to K-SUR. VARIES: the seed. NOT the empty set — an empty K makes `retractable_edges` empty, hence zero covers and r = UNREACHED on 100% of instances by construction. This arm separates 'the radius is large because K is big' from 'the radius is large because K is right', and it is chance-level correctness rather than zero information, which is the correct anchor.

K-MISS (audit control, taint true). K is consistent AND TRUE but incomplete. FIXED: truth of every assertion. VARIES: coverage per granularity, and placement. This is the arm every false arm is read against; without it a large radius is confounded with a weak claim set. Any comparison across its coverage levels runs on the 106 instances admissible at coverage 0.25, never on the full 831, because the strata are non-comparable populations (543 / 182 / 106, with survivors having systematically larger separation).

K-CORR (audit control, taint true). The tiered misfiling operator: one wrong temporal-tier placement flips several claims at once. FIXED: the operator, deterministic, already in `synth/knowledge.py` and never run on real graphs. VARIES: which node is misfiled, and the resulting realised wrongness, reported POST-filter because the Meek consistency check itself filters the error process (6.8% realised for an intended 10%, 25.6% for 25%, 51.6% for 50%, with up to two thirds of corrupted draws rejected outright).

T0-CONTROL (substrate sub-arm). The five random generators, density- and size-matched to the real corpus and run through the identical pipeline. FIXED: K construction, validity gate, coverage handling, sampling frame, reporting schema — everything the current comparator arm does not share. VARIES: generator, EXPECTED DEGREE in {2.00, 3.50, 9.86} (not edge probability), size in {5, 14, 20, 27, 36, 48, 76, 109} (the instance-weighted octiles of the admissible corpus, reaching 88.6% of instance mass where the current sweep's n<=30 reaches 46.2%), seed. K-SUR CANNOT RUN HERE — a random graph carries no variable semantics — so the only surrogate arm on this tier is the scrambled-name one; K-NULL and K-CORR run unchanged. Labelled a negative control on every figure and never pooled.

T0-FIXTURE (substrate sub-arm). The designed backdoor family plus the recovered M-bias, entered as the explicit five-node latent expansion E <- U1 -> Z <- U2 -> D plus E -> D, because the file's two BIDIRECTED edges are why is_dag=False and it is an ADMG rather than a broken DAG. FIXED: designed structure. VARIES: n. Always reported separately, because pooling the designed family with the random ones already moved one headline 14 points (r = 1 at 79.6% over 1,914 random rows against 65.3% over 2,334 pooled), and because the designed family supplies every radius above 5 including the pooled maximum of 13.
primary_table:
TABLE 1 — the transfer ladder. ROWS: one per design cell the protocol actually runs, a cell being (substrate tier x knowledge source x CPDAG tier), ordered T0-CONTROL, T0-FIXTURE, T1-BENCH, T2-APPLIED, T3-REAL down the page, and K-SUR, K-PUB, K-NULL within each tier for the deployment block with K-MISS and K-CORR appearing only in audit-block rows, with C-hat_E at Pi = 10.3 / 102.7 / 1026.8 and C-hat_O appearing only in audit rows.

COLUMNS, in three blocks divided by rules. BLOCK 1, DEPLOYMENT (oracle_on_path = false, populated in EVERY row including T3): n_instances on the cell's fixed instance set, printed beside its denominator-selection rate; share at r = 1, network-weighted with the pair-weighted figure in brackets and the dispersion after, labelled SEED or BETWEEN-NETWORK because the two are not interchangeable and a fixed-corpus cell has only the second; median r; max r; phi at shell r as median with interquartile range; share where the bound r <= min(s, |K_G0|) holds, printed with ITS OWN denominator, which is the measured-separation subset (463 of 831 on the current corpus, 55.7%) and not the row's n_instances; RoCA fire rate; H4 three-bucket agreement; assertable-edge fraction of C-hat. BLOCK 2, AUDIT (oracle_on_path = true, EMPTY in every T3 row): SAFE / equal / DANGEROUS shares; the surrogate's per-edge error split into reversed, omitted and invented, and additionally as a function of graph distance from X and of edge type; the A6-2 radius-transfer verdict with its sign AND its realised power; median EVPPI on the >=2-valid-set instances. BLOCK 3, BRIDGE, one column, the only one spanning every tier: the held-out compelled-edge error rate on C-hat_E, with the compelled-versus-assertable correction factor appended on T1 and T2 where the truth exists to compute it, and the named-minus-scrambled placebo gap beside it.

WHAT A ROW MEANS: one design cell aggregated over its own fixed instance set — the same (X,Y) triples under every knowledge source in that tier, so rows within a tier are joinable and differences are attributable to the knowledge source rather than to the population — carrying its dispersion, never pooled across tiers, and never mixing a coverage stratum with a differently stratified arm. Two exceptions are printed as rules in the caption, not discovered by the reader: a per-network number is a COUNT, never a percentage, because the median network yields 11 admissible instances and a proportion there carries SE = 0.147; and the T3 rows carry no fractions at all but list their instances one per line, because Sachs yields 13 admissible instances and any proportion on 13 carries SE >= 0.139.

WHY A REFEREE READS IT FIRST: the T3 rows have a fully populated deployment block, a structurally empty audit block, and a populated bridge column. That single visual fact is the paper's whole claim — the certificate computes on a real dataset with no graph, the calibration does not, and the bridge column is the only thing carrying calibration from where truth exists to where it does not.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_r:
Every T3 row's deployment block fills in. The radius, the shell failure fraction, the RoCA verdict and the |K| baseline are all computed on a real dataset from an estimated CPDAG and an elicited knowledge set, with no true DAG anywhere on the path, and the harness confirms `oracle_on_path = false` transitively over every input — including the knowledge provenance, which is where the current pipeline actually fails.

The bridge check passes: the surrogate's error rate on masked compelled edges sits within the between-network dispersion of its error rate on assertable edges, measured on T1 and T2 where both are computable, and that compelled-edge rate genuinely varies across networks rather than being a constant, so the T3 number is interpretable and the surrogate's realism is a measurement rather than an assumption.

The audit arm then shows the certificate conservative in the direction that matters — the DANGEROUS bucket stays small under C-hat_E across the Pi grid, as the 95% band did for r_0 at <= 1.7% at every n — while r is materially tighter than the |K| count, so pricing beats counting your own claims. K-SUR separates from K-NULL on the fixed 543-pair set at corpus level, so the knowledge is doing something beyond being the right size in the right place. A6-3 rejects on the matched control, giving the two-sample machinery power on structural features. A6-1 fails to reject between K-SUR and K-PUB at the realised power, which is reported as 'not distinguishable at d >= 1.10' and never as agreement. A6-2 shows no systematic radius inflation, so the surrogate is not optimistic about robustness.

RoCA fires on a minority of the instances where r is small, so the untestable class the radius prices is non-empty in practice and the narrow claim form is earned rather than asserted. The bound r <= min(s, |K_G0|) continues to hold out of sample under elicited, non-cascade-maximising knowledge, keeping the safe-moves reading r - 1 anchored to something an analyst can see. The matched control still separates from real structure by more than three seed-dispersion standard errors on a grid that now covers 88.6% of the admissible instance mass rather than 46.2%, so Decision 2's substrate tiering is a substrate argument rather than a tuning defect. And the week-1 prior-art gate returns that retraction on a Meek closure of asserted background knowledge is not AGM contraction, not a minimal correction set, and not a specification curve — which is the only way the operator survives as the differentiator against Taeb, Guo & Henckel.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_w:
Seven concrete outcomes, each of which this protocol can produce and none of which the current pipeline can.

(1) THE CPDAG STRUCTURE TEST GOES EITHER WAY AND BOTH ARE BAD FOR THE CURRENT NUMBERS. DOWN: under C-hat_E at the largest n the median undirected fraction falls below half the oracle's 7.85% assertable share, chain components fragment, the radius is undefined on most instances, and the honest headline becomes 'the radius is defined on a vanishing fraction of a discovered graph' — plausible, since 6 of 39 networks are already fully compelled and only 25 of 39 yield any admissible instance under the oracle. UP: PC's missed weak edges destroy v-structures, the undirected fraction RISES, and every oracle-CPDAG number in the project turns out to be a lower bound computed on the wrong graph — in which case the 831-instance corpus is not the population the framework applies to and the descriptive table committed before the first radius has to be recomputed from scratch.

(2) THE BRIDGE FAILS. |error on masked compelled edges - error on assertable edges| exceeds the between-network dispersion of either, or the compelled-edge rate turns out to be a constant across networks. The correction factor is then unstable or uninformative, the surrogate's error rate on a real dataset cannot be estimated by this route, and the protocol reports a fully computed deployment block on T3 with no way to say whether the knowledge feeding it is realistic — which is exactly the epistemic position the redesign was meant to escape.

(3) THE DANGEROUS DIRECTION. A6-2 shows K-SUR producing systematically larger radii than K-PUB on the fixed instance set, so a certificate computed on LLM knowledge overstates safety precisely where the framework is most likely to be used; or the three-bucket calibration under C-hat_E errs DANGEROUS at a rate that barely falls across a hundredfold sample increase, as the r_0 point hull did at 24.7% then 18.1%, which makes the point certificate indefensible and forces a band version.

(4) THE NULL IS NOT SEPARABLE. K-SUR and the size- and placement-matched random K-NULL produce indistinguishable radius distributions on the 543-pair set at corpus level. The radius is then a function of how many claims you make and where, not of whether they are right, and the entire knowledge-model axis collapses into |K| and a distance distribution — which H4 already computes for free.

(5) THE BOUND BREAKS. Under elicited knowledge the agreement with r <= min(s, |K_G0|) falls well below the 72.8% measured on real networks, with the 110-above / 16-below exception asymmetry worsening, so r is not bounded by anything the analyst can see and the safe-moves reading loses its anchor.

(6) PRICING BUYS NOTHING. RoCA fires on most instances where r is small, so the class of errors the radius prices is empty on this population; and H4 matches r's three-bucket calibration, so the number adds nothing over counting your own claims and only the geometry survives as a contribution.

(7) THE OPERATOR IS NOT OURS, RETURNED IN WEEK 1 RATHER THAN WEEK 12. The prior-art gate finds that retraction is AGM contraction under another name, or that the smallest subset of asserted constraints whose retraction breaks a property is a minimal correction set, or that the fraction of specifications crossing zero is r_0's established population analogue in the specification-curve tradition. In which case the one part of A4 claimed as unshared against Taeb, Guo & Henckel is not, the contribution narrows to the Meek-closure-plus-background-knowledge instantiation, and the remaining 240 agent-hours are re-scoped before they are spent.
known_weaknesses: The strict reading of the invariant moves the ENTIRE oracle-CPDAG arm into the audit arm, invalidating every number the project currently holds — 831 instances, the separation table, the radius distribution, the law agreement — as deployment-arm evidence. A maximum-power lens would keep C-hat_O as a labelled deployment idealisation with a caveat and have results now; mine says a CPDAG computed from the true DAG is a true-DAG quantity on the computation path, full stop. That costs roughly two months and the project's whole existing headline set.

The held-out compelled-edge probe measures error on a biased subpopulation BY CONSTRUCTION: compelled edges are compelled because they sit in v-structures or Meek cascades, and the edges an analyst must assert are exactly the ones the data could not settle.
