The correction factor is measurable on T1 and T2, but it is itself estimated on the benchmark tier, so T3's number is only as good as the correction's transferability — and the ledger records that no published structural-matching or transfer criterion for graph FAMILIES exists anywhere in the searched literature. This is the weakest joint in the design and the bridge check is the only thing standing between it and an unfalsifiable claim.

The transitive taint correctly exiles K-MISS and K-CORR to the audit arm, which is right under the invariant and costs the deployment arm its two most informative controls. The deployment block can therefore say 'the radius is large' and 'the knowledge was not vacuous' (K-NULL), but it cannot say 'the radius is large because the knowledge was incomplete rather than wrong' without stepping into the audit arm — and on T3 that step is unavailable, so the T3 rows carry the weakest interpretation of any tier despite being the protocol's headline.

Refusing to let the deployment arm read per-assertion confidence until the audit arm produces a calibration curve discards information the `elicit.py` scaffold was explicitly designed to retain, and it forecloses a soft-constraint geometry in v1. Our own CSCD result says soft beats hard under noisy knowledge — replacing hard constraints with a lambda-penalty restores recall to the no-knowledge level at comparable precision — so a Bayesian or soft-constraint lens would weight by confidence immediately and would have a measured reason to.

Component-restricting O* recovers the 280 pairs currently dropped as o_g0_extensions_intractable, and those are precisely the pairs with the largest chain components, i.e. the most under-determined ones. That should raise the radius distribution, and it will look like the redesign flattered its own framework. Pre-registering the predicted direction is the only defence and it is a weak one.

Replacing the true-DAG triviality filter with triviality at G0 changes the admissible population by an amount nobody can predict from outside; 3,738 screens were decided by that filter. Both populations are reported but only the observable one defines the frame, so the difference is a measured selection effect rather than a corrected one. A population-purity lens would insist the two be reconciled before any headline is stated.

Network-weighting as the headline underweights exactly the large networks where the tractability story is hardest, and the finite-n cut then drops nine of them outright (munin1, andes, diabetes, pigs, link, munin2, munin4, munin, munin3), losing 11.4% of admissible instance mass. A scalability referee will ask about precisely those networks and the answer will be that we did not run them.

Elicitation is local, on a neighbourhood window of C-hat, because a 1,041-node network does not fit in a prompt. That makes the surrogate's coverage a function of window size, which is a protocol parameter I fix rather than sweep. A query-policy lens would sweep it and would be right that an unswept window size is a hidden degree of freedom in every error rate the protocol reports.

EVPPI needs a loss defined against the estimand at the true DAG, so the decision-relevant quantity does not survive to T3 — the one tier where a practitioner most needs to know whether the certificate changes a decision. Restricting it further to instances with >= 2 valid adjustment sets is defensible but shrinks it again, and I have no oracle-free substitute.

The A6-1 discriminator has 80% power only against a shift of 1.10 between-network SDs, and reaching d = 0.8 needs about 25 applied DAGs against the 9 that yield instances today. Worse, exactly ONE dagitty file (Didelez_2010) supplies a published expert's own adjustment set that reaches the pipeline at all — 2 adjusted nodes on 8 instances. Every non-rejection from this arm is therefore uninterpretable as agreement, and no amount of machine time changes it.

The second coder is cut because there is one person on this project, so the reported kappa is INTRA-coder on a time-separated re-code of 3 of 7 papers. That is a materially weaker reliability statistic than the draft promised, and the mitigation — assigning the second read to the named collaborator on this line — is itself a task whose completion this vault measures at 54% when someone is waiting and 0% when self-initiated (n = 40).

The pre-registration's ban on adaptive elicitation is kept rather than lifted, even though adaptive and information-maximising elicitation is published and would raise coverage per call substantially. I defend the ban as a protocol commitment; an active-learning lens would lift it deliberately and accept the adaptivity accounting.

The whole design assumes the polynomial GAC predicate and the enumerating one coincide on Z = O(.), which is Theorem 14, verified on 2,240 pairs with zero disagreements but not proved; and every exact radius still inherits the Anti-Exchange Case B chain whose failure direction inflates radii, i.e. is optimistic about robustness. Both caveats travel with every number, and neither is retired by anything in this protocol.
total_budget:
WALL CLOCK: 12 weeks, in four phases, with one hard gate at the front.

WEEK 1 IS A GO / NO-GO AND NOTHING ELSE RUNS. The prior-art gate (8 units, 2 h each) returns a written verdict on stability radius, radius of robust feasibility, Renegar's distance to ill-posedness, AGM contraction, minimal correction sets, inconsistency measures for knowledge bases, the specification-curve family, and the two unresolved retrievals (arXiv:2511.10625v3 Appendix F.3, failed three times; the arXiv:2010.08611 identity conflict). If retraction is contraction under another name the contribution narrows and the remaining 240 agent-hours are re-scoped before they are spent. The vault's own record is the argument for putting it first: the competing preprint was named 51 days before anyone read it in full, and the full read then reshaped the differentiation paragraph.
Weeks 1-3: code changes and their differentials — the observable frame, the component-restricted O*, the `annotations` field, the sentinel extension including NO_RETRACTABLE_EDGES, the transitive `oracle_on_path` taint and its checker, the RoCA port.
Weeks 2-8, on the critical path: the K-PUB harvest, human-bound.
Weeks 3-9: elicitation, the held-out probes, the finite-n discovery arm, the matched control.
Weeks 9-12: the audit arm, the two-sample tests, the writing.

AGENT-HOURS: ~245, down from the draft's 300. A1 ~20, A2 ~30, A3 ~50, A4 ~35, A5 ~55, A6 ~55.

UNATTENDED MACHINE TIME, bounded by the repo's own caps rather than estimated: the T1/T2 re-screen is bounded by 39 networks x 1,200 s x 3 deployment arms + 39 x 1,200 for K-CORR + 9 x 1,200 for K-PUB (only 9 dagitty networks yield admissible instances) = 198,000 s = 55 h, with the observed slowest instance at 0.16 s so the realised figure is far below; the finite-n arm is 30 networks x 3 sample sizes x 1,200 s = 108,000 s = 30 h; the matched control at 24 cells x S seeds is roughly one sixth of the 2,880-draw arm it replaces. Total bounded machine time ~95 h.

CASH: ~7,900 cached LLM calls at temperature 0, roughly 20M input and 5M output tokens across two model families, ~EUR 650-900. The only cash line, and the draft never named one.

HUMAN-HOURS: ~89 for Ze, against the draft's 150. Prior-art gate 16 (8 units x 2 h). Pre-registration and threshold derivation 10 (4 documents x 2.5 h). K-PUB prose harvest 24 (7 papers x 3 h, plus 3 re-coded at 1 h). Code review 9 (6 changes x 1.5 h). Analysis and writing 30. A recruited second coder adds ~21 h of someone else's time and converts the intra-coder statistic into a real kappa.

WHAT WAS CUT, AND WHY, rather than left as a number that will not survive contact. (a) The second coder: 56 h -> 24 h, because there is one person on this project; the reliability statistic degrades from inter- to intra-coder and that is printed in the limitations. (b) Thoemmes_2013 from the harvest: it yields zero admissible instances, so its prose buys no rows; 8 papers -> 7. (c) The finite-n grid: 33 networks x 4 sample sizes -> 30 networks x 3, dropping the 9 networks above n = 109 and 95 of 831 admissible instances (11.4%), of which 89 come from diabetes alone; the sample sizes are derived from Pi spanning two decades (10.3 / 102.7 / 1026.8) rather than chosen. (d) The full-corpus scrambled elicitation replicate: moved onto the 1,808 masked probes, which is the right instrument anyway, saving ~2,400 duplicated calls. (e) EVPPI restricted to T1 and to instances with >= 2 valid adjustment sets, because a single-valid-set instance has no alternative decision for information to improve. (f) The per-network wall cap stays at the repo's own 1,200 s rather than being raised to a round 3,600, so censoring stays comparable with the existing runs.

THE GATE COST, stated because it shapes the protocol. One call to `is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag` took 1,839.78 s on a 46-node network with 25 undirected edges. Calling it once per graph in a ball is 12 covers x 1,839.78 s = 6.13 h for ONE shell of ONE instance, and 831 x 12 x 1,839.78 s = 18.35M s = 212 days for one shell of the corpus. THIS PROTOCOL CALLS IT ZERO TIMES. The polynomial `is_gac_valid_mpdag` does the identical work — verdict-identical on Z = O(.) by Theorem 14, verified on 2,240 pairs with 0 disagreements at 8.2x — in 9,972 calls at ~1.07 ms = 10.7 s. The remaining exponential, `optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag`'s global `enumerate_dag_extensions`, is component-restricted along the lines `theta`/`sub_component` already uses in the r_0 probe, turning 2^25 on ecoli70 into an enumeration over components whose largest node size is 10, with 33 of 39 networks at max_component_size <= 12.

BINDING CONSTRAINT: not compute, and not a deadline — Ze fixed that there is none. It is the HARVESTED-PUBLICATION REFERENT, and now with an integer on it. Of the 12 dagitty files, exactly ONE (Didelez_2010) carries an adjusted-node annotation AND yields admissible instances: 2 adjusted nodes on 8 instances. Nine dagitty networks yield instances at all, against 25 for the benchmark arm, giving the A6-1 discriminator an effective per-group n of 13.2 and 80% power only against d = 1.10; reaching d = 0.8 needs about 25 applied DAGs. No amount of machine time increases that. The mitigation — the dagitty public model repository, Tennant et al. (IJE 2021) and its forward citations, and the seven source papers themselves — was specified as a search task in the sweep and executed in none of the three passes, so it is both the binding constraint and the cheapest unstarted work on the board. And it is a task Ze must initiate alone, which this vault measures at 0% completion against 54% when a counterparty is already waiting (n = 40), so the protocol's real first move on that axis is to hand step one to the named collaborator on this line rather than to schedule it for himself.

name: Buy the Gate, Count Networks
one_sentence: The obvious protocol buys precision with more (X,Y) pairs and prints one radius per knowledge source; this one buys a polynomial validity gate once for about ten core-hours and then spends everything on independent networks, because the intraclass correlation recomputed from results/axisa3/per_network.csv is 0.398 on the r=1 indicator, which makes the committed 831 instances worth 60.1 effective observations against a hard ceiling of k/rho = 2.51 per network, and because every cross-source radius comparison is run on a common support at matched |K| — otherwise "this source gives a smaller radius" and "this source asserted fewer things" are literally the same number, since r <= |K| by construction.
one_sentence_correction_note: Three arithmetic errors in the prior draft are corrected here and drive different decisions: n_eff on the uncapped corpus is 60.1, not 21; a per-network cap LOWERS n_eff (60.1 -> 55.3 at cap 15) rather than doubling it; and elicited K is predicted to give LARGER radii than the oracle-cascade arm, not smaller, because the repository's own wrong-knowledge sweep measures the r=1 share falling 57.8% -> 42.1% as wrongness rises.

axes.decision: Three declared substrate tiers plus one labelled instrument arm plus one descriptive-only latent stratum, sized by NETWORK COUNT and never by instance count. T1 BENCHMARK CORPUS: the 39 parsed DAGs, expanded by ingesting bnRep (200+ networks from 150+ publications, each carrying acquisition mode data-driven / expert-elicited / hybrid) until the number of YIELDING networks reaches k* = 112, derived below. T2 APPLIED-PAPER DAGs: the 11 parsed dagitty files plus the dagitty public model repository plus the forward-citation set of Tennant et al. (IJE 2021) — the modality the gap-fill pass specified and never ran. T3 REAL DATASETS WITH A DOMAIN-ACCEPTED GRAPH: Sachs plus the four bnjson networks fitted to real data (ecoli70 from E. coli microarrays), reported as accepted-not-true, with precision and recall against the reference graph explicitly refused and the refusal printed in the caption. INSTRUMENT ARM (never a substrate tier): Erdos-Renyi parameterised by EXPECTED DEGREE over the corpus's own measured band (mean degree 1.60 to 9.86, median 2.92, computed over the 39 DAG rows of descriptive_structure.csv), never by edge_prob, run through the one pipeline with the same knowledge source, gate, cap and recorded seeds; it exists only to give the A6-3 positive control power, which is how Decision 2's rejection of structure-matched synthetic generators is honoured rather than contradicted. LATENT STRATUM: M-bias is recovered as an ADMG rather than forced through the is_dag parse flag, and is DESCRIPTIVE ONLY — see the compute axis for why this is a declared cut and not an oversight. Per-network instance cap 12 (derived in A2). THREE ACQUISITION-SIDE RULES, each closing a defect the ledger names: (i) a descriptive table is committed before any radius is computed, carrying per network the node count, edge count, mean degree, undirected fraction, chain-component size distribution, var-sortability and R^2-sortability under the fitted coefficients, acquisition mode and publication year; (ii) NO ARM'S DATA MAY BE USED UNTIL ITS GENERATOR SCRIPT IS COMMITTED — the current ER comparator has none, which is why its K-selection rule and gate are unverifiable from the tree, and it is the one arm that fails the third-party-rerun standard this project imposes on everyone else; (iii) ONE CANONICAL NUMBERS FILE — every report, figure and caption reads its statistics from a single machine-written numbers.json, because four committed files presently carry different values for the same separation statistic and the two ledgers disagree about which belongs to which.
axes.justification: The acquisition target is arithmetic, not ambition. Recomputing the one-way-ANOVA intraclass correlation from results/axisa3/per_network.csv over the 25 yielding networks gives rho_hat = 0.3978 on the r=1 indicator (N=831, k=25, m0=30.51, MSB=3.179, MSW=0.150) and 0.4578 on separation>=2 (N=463, k=21, m0=19.44). At the observed mean cluster size of 33.2 the design effect is 13.8 and n_eff = 60.1, so the committed 61.1% r=1 share carries a network-clustered 95% half-width of 12.3 points, i.e. roughly [49, 73] — the dispersion the ledger's A6 convention demands and that no headline in circulation carries. Because n_eff -> k/rho as cluster size grows, 25 yielding networks cap the effective sample at 62.8 no matter how many pairs are ever drawn, and the observed 60.1 is already 96% of that ceiling: the corpus is saturated. The top five networks supply 66.4% of the 831 instances (barley 189, insurance 160, diabetes 89, Polzer_2012 66, magic-niab 48), so extra pairs buy correlated rows and nothing else. k* = 112 follows from the audit's power requirement: the DANGEROUS ceiling test needs n_eff >= 200 (Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95% upper bound at an observed 1.7% is 3.83% at n_eff=200, 5.09% at n_eff=150 which resolves nothing), the design point is n_eff = 250 (upper bound 3.62%), and at cap 12 the design effect is 1 + 11*0.398 = 5.378 so n_eff = 2.231k, giving k = 250/2.231 = 112. Only 25 of 39 parsed networks yielded any admissible instance under the current frame and 33 of 39 have a chain component of size >= 2, so k* = 112 needs roughly 140 to 175 acquired networks at the observed yield — which is why bnRep is load-bearing and why the stopping rule below narrows the claim rather than the corpus. bnRep is independently licensed by the ledger's A1 entry as the second acquired source that turns a corpus claim into a population claim. The expected-degree parameterisation is forced by the ledger's correction that ER's expected degree is (n-1)p and grows with n, so no single edge_prob cell holds the corpus density constant across a size sweep. M-bias is recovered because the pre-registration's exclusion argument is correct as written (bidirected edges make it an ADMG; silently dropping them makes it indistinguishable from a real 3-node DAG) and because it is the textbook structure the framework prices.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE TRANSFER TEST, pre-registered on a STRUCTURE-ONLY statistic. The joint distribution is (max chain-component size, undirected fraction, separation s, mean degree) — deliberately excluding |K_G0|, which the prior draft included and which is knowledge-source-dependent, so a tier could be rejected for how it was elicited rather than for what it is. Before any radius is reported over an acquired tier, run a permutation two-sample test of that joint against T1 at alpha = 0.01 with 10,000 permutations (alpha = 0.01 is Bonferroni-conservative for the three tier comparisons at family 0.05; 10,000 permutations puts the Monte Carlo standard error at 0.001, an order below alpha). DECISION RULE: if T2 or T3 is rejected against T1, no quantity measured on T1 may be stated over that tier, the pooled row is deleted from the primary table, and the tiers are reported separately. SECOND RULE, on yield: if an acquired tier's yield (fraction of its networks producing at least one admissible instance under the new frame) differs from T1's by more than 15 percentage points, the admissibility frame itself is shaping the tiers differently and no pooled row may be printed regardless of the transfer test — the frame, not the substrate, would be the variable. THIRD RULE, on acquisition: if after exhausting bnRep and the dagitty repository k_yield < 112, print the achieved network-clustered half-width and NARROW the claim to the achieved precision. The claim is never widened by drawing more pairs from networks already held; that is the move this axis exists to forbid.
axes.cost: Compute: acquisition, parse and CPDAG for roughly 175 networks is about 5 to 10 minutes, extrapolated from the committed seconds_to_cpdag column (60.95 s total over 39 networks, 1.56 s mean, 21.8 s maximum on one) — the extrapolation is by network count and the risk is that bnRep networks are larger than the current median, which the 21.8 s maximum bounds only loosely. Sortability probes are seconds. Agent-hours: about 14 for the bnRep ingester, the ADMG stratum path, the sortability probes and the canonical numbers file. Human-hours: about 5 to adjudicate licence terms and the acquisition-mode labels, which are the field the realism audit conditions on.

axes.decision: An observables-only sampling frame, declared before it runs, plus a COMMON SUPPORT rule that fixes the instance population before any source is compared. FRAME: draw X uniformly from nodes lying in a chain component of C-hat of size >= 2; draw Y uniformly from possde(X, G0) minus {X}; then apply only the four filters that read no true DAG — knowledge_inconsistent (Meek Algorithm 1 returns FAIL), O(G0) not identified, O(G0) extension enumeration above the component-restricted cap, and O(G0) empty-and-valid re-derived on G0 by the polynomial GAC predicate rather than on the DAG. The five true-DAG filters are REMOVED from the deployment path: no_causal_path tested on dag.descendants (42,618 rejections), no_valid_adjustment_set, empty_set_trivially_valid (3,738), no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity (1,659), and knowledge selection itself. The degeneracy facts they encoded become AUDIT-ARM LABELS attached to retained instances, so the population is shaped by nothing the analyst cannot see. COMMON SUPPORT: the primary table's row population is the set of instances on which EVERY OBSERVABLE knowledge source (LLM surrogate, harvested-publication, null, random-consistent) yields a K that survives the Meek consistency filter. The oracle sources are evaluated on that support and never define it — if they did, the truth would re-enter the deployment population through the back door, which is exactly what a naive fixed-instance-set rule does. Per-source attrition to the common support is printed as a first-class number. CAP: 12 instances per network. CENSORING: a per-instance wall cap of 60 s emitting CENSORED-BUDGET, recorded separately from o_g0_extensions_intractable (a measurement limit) and separately again from a structural rejection — the three-way separation the vault's audit apparatus already enforces. RECORDS: a per-network _meta row with total ordered pairs, sampled pairs, the REALISED count (never the target rate, which currently disagrees with the integer stride by up to 23% on hailfinder), the seed, and the realised u_G0 distribution. Per (X,Y), record the number of valid adjustment sets, because that decides whether the incumbent test has power on that instance. WEIGHTING: every aggregate is printed both network-weighted and pair-weighted, per network first, zero-yield networks kept in the denominator; NETWORK-WEIGHTED IS THE HEADLINE, because the clustering is at network level and n_eff is a network-level quantity — the ledger records both weights and no rule, and the two differ materially (r=1 at 61.1% pair-weighted against 71.3% network-weighted). Before any radius, publish the pre-filter and post-filter distributions of (component size, s, |K|): the population-shaping report the pre-registration promised and never delivered.
axes.justification: The invariant permits the true DAG in exactly two post-hoc places and the ledger's A2 entry enumerates which filters violate that and which four survive; the observables-only causal-path test Y in possde(X, G0) is named there as the replacement. THE CAP IS DERIVED AND ITS PURPOSE IS NOT POWER. Recomputing n_eff against cap over the 25 yielding networks at rho_hat = 0.398 gives: cap 5 -> N=120, n_eff=47.8; cap 8 -> 181, 52.0; cap 10 -> 217, 53.5; cap 12 -> 245, 54.4; cap 15 -> 277, 55.3; cap 20 -> 327, 56.3; uncapped -> 831, 60.1. Capping therefore COSTS about 10% of the effective sample and saves 70% of the instances — the prior draft's claim that capping at 15 raises n_eff from 21 to 49 is wrong in both numbers and in sign. The correct justification is marginal information: below cap 12 an instance is worth 0.222 units of n_eff on average, the 13th through 20th are worth 0.021 each, and beyond cap 50 they are worth 0.0048 each — a 46-fold difference. Cap 12 keeps 90.5% of the achievable n_eff for 29.5% of the compute and stops barley (189 instances, 23% of the corpus) from setting a pair-weighted headline. The near-flatness of that whole column, 47.8 to 60.1 across a 7-fold change in N, is the demonstration that k binds and pairs do not. THE COMMON SUPPORT RULE closes a confound the ledger's CHECKABLE #8 implies but nobody has stated: drop_inconsistent restores consistency and does nothing about truth, and up to two thirds of corrupted draws are rejected outright, so a knowledge source that asserts aggressively loses instances that a timid source keeps — and a fixed instance set defined post hoc is then a different population per source. Recording the count of valid adjustment sets is licensed by Su and Henckel: a robustness test needs at least two valid sets, so pairs with exactly one are where testing is unavailable and pricing is the only instrument. The realised-rate defect and the missing shaping report are both open items in the ledger's A2 section. The u_G0 record is new and is the single most important unmeasured cost driver: across ALL 831 committed admissible instances g0_undirected_edges is exactly 0, a direct consequence of oracle knowledge, so every timing in the tree (7.16 s total, 0.158 s slowest) is uninformative about what an elicited, partial K will cost.
axes.falsifiable_check: THREE CHECKS. (1) FILTER SHAPING: run the frame with and without each retained filter and compare the resulting (component size, s, |K|) joint by a two-sample permutation test, and compare the frame's separation distribution against the current enumerate-everything policy's. DECISION RULE: if removing a filter shifts the separation distribution by a KS statistic above 0.10, that filter is population-shaping and every claim conditioned on it must name it in the sentence, not in an appendix. The 0.10 threshold is above the noise floor by construction: at the expected N of about 1,340 split evenly the two-sample KS critical value at alpha=0.05 is 1.358*sqrt(2/670) = 0.074, so 0.10 is a practical-significance bar rather than a significance test. (2) THE FRAME'S OWN FAILURE MODE: if the new frame's separation distribution has a LARGER share at s = 1 than the old policy's, the frame has selected for pairs where the radius is trivially defined; it is rejected and rewritten, because that is the failure that would make the whole table look good for the wrong reason. (3) COMMON-SUPPORT ATTRITION: if any source retains less than 60% of the frame's instances into the common support, that source is reported as a descriptive stratum with its attrition printed and never as a table row with an interval — a source that loses 40% of the population has stopped being a treatment applied to a fixed population and has become a selection rule.
axes.cost: Compute: screening is pure graph work; the frame over roughly 175 networks is about 10 minutes. The stage-0 pilot that measures the u_G0 distribution under elicited K is 3 core-hours and gates the sweep budget — it is not optional, because without it the deployment sweep's cost is unknown to within an order of magnitude. Agent-hours: about 12 for the frame rewrite, the common-support machinery and the _meta schema. The expensive part is not compute but honesty: removing the five DAG-reading filters changes the admissible population, so every committed number changes, and that is reported as a change with the old and new populations side by side, never presented as a fix.

axes.decision: Both select_knowledge functions are deleted from the deployment path — benchmarks/measure.py:103 and synth/component_generator.py:416 — not tuned. They are replaced by a KnowledgeSource protocol whose single method is elicit(chat, node_names, provenance) -> list[Constraint], with no dag parameter anywhere in its call graph. SEVEN SOURCES, all emitting the same Constraint type across four granularities (required edge, forbidden edge, tier, ancestral). OBSERVABLE: S1 LLM SURROGATE, queried causal-order-first then by triplets and NEVER by pairwise edge questions, temperature 0, R = 3 elicitation replicates whose only difference is a permuted variable-presentation order (which is simultaneously the dispersion mechanism and the measurement of mention-order bias), R = 10 on a 12-network dispersion subsample, model id and prompt hash stored with a mandatory response cache, K frozen before r is computed, refinement budget declared as 0 and reported. S2 HARVESTED FROM SOURCE PUBLICATIONS, every constraint carrying a verbatim quote and a document locator, produced by an LLM extraction pass and audited by a HUMAN sample — never by a second model, since judges and domain experts reach opposite conclusions on the same pairs and the bias is worst in the comparative setting. S3 NULL (K empty), reporting identification status and effect-set width at C-hat rather than a radius. S6 RANDOM-CONSISTENT, the labelled negative control: |K| matched per instance to S1's realised |K|, orientations drawn uniformly from the orientable edges of X's chain component without regard to truth, rejected and redrawn if Meek returns FAIL. STIPULATED, audit-labelled, never pooled with the observable four: S4 ORACLE-TRUE-SUBSET (the taxonomy's MISSING arm, consistent AND true but incomplete), S5 ORACLE-CASCADE (the existing knowledge_to_recover, kept for exactly two jobs — reproducing the committed numbers under the new frame, and scoring an elicited K post hoc), S7 TIERED MISFILING, the correlated-error operator that already exists in synth/knowledge.py, is deterministic, is called the realistic case by its own docstring, and has never been run on real graphs. EVERY SOURCE EMITS THE FULL CHECKABLE VECTOR, item by item against the ledger's list: (1) admissibility — the error unit is the fraction of assertions that PASS Meek Algorithm 1 and are false, reported as consistent-but-false and never as noise; (2) coverage per granularity, four numbers, never pooled; (3) placement — the distribution of graph distance from X to each assertion, and from Y; (4) error rate on ONE common scale across sources, as a fraction of the orientable edges in X's chain component, deliberately the same denominator as b-LOAD's rho and mu and CSCD's 0.3 so the three arms are quantitatively comparable, with realised-versus-intended printed for the stipulated sources (the repository measures 6.8% realised for an intended 10%); (5) error asymmetry — omission, commission and reversal as three separate rates, never one scalar; (6) error correlation — a permutation test asking whether wrong assertions are closer together in the graph than a same-count uniform null predicts; (7) dependence on graph position — error rate as a function of distance from X AND split by edge type, data-compelled versus orientable; (8) consistency survivorship — pre-filter K, post-filter K and the rejection rate all stored, with generator and referent compared only AFTER the same filter; (9) elicitation form — the query form declared and cycles-emitted-before-repair reported as a property of the source; (10) assertion-type stratification — accuracy split by assertion type AND by network, never a single scalar; (11) prompt as part of the error model — prompt versioned and hashed with the K it produced, and NO null anywhere in the protocol may assume independence across assertions; (12) provenance and caching — cache mandatory, model id and prompt hash stored, K frozen before r; (13) confidence retained not thresholded — stored, kept as a distinct confidence-weighted object, and the deployment arm is FORBIDDEN to read it until the audit arm publishes a calibration curve of stated confidence against measured correctness; (14) the MISSING control arm — S4, with taxonomy.classify() actually implemented so every assertion lands in the {ORIENTATION, ANCESTRAL, TIER, SPURIOUS, MISSING} x {BENIGN, EFFICIENCY, VALIDITY, UNIDENTIFIABLE} grid and the severity distribution is reported.
axes.justification: This is the ledger's largest single defect against the invariant, and the repository is worse than the ledger states: select_knowledge calls knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag), 543 of 831 admissible instances (65%) sit at coverage 1.0 where G0 IS the true DAG exactly, and recomputation over instances.jsonl shows g0_undirected_edges = 0 on ALL 831 admissible instances at every coverage level — the ball is centred on a fully oriented graph in the entire corpus, not merely in two thirds of it. knowledge_to_recover is also greedy and cascade-maximising, biasing |K_G0| downward, which is the other binding term of r_val <= min(s, |K_G0|). THE TWO BIASES HAVE OPPOSITE SIGNS and that is why the fixed-support comparison is the whole point: oracle centring makes the radius optimistic (the repository's own wrong-knowledge sweep measures the r=1 share falling 57.8 -> 56.8 -> 50.2 -> 42.1% as the flip rate rises 0 -> 0.5, i.e. wrongness INCREASES the radius), while cascade-greed makes |K| small and the radius conservative. Which dominates is unmeasured, and the prior draft's prediction that elicited K gives smaller radii is backwards on both counts. S6 exists because r <= |K| by construction, so any cross-source radius comparison at unmatched |K| confounds knowing less with being wrong; matching |K| per instance and randomising the orientations gives the floor a coin-flip expert would produce, which is the only thing that makes 'the surrogate knows something' a measurement rather than a hope. Order-and-triplet elicitation is forced by Vashishtha et al.: pairwise queries to an imperfect expert produced over 3,000 cycles on Child and over 5,000 on Neuropathic where triplet queries produced none, with SHD falling 177 to 28, and Child, Asia, Alarm, Insurance and Sachs are all inside our own BIF corpus, so pairwise elicitation would manufacture part of the error process we then measure. R = 3 is the minimum that yields a between-replicate variance estimate at all (2 degrees of freedom) and R = 10 on a subsample supplies the 9-degree-of-freedom estimate that variance is actually taken from; temperature 0 alone would give zero dispersion, which would violate the requirement that every rate carry its variance. All four granularities are mandatory because b-LOAD's noise study is confined to required edges and that confinement is the one weakness all four of its reviewers named. Confidence is retained but quarantined because expert confidence statements are systematically miscalibrated, so a confidence is data about the expert and not evidence about the edge. The NULL arm is forced by the Gervet precedent, where an expert-designed structure added at most +0.01 AUC on seven of nine datasets.
axes.falsifiable_check: FOUR CHECKS. (1) THE INVARIANT GUARD, machine-checkable rather than a paragraph: an AST test asserting that no function reachable from the deployment entry point takes a dag argument or references knowledge_to_recover, either select_knowledge, or dag.descendants, plus a manifest field true_dag_on_path printed per reported quantity. DECISION RULE: any deployment-arm number whose manifest field is not FALSE is unpublishable, and the test failing is a build failure, not a warning — the same idiom the vault already uses to assert the absence of a transport layer in mailsearch. (2) THE |K| CONFOUND CHECK, and it can kill the headline: stratify every cross-source radius comparison by |K_G0| decile and re-run it within strata. DECISION RULE: if the radius gap between S1 and S4/S6 vanishes once |K| is conditioned on, the finding is a statement about how much each source asserts and not about whether it is right, and it must be restated in those words. (3) THE CASCADE CHECK, which decides whether the ledger's charge against knowledge_to_recover is true: compute the cascade-size distribution (edges compelled per assertion) for S1, S2, S4, S5 and S7 on the same networks. DECISION RULE: if S1's or S2's distribution is not distinguishable from S5's at alpha = 0.05, the greedy bias is NOT an artefact, the ledger's claim that knowledge_to_recover systematically under-counts |K| is refuted, and that is written as a refutation of our own premise rather than quietly dropped. (4) THE CORRELATION NULL: the permutation test for checkable #6 uses a same-count uniform null over the orientable edges, and its own validity is checked by running it on S6, whose errors are uniform by construction. DECISION RULE: if the test rejects on S6 the instrument is broken and no correlation finding may be reported from it.
axes.cost: Model calls, derived per network from the committed structure: 7.1 chain components, 19.7 undirected edges and 24.8 nodes-in-components per network (276 components, 767 undirected edges, 969 nodes-in-components over 39 networks), giving one causal-order query per component, one triplet and one forbidden-edge query per undirected edge, one tier query per component and one ancestral query per retained instance — about 65.6 queries per network-replicate. At 112 networks x R=3 that is 22,000 calls, plus 12 networks x 7 extra replicates for the dispersion subsample (5,500), plus the contamination screen at 2 models x 3 conditions x 40 networks (6,400), plus the harvest extraction at roughly 10 calls over about 50 source papers (500): about 34,500 calls in total. Agent-hours: about 45 to build elicit.py, taxonomy.py, the random-consistent sampler and the harvesting extractor out of the current NotImplementedError scaffold (31 NotImplementedError bodies across the five knowledge modules), whose specifications are already better than anything the built code does. Human-hours: about 12 for the extraction audit — 60 harvested records verified per tier at roughly 4 minutes each, which with zero errors bounds the extraction error rate at 4.87% by an exact one-sided 95% interval; 80 records would give 3.68% and cost 4 more hours per tier, which is the trade made explicitly.

axes.decision: Centre at G0 = Meek(C-hat, K) and never at the truth, which breakdown_radius already satisfies since it takes no DAG. The distance is on KNOWLEDGE SETS, not on graphs: d(K, K') = |K minus K'| for K' a subset of K, so one unit is one asserted claim withdrawn. The operator is RETRACTION, with a declared BLOCK retraction for a tier — retracting a tier removes its whole orientation block, counts as one move, and is reported in a separate column because the unit differs — and a forbidden-edge retraction move, which the current operator lacks entirely. r_val = min{|S| : Z = O(G0) is not valid at Meek(C-hat, K minus S)}. Because failure is upward-closed under retraction (THEOREMS.md Theorem 1: refinement shrinks the represented DAG set, so orienting more can never invalidate a fixed valid set), r_val is the cardinality of a minimum MINIMAL CORRECTION SET and is computed accordingly: one predicate call at S = K decides UNREACHED outright; a deletion-filtering descent returns a minimal failing set in at most |K| further calls, giving an upper bound; exhaustive shell certification then proves exactness up to a per-instance budget of B = 20,000 predicate calls. SENTINELS, declared in conventions.py BEFORE measurement: UNREACHED when validity survives S = K; CENSORED-EXACT carrying the bracket [j_certified + 1, |S_found|] when B binds; CENSORED-BUDGET when the 60 s wall binds; the certified depth j printed per instance as a first-class column. THE REFERENCE MEASURE INSIDE SHELL j, which does not exist anywhere in the project today: phi(j), the fraction of size-j retraction sets that fail, estimated from m = 384 uniform draws (1.96^2 * 0.25 / 0.05^2 = 384.2, the worst-case-p half-width-0.05 sample size), run on 100% of the primary source and 25% of the others. WHAT THIS RETIRES, and it is a gain the design should claim: moving from the covering-graph walk to exhaustive K-subset enumeration retires the open assumption chain Anti-Exchange Case B => Lemma R => Property S => Lemma L => Conjecture 2 => radius_local_up is exact. Exactness now comes from enumeration, not from a conjecture whose failure direction was radii too LARGE, i.e. optimistic about robustness. The retirement is stated with the old chain's direction recorded, because every previously committed radius still carries it. SHD is never used as a unit, no rank arithmetic is performed on the MPDAG poset, and the unit is named on every figure and in the manifest's RADIUS_CONVENTION string.
axes.justification: The MPDAG covering relation has no known graphical characterisation — stated three times in Taeb, Guo and Henckel — so neighbours cannot be enumerated and a poset walk cannot be defended; for |V| >= 4 the poset is not graded, so 'number of edges changed' is not a distance unit at all, and SHD provably over-certifies (SHD1 <= SHD2 <= d_L,pseudo, with an explicit example at d_L,pseudo = 1 and SHD = n-1). A knowledge-set metric sidesteps all of that, is the analyst's own unit, and is what the r_0 probe already computes in 0.02 to 0.04 s. B = 20,000 IS DERIVED FROM THE OBSERVED |K| DISTRIBUTION AND IT SITS AT A KNEE. Over the 831 admissible instances |K_G0| has median 10, mean 12.4 and maximum 122, with 28.6% above 16 and 14.4% above 24. Computing, per instance, the largest depth certifiable within B: at B = 5,000, 77.5% of instances reach depth >= 4; at B = 20,000, 90.9% do and 71.4% are exhausted outright (|K| <= 14, so 2^|K| <= B and UNREACHED becomes decidable); at B = 50,000, still 90.9% — the remaining tenth has |K| so large that no affordable budget reaches depth 4. Twenty thousand is therefore the point where more budget buys literally nothing, which is a derivation rather than a choice. That budget is well matched to where the radius mass sits: r <= 4 covers 98.1% of the 831 committed radii (508 at 1, 260 at 2, 43 at 3, 4 at 4), so the bracket is needed for a small minority. The shell measure answers the unmeasured slack: the existing calibration table puts conservativeness at 0.43 to 0.47, meaning roughly 44% of graphs outside the certified radius still admit Z, and BFS to the nearest failure says nothing about that. A guarantee that is right 100% of the time and tight 56% of the time is two numbers, not one.
axes.falsifiable_check: TWO CHECKS. (1) MONOTONICITY AUDIT: on a stratified sample of 5,000 instances, verify that failure at S implies failure at every S' containing S, by drawing supersets at random. With zero counterexamples the one-sided 95% upper bound on the violation rate is 3/5,000 = 0.06%. DECISION RULE: a single counterexample refutes Theorem 1 as implemented, invalidates the minimal-correction-set formulation and the descent that depends on it, and HALTS the protocol until it is resolved. It is not a warning. (2) PRIOR-ART CHECK, run BEFORE the differentiation paragraph is written and not after, because the ledger records that the stability-radius family (Sotskov and Emelichev), the radius of robust feasibility (Goberna, Jeyakumar, Li, Vicente-Perez), Renegar's distance to ill-posedness, minimal correction sets (Liffiton and Sakallah), AGM contraction and epistemic entrenchment, and multiverse / specification-curve analysis all return zero corpus hits and were never queried. Four specific unresolved reads block specific sentences and are scheduled in stage 0: Appendix F.3 of arXiv:2511.10625v3 (unretrieved in three passes, and the two readings of its section 6 conflict); the identity of arXiv:2010.08611 (two different titles across three passes); the Bang and Didelez citation conflict (arXiv:2306.01638 against arXiv:2503.21526); and arXiv:2503.09453, which the ledger names the single highest-value unread paper because if its expert-validated structures carry a reference independent of the expert, A6 changes from BUILD to CALIBRATE and this protocol's most expensive arm shrinks. DECISION RULE: if r is an instance of a named existing quantity — and 'the smallest subset of asserted constraints whose retraction breaks a property' is a minimal correction set by definition — the contribution is restated as the first instantiation of that quantity on the MPDAG background-knowledge lattice with a measured calibration, the naming is cited rather than claimed, and the MCS/MaxSAT solver literature is imported as tooling. An unrun prior-art search is worse than a conceded one.
axes.cost: At the polynomial gate's measured rate of 1.07 ms per call, a depth-4 certification at |K| = 12 is 794 calls = 0.85 s, and at |K| = 24 it is 12,951 calls = 13.9 s — which is why the wall cap is 60 s, giving better than 4x margin over the certified region so that anything hitting the cap is the extension-enumeration corner rather than the radius search. The shell measure at m = 384 draws over up to four shells is about 1.6 s per instance, so about 3 core-hours across the sweep. Agent-hours: about 24 for the minimal-correction-set search, the block and forbidden-edge moves, the shell sampler and the sentinel extensions. The prior-art search plus the four blocking reads is about 8 agent-hours and 8 human-hours, and it is the cheapest item on the whole board that could kill the framing.

axes.decision: TWO PANELS, and only one of them is a deployment arm. PANEL A, CPDAG computed from the true DAG, is a REFERENCE arm: its manifest field reads true_dag_on_path = TRUE-VIA-CPDAG, not FALSE, because an oracle C-hat is a true-DAG quantity on the computation path and the invariant admits the true DAG only to generate the sample and to audit. Panel A carries the geometry, the certification and the corpus-wide power; it may never be stated in a deployment sentence, and the forbidden form 'robust under an estimated CPDAG' stays forbidden for it. PANEL B, C-hat estimated at finite n by a CPDAG-EMITTING method only, is the deployment arm: PC with a declared CI test and alpha plus GES as a second estimator, on the grid n in {200, 1000, 5000, 20000} with 20 seed replicates per cell, up from the current 5. Discovery front-ends emitting a fully oriented DAG by skeleton-times-order factorisation are inadmissible: they commit to one topological order and destroy the undirected chain component the radius is defined on. The estimand and its standard error come from Sigma-hat alone through the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell form already implemented, the same formula serving population Sigma and sample Sigma-hat; the true DAG enters only to generate the sample by ancestral simulation and, post hoc, to audit. Var- and R^2-sortability are reported per Panel-B cell, because the simulation is exactly where the sortability leak enters and 'we standardised' is not a defence. SCOPE SENTENCE, printed and not buried: the certificate is a deterministic functional of (C-hat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n), not a post-discovery confidence interval, so the post-selection-inference results that invalidate naive two-step CIs constrain what may be said about the ESTIMATE and not about r; that boundary is stated rather than ignored. THE PROTOCOL OBJECT IS THE 95% BAND, NOT THE POINT HULL. THE GATE IS REPLACED, NOT WAITED ON: is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag leaves production entirely and survives only inside the certification differential. In production each candidate graph is decided by a pair of sound one-sided tests — first a FAILURE WITNESS, one consistent DAG extension constructed by Dor-Tarsi in polynomial time and tested by the back-door criterion, which PROVES failure when it fires; then is_gac_valid_mpdag, whose positive verdict is the VALIDITY CERTIFICATE. If neither resolves, the graph is CENSORED and the instance carries a bracket rather than a guess. Wherever extension enumeration remains (computing O(G0)), it is restricted to X's chain component, since pa_D(X) does not depend on the orientation of other components.
axes.justification: The band is forced by measurement, not preference: the point hull errs in the DANGEROUS direction 24.7% at n = 200 and still 18.1% at n = 20,000, while the 95% band errs at most 1.7% at every n, even though the band's raw agreement looks worse (7.8% against 57.0% on magic-irri at n = 200). A danger rate barely improving across a hundredfold increase in n says this is a coverage problem, not a sample-size problem, which is why the budget goes to replicates rather than to larger n. THE GATE ARITHMETIC IS THE WHOLE PROTOCOL. A depth-4 certification at the median |K| is 794 validity decisions on one instance. At the measured worst-case cost of 1,839.78 s per call that single instance takes 16.9 days, and the full sweep of roughly 12,000 arm-instances takes about 62 years; at the polynomial gate's 1.07 ms it is 0.85 s and about 19 minutes. That is not an optimisation, it is the difference between a protocol and a wish, and it is bought once. The substitution is licensed by measurement already in the tree — the GAC predicate was verdict-identical on 2,240 pairs with zero disagreements at 8.2x (20.22 s to 2.47 s), and Theorem 14 says back-door and GAC coincide on Z = O(.) — and the witness/certificate pair is what makes it SOUND rather than merely fast, since an implementation that over-declares invalidity under-estimates r, the safe direction. The component restriction is what turns 1,839.78 s on a 46-node network into the 0.02-0.04 s the r_0 probe already achieves on that same network; the ledger names it the highest-leverage change in the repo and says it needs a theorem plus a differential, so the differential runs first and the theorem is written against it. Panel A's relabelling is not pedantry: the current manifest carries the oracle-CI problem as a paragraph in assumption_status, and as a field it becomes an invariant the harness enforces.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE CERTIFICATION DIFFERENTIAL, and it gates everything else. It is TWO differentials plus a theorem, not one, because the exact reference is unaffordable in the regime where it matters most. D1, global enumeration against component-restricted enumeration, on 46,800 stratified comparisons matching the fast_gate precedent, stratified over u, the number of undirected edges in G0: 45,000 at u <= 12, 1,500 at u in 13-16, 300 at u in 17-20. D2, component-restricted enumeration against polynomial GAC, over the full range of u including the instances D1 cannot reach. Above u = 20 the global reference costs more than 57 s per comparison and the composed claim rests on the theorem alone; those instances carry GATE-EXTRAPOLATED in the primary table and are reported in their own stratum. DECISION RULE: accept the substitution if and only if (a) every disagreement is in the SAFE direction, meaning the cheap test declares failure where the enumeration says valid and therefore under-estimates r, and (b) the exact one-sided 95% upper bound on the disagreement rate clears the per-stratum bar. THE BAR IS PER STRATUM AND MUST BE STATED HONESTLY, because with zero disagreements the achievable bound is 3/45,000 = 0.0067% at u <= 12, 3/1,500 = 0.20% at u in 13-16 and 3/300 = 1.0% at u in 17-20: the substitution is certified below 0.1% only for u <= 12, at 0.2% to 16, at 1.0% to 20, and extrapolated above. Buying 0.1% in the top stratum would cost roughly 48 core-hours and is declined explicitly. If ANY disagreement appears in the DANGEROUS direction — cheap test says valid where the enumeration says invalid, inflating r — the protocol reverts to the enumerating predicate, the corpus is re-scoped to u <= 12, and the primary table shrinks accordingly. That fallback is declared now so it cannot be produced afterwards as a rescue. SECOND RULE: the substitution's predicted direction is stated before the differential runs and the disagreement rate published WITH ITS SIGN, because the author's last prediction of this shape — that fast_gate was strictly weaker — was measured to be exactly backwards (16 disagreements in 46,800, all one-directional, all strictly stricter).
axes.cost: Certification: at a per-extension cost of 5.5e-5 s (1,839.78 s over 2^25 extensions on ecoli70), D1's three strata cost 2.8 + 1.5 + 4.8 = 9.1 core-hours at each stratum's worst-case u and about 2.8 core-hours at each stratum's mean u; budget 10, expected 3. D2 is minutes. THE FINITE-N ARM IS WHERE SCOPE IS CUT AND THE CUT IS STATED: 17 of the current 39 networks have |V| <= 60 and a chain component of size >= 3, which is the eligibility rule, and PC runs on all 17 at 4 sample sizes x 20 seeds = 1,360 runs, budgeted at a measured mean of 80 s = 30 core-hours; GES runs on 6 of the 17 at 2 sample sizes x 20 seeds = 240 runs at about 240 s = 16 core-hours. Total 46 core-hours with a 1,800 s per-run cap and censoring recorded. The consequence is printed rather than discovered: the deployment panel covers 17 networks against the reference panel's 112, so NO finite-n statement may be made over the corpus — Panel B is a per-network panel and says so. The deployment radius sweep is about 12,000 arm-instances at a budgeted 3 s mean under a 60 s cap, roughly 10 to 20 core-hours, and its true cost is unknown until stage 0 measures the u_G0 distribution under elicited K, because all 831 committed instances have u = 0. The ER instrument arm is about 1.5 core-hours. Agent-hours: about 32, most of it the witness construction and the two differential harnesses.

axes.decision: Build the referent; do not cite one, because none exists. Four pre-registered tests, two calibration statistics, two comparators, and a dispersion rule that applies to every number the protocol prints. A6-1 DISCRIMINATOR: per network build K twice, once from the generator under test and once from the referent, apply the SAME Meek consistency filter to both, and permutation-test the seven-feature vector (coverage per granularity, distance-from-X distribution, separate false-assertion and false-omission rates, pairwise distance among wrong assertions, Meek rejection rate, cascade size, cycles before repair). A6-2 RADIUS TRANSFER, the one with teeth because the reported quantity is r and not K: hold the instance set fixed to the COMMON SUPPORT and the |K| stratum fixed, and compare full radius distributions on the pre-declared summary (share at r = 1, median, max, agreement rate with r_val <= min(s, |K_G0|)), with the tolerance pre-registered BEFORE the referent is looked at and the SIGN reported, since a generator producing systematically larger radii is optimistic about robustness. A6-3 POSITIVE CONTROL on the degree-matched ER instrument arm, because on the current unmatched arm a rejection would be uninterpretable. A6-4 CONTAMINATION SCREEN: named names, scrambled names, and a cold-recall probe with no data, across at least two models — the second model is a contamination instrument and never a judge of correctness — on a 40-network stratified subsample, plus a genuinely clean stratum of networks whose source publication post-dates the model cutoff, constructible because bnRep carries publication years. TWO CALIBRATION STATISTICS, because the prior draft borrowed one definition for two different questions. A-CAL-1, THE GUARANTEE TEST, which is what the framework actually promises: reveal the truth, let W be the set of assertions in K that are false, and bucket each instance as DANGEROUS if |W| <= r-1 and Z is invalid in the true DAG (the certificate covered this error level and the set is wrong anyway), HELD if |W| <= r-1 and Z is valid, SAFE if |W| >= r and Z is invalid (the certificate correctly declined to cover it), and SLACK if |W| >= r and Z is valid. A-CAL-2, THE ESTIMATION TEST, the ledger's existing three buckets EQUAL / SAFE (radius smaller than the reference) / DANGEROUS (radius larger), comparing Panel B's r against Panel A's on the same instances. The pre-registered 5% ceiling attaches to A-CAL-1's DANGEROUS for the knowledge arms and to A-CAL-2's for the finite-n arm; they are different tests and are never averaged. COMPARATORS: for every instance, whether the RoCA over-identification test would have fired and whether it had power at all (two or more valid sets); and H4, the naive |K|-count baseline a practitioner would actually use, pre-registered and unrun for six sessions, scored by whether r adds anything over |K| in predicting the DANGEROUS bucket. DECISION RELEVANCE: the realised absolute bias of the adjusted effect at G0 against the true DAG, reported conditional on r — measurable with no invented loss function — as the primary answer to 'does the certificate buy anything', with EVPPI per asserted constraint as a secondary under a declared squared-bias loss. DISPERSION RULE: every headline fraction carries a network-clustered bootstrap 95% interval computed on n_eff and not on N, plus the between-seed component for Panel B and the between-replicate component for the LLM source; a bare fraction is not a permitted output anywhere in this protocol.
axes.justification: No published study measures a domain expert's per-edge error rate, separating omission from commission, on expert-specified causal DAGs scored against a known-true DAG; this survived a 1,100-note corpus grep, a seven-dimension web sweep and a gap-fill that exhausted a 200-call budget and hit HTTP 403 at the four journals where such a measurement would live. So the referent is built here. Splitting the calibration in two is forced by what the buckets mean: the ledger's three-bucket precedent comes from the r_0 band study, where DANGEROUS means an estimated radius exceeding an oracle radius, which is a finite-sample question; the question this framework exists to answer is whether the promise 'you may be wrong about up to r-1 claims' survives the truth being revealed, and that has no definition in the existing convention. The n_eff denominator is forced by the recomputed rho_hat: an interval computed on N = 831 would claim a precision the data does not have, and the same 61.1% carries a 12.3-point half-width on n_eff = 60.1 against a 3.3-point one on N. The three-bucket form is forced because agreement hides the sign and the sign is the whole guarantee — the same measurement that chose the band over the point hull. The RoCA comparator is forced by the licensed narrow claim form: graph-knowledge errors are NOT globally untestable, and the class the radius prices is the class of orientation errors that keeps all valid adjustment sets valid, which consistency checks cannot see; the honest way to hold that line is to report, instance by instance, where the incumbent fires and where it does not. H4 is forced because the radius has never once been compared with counting your own claims, and a referee will ask. The realised-bias leg is forced by our own CSCD rejection, where both reviewers read epistemic restraint as a ceiling rather than a strength.
axes.falsifiable_check: THE CALIBRATION CEILING, pre-registered at 5% DANGEROUS on A-CAL-1, and the ceiling itself is derived rather than chosen. Exact one-sided 95% upper bounds at an observed rate matching the band precedent of 1.7% are: 7.66% at n_eff = 60, 6.16% at 100, 5.09% at 150, 3.83% at 200, 3.62% at 250, 3.26% at 400. So any ceiling below 3.7% is unattainable at the design n_eff and could never be SUPPORTED, and any ceiling above 18.1% would be weaker than the point-hull instrument this project already rejected; 5% is the round value just above the attainable floor and far below the rejected instrument, and the whole interval that makes it meaningful is printed. THREE OUTCOMES, declared in advance so none can be relabelled: at n_eff = 250 an observed 1.7% gives an upper bound of 3.62% and the certificate is SUPPORTED; REFUTATION requires the one-sided 95% LOWER bound to exceed 5%, which at n_eff = 250 means 19 or more DANGEROUS instances (7.6%); anything between is UNDETERMINED with the interval printed. Note the arithmetic that makes n_eff the whole question: at n_eff = 150 the same observed 1.7% gives 5.09% and clears nothing, and the current 25-network corpus cannot exceed n_eff = 62.8. SECOND RULE, contamination: if a network's named-minus-scrambled accuracy gap exceeds its pre-registered threshold AND cold recall reproduces the published adjacency above chance, that network moves to a separately reported memorisation stratum and never enters a pooled row — on the verified precedent that pooling a designed family with random ones moved a headline by 14 points (79.6% to 65.3%). THIRD RULE, on the audit's own honesty: the named-minus-scrambled gap BOUNDS memorisation from above and domain knowledge from below and does not separate them, because scrambling destroys exactly the semantics the surrogate is supposed to supply; so the post-cutoff stratum, not the scrambling, carries any clean claim, and if that stratum is empty the surrogate's accuracy is reported as uninterpretable rather than as a measurement. FOURTH RULE, on H4: if |K_G0| alone predicts the DANGEROUS bucket as well as r does, the radius has not earned its compute and that is written in the abstract, not the appendix.
axes.cost: Audit compute is negligible — it scores rows already computed — except the contamination elicitation at about 6,400 model calls, and the realised-bias leg, which needs the adjusted effect computed at both G0 and the true DAG on every instance and adds about 2 core-hours. Agent-hours: about 28 for the four tests, the two calibration statistics, the clustered bootstrap, the RoCA comparator harness and the EVPPI computation. Human-hours: about 18, spent on the three things no tool can do — writing the A6-2 tolerance before the referent is looked at, adjudicating the harvest audit sample, and the four blocking prior-art reads. This axis is where the human-hours concentrate and that is the correct place for them.

arms: D-LLM (deployment, LLM-surrogate K, R=3 elicitation replicates). FIXED: the common-support instance set, the panel, the estimator, the gate tier, the per-network cap of 12, the seeds. VARIES: nothing but the knowledge source; across replicates, only the variable-presentation order, which is both the dispersion mechanism and the mention-order-bias measurement. This is the arm the framework is actually about, and it is the only one whose radius may be called an analyst's radius.

D-PUB (deployment, K harvested from each network's source publication). FIXED: identical to D-LLM, on the same common-support triples. VARIES: the knowledge source only. Expected thin — exactly one of the 12 dagitty files yields a published author's own adjustment set, and only 2 of 12 carry any adjusted node at all — so it is powered as a descriptive stratum, not as a two-sample referent, and that limit is printed rather than discovered.

D-NULL (deployment, K empty). FIXED: the instance set. VARIES: K is vacuous. Reports identification status and effect-set width at C-hat, not a radius. Its job is to make 'the radius is large' distinguishable from 'the knowledge was vacuous'.

D-RANDOM (deployment, labelled negative control: |K| matched per instance to D-LLM's realised |K|, orientations drawn uniformly from the orientable edges of X's chain component with no reference to truth, redrawn on Meek FAIL). FIXED: the instance set and |K|. VARIES: only whether the assertions carry information. This is the floor a coin-flip expert produces and it is what makes any D-LLM result a measurement rather than a hope; it also supplies the null against which the error-correlation permutation test is itself validated.

D-ORACLE-SUBSET (stipulated true-but-incomplete K, the taxonomy's MISSING arm). FIXED: the instance set and the computation path. VARIES: K is stipulated from the truth and LABELLED as stipulated. It is the control every false arm is read against, it may never be pooled with D-LLM or D-PUB in a printed row, and — critically — it does not participate in defining the common support, because if it did the truth would shape the deployment population.

D-LEGACY (knowledge_to_recover at coverage 1.0 / 0.5 / 0.25). FIXED: the new observables-only frame, the new gate, and a fixed instance set, so the composition effect that produced the 543/182/106 collapse and the falling 69.8/51.1/34.0 r=1 share cannot recur. VARIES: coverage only. Retained solely to reproduce the committed numbers under the redesign and to serve as the audit-arm scoring yardstick.

D-TIERED (correlated-error reference: the existing tiered-misfiling operator in synth/knowledge.py, which misfiles a node into a wrong temporal tier before reading off assertions so one mistake flips several claims at once). FIXED: the instance set. VARIES: the error correlation structure. Oracle-derived and therefore labelled stipulated. It exists because only uniform random reversal has ever been run on real graphs, and the module's own docstring calls the correlated case the realistic one.

A-CAL-1 (guarantee audit over every deployment arm). FIXED: everything the deployment arms computed. VARIES: the truth is revealed, for scoring only. Output: HELD / SLACK / SAFE / DANGEROUS shares with an exact one-sided Clopper-Pearson bound on DANGEROUS computed on n_eff, per tier, never pooled across tiers.

A-CAL-2 (estimation audit, Panel B against Panel A on the same instances). FIXED: the instances and the knowledge source. VARIES: whether C-hat and Sigma are oracle or estimated at finite n. Output: the ledger's EQUAL / SAFE / DANGEROUS buckets and the danger-rate curve for the band against the point hull.

A-ERR (knowledge-error decomposition over D-LLM, D-PUB, D-RANDOM, D-ORACLE-SUBSET, D-TIERED). FIXED: the elicited K, frozen before any radius. VARIES: nothing; this arm only measures. Output: omission, commission and reversal separately, per granularity, per network, as a function of graph distance from X, and split by data-compelled versus orientable edge type. This is the referent the project must build and the most load-bearing unmeasured quantity on the board, because the radius equals that distance.

A-CONTAM (contamination screen over D-LLM). FIXED: the networks and the prompt template. VARIES: named names / scrambled names / cold recall, across two models, plus a post-cutoff clean stratum. Output: a per-network memorisation flag that routes networks into a separate stratum.

A-INCUMBENT (RoCA comparator over every deployment instance). FIXED: the instance and the data. VARIES: the instrument — pricing against testing. Output: for every instance where r fires, whether the over-identification test would have fired, and on how many instances it had power at all.

A-BASELINE (H4, the naive |K|-count baseline). FIXED: the instances. VARIES: the statistic — r against |K_G0|. Output: whether r adds anything over counting your own claims in predicting the DANGEROUS bucket. Pre-registered for six sessions and never run.

C-PREDICATE (certification differential, and it runs first). FIXED: the instances. VARIES: the validity predicate only — D1 compares global enumeration against component-restricted enumeration on 46,800 comparisons stratified over u; D2 compares component-restricted enumeration against polynomial GAC across the full range of u. This arm gates the entire protocol.

C-MONO (monotonicity audit). FIXED: the instances. VARIES: the retraction set, drawn as random supersets of a known failing set. Output: a violation rate whose one-sided 95% upper bound is 0.06% at zero counterexamples; a single counterexample halts the protocol.

C-ER (instrument calibration, degree-matched Erdos-Renyi). FIXED: the pipeline, the knowledge source, the gate, the cap, with seeds recorded. VARIES: the generator and the expected degree across the corpus's measured band 1.60 to 9.86. NOT a substrate tier — Decision 2 declined those — it exists solely so the A6-3 positive control has power, and it is labelled that way in every caption.

S-FINITE (Panel B, the only deployment statistical arm). FIXED: the networks (the 17 eligible at |V| <= 60 with a chain component of size >= 3), the K frozen from D-LLM, the estimator formula, the parameterisation. VARIES: n in {200, 1000, 5000, 20000}, 20 seed replicates, and the discovery method (PC on all 17, GES on 6). Output: the two-panel table, the danger-rate curve, and the per-cell sortability profile.
primary_table: TITLE: Certificate behaviour by knowledge source, on the common support, at matched |K|. A ROW is one (knowledge source x substrate tier) cell evaluated on the COMMON SUPPORT — the instances where every observable source yields a Meek-consistent K — so every row differs from every other in exactly one declared thing and no row is computed on a population its own source selected. Rows: five knowledge sources carrying radii (LLM surrogate, harvested publication, random-consistent negative control, oracle-true-subset control, oracle-cascade legacy) crossed with three substrate tiers, plus one NULL row per tier and one Erdos-Renyi instrument row labelled as instrument calibration and never as substrate: nineteen declared cells. A cell with fewer than 8 yielding networks is printed as raw counts with NO interval, because at k = 8 the network-clustered half-width on a mid proportion exceeds 20 points and an interval that wide would be read as a measurement. COLUMNS, in twelve groups: (1) k networks / N instances / n_eff, always printed as a triple, because a fraction without n_eff is the defect this protocol exists to fix; (2) |K_G0| median and IQR, printed BEFORE any radius column, because r <= |K| by construction and a radius comparison at unmatched |K| is a comparison of how much was asserted; (3) share with r_val = 1, network-weighted as the headline with the pair-weighted value beside it, both with a network-clustered bootstrap 95% interval and, for D-LLM, the between-replicate component printed separately; (4) median r_val with IQR, plus the share carrying CENSORED-EXACT with its bracket and the share carrying CENSORED-BUDGET; (5) the certified depth distribution, since exactness is now a per-instance property and not a global claim; (6) share with r_val = UNREACHED, meaning validity survives retracting all of K; (7) phi(1), the fraction of single retractions that fail, with its interval — the shell reference measure that quantifies the certificate's slack against the measured 0.43-0.47 conservativeness; (8) A-CAL-1 buckets HELD / SLACK / SAFE / DANGEROUS with the exact one-sided 95% upper bound on DANGEROUS computed on n_eff; (9) knowledge error — omission / commission / reversal, per granularity, from A-ERR, on the same denominator as b-LOAD's rho and CSCD's 0.3; (10) share of instances on which the RoCA test would have fired and the share on which it had power at all; (11) mean absolute realised bias of the adjusted effect, conditional on r; (12) two printed booleans, true_dag_on_path and gate_certification_class (CERTIFIED-0.1%, CERTIFIED-1%, or EXTRAPOLATED), both machine-checked rather than asserted. WHAT A ROW MEANS: for this knowledge source on this substrate tier, across k independent networks and at a stated level of asserted knowledge, here is how many claims an analyst can withdraw before the adjustment set stops being valid, how often the promise failed once the truth was revealed, how much slack sits just outside the certified region, how much the estimate actually moved, and whether the test that already exists would have caught the same errors. Every row is a Panel A row; the Panel B companion table repeats columns (3), (4), (8) and (11) over the 17 eligible networks, and no sentence about deployment behaviour is written from the Panel A table alone.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_r: Five things, each a column rather than a sentence. (1) On elicited knowledge, not oracle knowledge, A-CAL-1's DANGEROUS bucket has a one-sided 95% upper bound below the 5% ceiling at n_eff >= 200 — the promise 'you may be wrong about up to r-1 of your claims' survives the truth being revealed, under knowledge an analyst actually has rather than knowledge read off the answer. (2) The radius distribution is non-degenerate: substantial mass at r >= 2 with intervals excluding a degenerate all-ones distribution, so the certificate discriminates between instances instead of restating that knowledge is load-bearing. (3) At MATCHED |K|, the radius under elicited K is at least as large as under the oracle-true-subset arm — the direction the repository's own wrong-knowledge sweep predicts, since the r=1 share falls 57.8% to 42.1% as wrongness rises — and the DANGEROUS rate nonetheless stays under the ceiling. That combination is the framework's actual claim: wrong knowledge inflates the radius, and the certificate still holds. If instead the radius were smaller under elicited K, the cascade-greed bias in knowledge_to_recover would be dominating and the finding would be about |K|, not about correctness. (4) D-LLM separates cleanly from D-RANDOM at matched |K| — a coin-flip expert does not reproduce the surrogate's radius distribution — which is the only thing that makes the surrogate arm a measurement of knowledge rather than of cardinality. (5) On the instances where r = 1, RoCA fires on a minority, so pricing covers a class that testing provably cannot see, which is the narrow claim the ledger licenses and the only one that survives Su and Henckel. Secondarily, A6-1 fails to reject the surrogate against the harvested-publication referent on the seven-feature vector after both pass the same Meek filter, which is the only available evidence that the simulated knowledge distribution resembles a real one, and H4 shows r predicting the DANGEROUS bucket better than |K_G0| alone.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_w: Seven concrete, pre-registered ways this table kills the framework. (1) THE GUARANTEE FAILS: A-CAL-1's DANGEROUS one-sided 95% LOWER bound exceeds 5% — at n_eff = 250 that is 19 or more instances where the analyst was wrong about fewer than r claims and the adjustment set was invalid anyway. The certificate is then not a guarantee under elicited knowledge, and the framework's central sentence is gone. (2) THE CERTIFICATE IS VACUOUS: r = 1 on more than 90% of instances under elicited K with the interval excluding lower values, so the answer is always 'one withdrawn claim kills you' and carries no information a coverage count would not. (3) THE RADIUS IS A CARDINALITY: the D-LLM / D-RANDOM gap vanishes at matched |K|, or |K_G0| predicts the DANGEROUS bucket as well as r does under H4. Then the radius is measuring how many things were asserted, not whether they were right, and every headline must be restated in those terms. (4) INCUMBENT DOMINATES: RoCA fires on most instances where r is small, and the class the radius prices turns out to be mostly detectable by an existing test with released code. (5) THE SURROGATE IS RECITING: A6-4 shows the named-minus-scrambled gap above threshold AND cold recall reproducing published adjacency above chance across the benchmark tier, with the post-cutoff clean stratum too small to rescue it — then the LLM arm measures memorisation of ASIA, ALARM, CHILD, INSURANCE and SACHS, not expertise, and the knowledge model has no referent at all. (6) THE GATE SUBSTITUTION IS UNSOUND: D1 or D2 finds any DANGEROUS-direction disagreement, in which case the protocol reverts to the enumerating predicate, the corpus is re-scoped to u <= 12, and the framework becomes a claim about small chain components; or, more quietly, the stage-0 pilot finds that elicited K puts most instances above u = 20, where the substitution is only extrapolated and the primary table's certification column reads EXTRAPOLATED on the majority of rows. (7) THE EMPIRICS CANNOT BE STATED AT ALL: after exhausting bnRep and the dagitty repository, k_yield stays below about 41 networks, at which point the network-clustered half-width on the r=1 share remains above 10 points and no population sentence may be written. That outcome is not hypothetical — it is where the project stands today, with k = 25, n_eff = 60.1 and a half-width of 12.3 points on the committed 61.1%, a fact that every bare fraction currently in circulation conceals.
known_weaknesses: THE POWER ARITHMETIC IS ESTIMATED FROM DATA THIS PROTOCOL DELETES. rho_hat = 0.398 and 0.458 come from a corpus generated by the oracle knowledge model that A3 removes. Under elicited K it may move in either direction, and k*, the cap, and every n_eff in the schedule move with it. Stage 0 re-estimates it on the 25 current yielding networks and recomputes the acquisition target, but the headline arithmetic is provisional until that pilot lands.

THE COMPUTE ESTIMATE FOR THE DEPLOYMENT SWEEP IS THE WEAKEST NUMBER IN THE BUDGET. All 831 committed admissible instances have g0_undirected_edges = 0, so every timing in the repository (7.16 s total, 0.158 s slowest) was measured on fully oriented centres and says nothing about what a partial elicited K costs. The sweep is budgeted at 10 to 20 core-hours on an assumed 3 s mean with a 60 s cap, and if the u distribution under elicited K is heavy the caps bind and the primary table fills with CENSORED-BUDGET rather than radii. Stage 0 measures this before the budget is committed, which converts the risk from a cost overrun into a scope decision, but it does not remove it.

THE GATE IS CERTIFIED WHERE IT IS CHEAP AND EXTRAPOLATED WHERE IT MATTERS. With zero disagreements the achievable per-stratum bounds are 0.0067% at u <= 12, 0.20% at 13-16 and 1.0% at 17-20, and above u = 20 the global reference costs more than 57 s per comparison so the composed claim rests on the component-restriction theorem alone. Buying a 0.1% bound in the top stratum would cost about 48 core-hours and is declined explicitly. A referee entitled to ask about the regime where the enumeration is most expensive and most likely to differ will find a 1% bound and an extrapolation.

A COVERAGE-FIRST LENS WOULD KEEP ALL 831 INSTANCES. The cap at 12 discards 70% of them and, contrary to what a power argument would like, this LOWERS n_eff from 60.1 to 54.4. The cap is justified on marginal information (0.222 units of n_eff per instance below the cap against 0.021 for the 13th through 20th) and on stopping barley's 189 instances from setting a pair-weighted headline, not on precision. A referee who counts rows will see a smaller table than the one already committed and the n_eff column is the only thing defending it.

A REALISM-FIRST LENS WOULD SPEND THE BUDGET HARVESTING APPLIED-PAPER KNOWLEDGE. That is the only genuinely human knowledge available, and D-PUB is the arm the whole realism argument would rest on. It is powered descriptively only, because exactly one of twelve dagitty files yields a published author's own adjustment set and only two carry any adjusted node. The budget goes to network breadth instead because n_eff <= k/rho binds everything. If the harvested arm is the scientifically important one, this allocation is wrong.

A THEORY-FIRST LENS WOULD DEMAND THE COMPONENT-RESTRICTION THEOREM BEFORE ANYTHING RUNS. The differential runs first and the theorem is written against it, accepting that 46,800 stratified comparisons are evidence and not a proof.

A NOVELTY-FIRST LENS WOULD NOT NAME r AS A MINIMUM MINIMAL-CORRECTION-SET CARDINALITY, since that hands a reviewer the MUS/MCS objection. It is named deliberately: the naming buys a solver and closes an unrun search. If the prior-art pass shows r is a known quantity under another name, the contribution shrinks to the instantiation plus the calibration, and this protocol will have made that shrinkage happen in stage 0 rather than in review. Four blocking reads sit on that path and three of them failed retrieval in every previous pass.

THE FOUR-BUCKET GUARANTEE TEST IS NEW AND UNVALIDATED. A-CAL-1 defines DANGEROUS as |W| <= r-1 with Z invalid in the true DAG, where W is the set of false assertions. That definition is mine, it makes a tier's falsity count as one claim to keep units consistent with block retraction, and no precedent scores a breakdown radius this way. If the definition is wrong the ceiling test is measuring the wrong event, and nothing in the protocol would catch that.

bnRep IS LOAD-BEARING AND UNVERIFIED BY ME. I have not checked its licence, its parse yield to DAGs, or how many of its networks produce a chain component of size >= 2. Only 25 of 39 current networks yielded any instance and 33 of 39 have a component at all, so k* = 112 needs roughly 140 to 175 acquired networks at the observed yield. If the yield is materially lower, k* is unreachable and the honest response is the stopping rule's narrowing, which is a worse outcome than the one designed for.

THE CONTAMINATION SCREEN IS CUT TO 40 NETWORKS ACROSS TWO MODELS on cost grounds, and the memorisation flag routes networks out of pooled rows.
