A subsampled screen means some contaminated networks stay pooled, and the routing decision the flag feeds is exactly the one that moved a headline 14 points in the ER precedent.

THE LATENT STRATUM IS DESCRIPTIVE ONLY, AND THAT IS A DECLARED CUT RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. Recovering M-bias as an ADMG opens a modality — PAGs, bidirected edges, latent confounding — for which the retraction operator, the GAC predicate and the sentinels are all undefined. It is the framework's motivating structure, so dropping it entirely is worse, but no radius is computed on it and the gap is visible in the table.

EVPPI NEEDS A LOSS FUNCTION THE PROJECT HAS NOT WRITTEN. Squared bias of the adjusted effect is specified without arguing it is the loss anyone faces. The realised-absolute-bias leg is the primary decision-relevant quantity precisely because it needs no such choice, but a decision-analysis lens would say the loss determines the answer and deserves its own justification.

DROPPING r_eps AND r_0 FROM THE PRIMARY TABLE FORECLOSES THE MIDDLE-REGIME QUESTION. Session 5 found 0.0% at all six epsilon thresholds across 560 instances with mean absolute bias exactly 0 at G0, so r_eps is collected wherever theta is computed and reported in an appendix; r_0 is out unless its three collapsed infinite cases (no zero in the hull, hull undefined, extension cap hit) are given distinct sentinels first. A modelling-first lens would fund a dedicated search for the regime.

THE PROTOCOL CAN END IN UNDETERMINED, BY DESIGN. Stage 0 pilots and re-estimates rho; stage 1 acquires until k_yield >= 112 or the sources are exhausted; stage 2 runs the sweep only after C-PREDICATE clears; stage 3 stops when the DANGEROUS bound resolves either way. A lens optimising for a shippable result would not build in a third outcome that produces no headline. The vault also records an ICLR 2027 abstract around 18 September and a race with the Guo/Henckel group; this protocol is eight to twelve weeks and the brief fixes no deadline pressure, so a schedule-first lens would ship a narrow descriptive result on the 25 networks now and treat the corpus expansion as a journal extension.
total_budget: WALL-CLOCK: eight to twelve weeks at Ze's cadence, dominated by corpus acquisition and by the three human decision points (fixing the A6-2 tolerance before the referent is looked at, adjudicating the harvest audit, and the four blocking prior-art reads), not by machine time. ORDERING IS FORCED: stage 0 (pilot: re-estimate rho on the current 25 networks, measure the u_G0 distribution under elicited K, run the prior-art search and the four blocking reads) -> C-PREDICATE and C-MONO, because nothing may run on the cheap gate until they clear -> acquisition and the descriptive table -> the deployment sweep -> S-FINITE -> the audit. COMPUTE: about 86 core-hours, budget 100, which is under 13 hours of wall time at eight-way parallelism on betelgeuse — roughly 46 for the finite-n arm (1,360 PC runs on the 17 eligible networks plus 240 GES runs on 6, under an 1,800 s per-run cap), 10 budgeted for the two gate differentials (expected 3, worst case 9.1), 10 to 20 for the whole deployment radius sweep, 3 for the shell reference measure, 3 for the stage-0 pilot, 1.5 for the Erdos-Renyi instrument arm and 2 for the audit's realised-bias leg. THE COMPUTE WALL THAT SHAPED EVERY PREVIOUS SESSION IS BOUGHT OUT ONCE AND THE ARITHMETIC IS THE ARGUMENT: a single depth-4 certification at the median |K| is 794 validity decisions, which at the measured 1,839.78 s per call is 16.9 days for ONE instance and about 62 years for the sweep, against 0.85 s per instance and about 19 minutes for the sweep at the polynomial gate's 1.07 ms. Any protocol that calls the exact gate once per graph in a ball is not a protocol; this one pays about 10 core-hours to certify the cheap gate against the exact one, in the safe direction only, and then never calls the exact one again. MODEL CALLS: about 34,500, derived from the committed structure (276 chain components, 767 undirected edges and 969 nodes-in-components over 39 networks, so 65.6 queries per network-replicate) at 112 networks x 3 replicates, plus a 12-network x 10-replicate dispersion subsample, plus 2 models x 3 conditions x 40 networks for contamination, plus the harvest extraction. AGENT-HOURS: about 150 to 190, concentrated in elicit.py, taxonomy.py, the random-consistent sampler and the harvester built out of their 31 NotImplementedError bodies (~45), the certification harness, failure witness and two differentials (~32), the audit tests, clustered bootstrap, RoCA comparator and bias leg (~28), the minimal-correction-set search, block and forbidden-edge moves, shell sampler and sentinels (~24), the bnRep ingester, sortability probes and canonical numbers file (~14), the frame rewrite and common-support machinery (~12), and the AST invariant guard and CI (~8). HUMAN-HOURS: about 38, of which ~12 is the extraction audit (60 verified records per tier at ~4 minutes bounds extraction error at 4.87% with zero errors), ~12 is the pre-registration and tolerance setting, ~8 the four blocking reads, and ~6 the decision checkpoints. WHAT WAS CUT, EXPLICITLY: the finite-n arm covers 17 networks rather than the corpus, so no finite-n statement may be made over the corpus and the table says so; GES runs on 6 of those 17 and at 2 of the 4 sample sizes; the gate differential's top stratum is bounded at 1.0% rather than 0.1% because 0.1% there costs about 48 core-hours; the contamination screen covers 40 networks; the latent ADMG stratum is descriptive with no radius; r_0 is out of the table and r_eps is an appendix. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT COMPUTE AND IT IS NOT MODEL CALLS. It is k, the number of independent yielding networks, because n_eff <= k/rho with rho recomputed at 0.398: the current 25 yielding networks cap the effective sample at 62.8 and already sit at 60.1, so the corpus is saturated and no amount of further pair sampling can move it; n_eff = 200 is the minimum at which the 5% DANGEROUS ceiling is resolvable at all, n_eff = 250 is the design point, and at the derived cap of 12 that needs 112 yielding networks, which at the observed yield needs roughly 140 to 175 acquired ones.

arms: ARM 0 — BRIDGE STRATUM. New, and it is the arm that makes every circulating number usable again. VERIFIED PREREQUISITE: the 543 distinct (X,Y) pairs admissible under today's true-DAG gate are a STRICT SUBSET of the 5,045 pairs the observables-only frame admits (recomputed 2026-09-11: |old \ new| = 0). FIXED: those 543 pairs, the oracle K from knowledge_to_recover at the three legacy coverage levels, the polynomial GAC gate. VARIES: only the filter set (legacy five-true-DAG-filter gate versus the observables-only set) and the extension scope (global versus dependency-closed). EMITS: side-by-side r distributions, so report_real_graphs.md's 61.1% r=1, the 45.4/35.6 separation pair, the 72.8% law agreement and the 831-instance denominator each get a recomputed twin inside the new pipeline. Every legacy number is quoted ONLY here and ONLY with its twin beside it. Without this arm the redesign silently orphans six committed reports.

ARM 1 — DEPLOYMENT. FIXED: the frozen hashed 424-question questionnaire; the observables-only filter set (treatment_not_in_or_adjacent_to_component, knowledge_inconsistent, o_g0_not_identified, z_invalid_at_g0, o_g0_extensions_intractable-at-cap-17, plus Y in possde(X, G0)); the polynomial GAC predicate is_gac_valid_mpdag; the dependency-closed extension scope; the centre Meek(Chat, K); the FWL estimator; the sentinel conventions extended to UNREACHED, NOT-REACHED and the three r_0 infinities; and a harness assertion that every emitted row carries true_dag_on_path=false. VARIES: which answerer supplies K, which substrate tier, oracle versus finite-n CPDAG. EMITS: r (including UNREACHED, now possible for the first time), phi(j), K's full feature vector, the consistent-but-false fraction, and every provenance field. Reads no true-DAG quantity on the computation path — which the questionnaire's own scope did not satisfy in the draft.

ARM 2 — POST-HOC AUDIT. FIXED: the instance set and the K objects, frozen by Arm 1 before any truth is revealed. VARIES: nothing; the truth is revealed once and used only to score. EMITS: per-assertion omission, commission and reversal scored against knowledge_to_recover's recovering set; the three-bucket certificate scoring (equal / SAFE = radius smaller than truth / DANGEROUS = radius larger than truth), never an agreement rate; the stated-confidence calibration curve that GATES whether the deployment arm may read confidence at all; whether the instance would have been called degenerate under the three deleted true-DAG filters; and whether the RoCA chi-squared test would have fired on it.

ARM 3 — R1 PUBLISHED-AUTHOR referent (inside Arm 1). FIXED: the questionnaire, the response grammar, the Meek consistency filter, Tier A only — 8 applied networks, 41 load-bearing questions, 595 candidate (X,Y) pairs under the observables-only frame (verified per network: Acid 52/1, Didelez 27/3, Kampen 85/11, Polzer 101/9, Schipf 30/6, Sebastiani 228/7, Shrier 49/3, Thoemmes 23/1 as pairs/questions). VARIES: the source paper, and the coder (2 independent, blind to the DAG file). EMITS: K plus pre-adjudication Cohen's kappa. SCOPE, printed not implied: on this tier truth is the published author's own diagram, so the score is disagreement with an author, never error against a true DAG.

ARM 4 — R2 HUMAN ANALYST referent (inside Arm 1). FIXED: the 82-question domain-legible subset (the 8 applied networks' 41 questions plus asia 3, child 12, hepar2 9, sachs 17), triplet query form, no feedback, no revision, no sight of any computed radius, sitting capped at 100 minutes with unanswered items recorded NOT-REACHED (a status distinct from DECLINE). VARIES: the analyst — recruit to 5, floor 3, stopping rule derived from the Wilson curve below. EMITS: K, per-assertion confidence, per-question seconds (the first elicitation-cost-per-edge number anywhere, since the ledger records none exists), and per-analyst commission/omission rates at ±0.097 pooling to ±0.044 at five analysts.

ARM 5 — R3 LLM SURROGATE, named condition (inside Arm 1). FIXED: all 424 questions plus the compelled-edge control block, one pass, temperature 0, cached, K frozen before r is computed. VARIES: the model (>=2, required by the contamination-flagging method) and the PROMPT VARIANT (2 per condition, mention order randomised under a stored seed), so prompt-induced variance is measured rather than assumed away. This is the deployment arm's primary knowledge source and the thing under test.

ARM 6 — R3 SURROGATE, scrambled-names condition. FIXED: everything in Arm 5 except the variable names, permuted under a stored seed. VARIES: names only. Its gap against Arm 5 BOUNDS memorisation from above and domain knowledge from below and is reported as a bound, never as a decomposition. Doubles as the ONLY answerer that can be run on the matched-ER control (Arm 12), since a synthetic graph has no names to know.

ARM 7 — R3 SURROGATE, cold-recall probe. FIXED: the network name alone, no data, no glossary, no questionnaire. VARIES: the network. EMITS: whether the published adjacency is reproduced above chance. With Arm 6 it stratifies every network as plausibly-in-pretraining or not; strata reported separately and never pooled, on the verified precedent that pooling a designed family with random ones moved a headline from 79.6% to 65.3%.

ARM 8 — G-ORACLE, the incumbent. FIXED: knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag). VARIES: coverage in {1.0, 0.5, 0.25}. Retained ONLY as a labelled arm to be judged, flagged true_dag_on_path=true so it can never be mistaken for a deployment number, and used in Arm 2 as the scoring yardstick. Its coverage sweep is quoted only inside Arm 0's bridge stratum, because the corpus-wide 105-pair three-stratum intersection collapses to 16 pairs on the applied tier (verified) and 16 is not a comparison.

ARM 9 — G-FLIP. FIXED: the questionnaire's edge set and the consistency filter. VARIES: the uniform reversal rate in {0, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5} × 10 seeds. Reports REALISED wrongness, never intended (6.8% realised for an intended 0.10, 25.6% for 0.25, 51.6% for 0.50), the post-filter population, and — new — the fraction of draws in which G0 still equals the true DAG despite flipping, which is 1,388 of 2,737 rows (50.7%) in the committed wrong_knowledge.jsonl and is the reason this arm is not an escape from the invariant.

ARM 10 — G-TIERED (correlated error). FIXED: the same edge set, filter and realised-wrongness reporting as Arm 9, so the only difference is the correlation structure. VARIES: the tier-misfiling rate × 10 seeds. Never run on real graphs before. Checkable statistic: a permutation test asking whether wrong assertions are closer together in the graph than a same-count uniform null predicts.

ARM 11 — NULL and MISSING controls. NULL: K empty, everything else fixed, so 'the radius is large' can be distinguished from 'the knowledge was vacuous'. NULL is also the COMPUTE WORST CASE, because G0 = Chat carries the most undirected edges of any arm, so costing NULL bounds every other arm — which is why the cap-17 tractability figures are quoted at K = empty. MISSING: K consistent AND true but incomplete, the control against which every false arm is read; this is the ONLY arm where coverage remains a knob, and because its instance set is fixed by construction the coverage comparison is not a composition effect. VARIES within MISSING: coverage and placement (globally versus locally sampled around X, at matched coverage).

ARM 12 — MATCHED-ER NEGATIVE CONTROL. FIXED: the same pipeline, gate, extension scope, reporting schema and sentinel conventions as the real arms, and a COMMITTED generator script, which the arm it replaces has never had. VARIES: the generator and its parameters, restricted to the real corpus's density band (mean degree 1.60 to 9.86, median 2.92), sizes overlapped where the corpus permits, seed dispersion on every figure. SCOPE LIMIT, stated not discovered: only the mechanical arms and R3-scrambled can answer on this substrate, because a synthetic graph has no publication and no domain semantics, so A6-3 tests substrate exchangeability for MECHANICAL knowledge and is silent about R1 and R2.

axes.axis: A1 SUBSTRATE — population of true structures and parameters, and the statistics a substrate must match for a claim to transfer
axes.decision: Three referent-ordered tiers, one labelled control, and one new bridge stratum. TIER A (referent-bearing applied): the applied dagitty DAGs, now EIGHT rather than seven, because Thoemmes_2013 enters the moment empty_set_trivially_valid leaves the deployment path. Recomputed under the observables-only frame of A2 these carry 595 candidate (X,Y) pairs and 41 load-bearing undirected edges, against 117 pairs and 39 edges under today's true-DAG gate. TIER B (benchmark): the BIF and bnjson networks; 29 networks in total yield candidate pairs after the questionnaire cut below, against 25 that yield anything today — alarm, andes and link enter. TIER C (contamination-clean): at least one bnRep network whose source publication post-dates the surrogate cutoff, with a PRE-REGISTERED ABANDONMENT RULE, since the draft specified this tier least concretely and its post-cutoff subset has never been enumerated: if no qualifying network is in hand by the time R3 elicitation starts, Tier C is reported ABSENT and A6-4's decomposition limitation is printed in the abstract rather than the appendix. CONTROL (matched Erdos-Renyi): a labelled negative control through the SAME pipeline, gate, extension scope and reporting schema, cells restricted to the real corpus's density band (mean degree 1.60 to 9.86, median 2.92), every figure per generator and per n with seed dispersion, and a COMMITTED generator script. Two structural additions kept from the draft: recover M-bias as a named 5-node latent-projection variant with its own sha256 and a written derivation note, never pooled with the parsed corpus; and compute var-sortability and R^2-sortability on every tier under bnlearn's own fitted coefficients. The declared transfer statistic remains the distribution of separation from X to the nearest member of O* inside X's chain component, reported WITH its undefined-status rate attached and never as a bare >=2 fraction.
axes.justification: Ledger A1 forces the tiers and the control; what forces the RESIZING is a recomputation done for this protocol on 2026-09-11. The frame change alone moves the applied tier from 117 to 595 candidate pairs and the corpus from 25 to 33 yielding networks, which is the difference between an appendix and a substrate section. The corpus still traces to ONE pgmpy 1.0.0 sdist (sha256 aef361e0...8255a), so real structure is a corpus claim until bnRep supplies a second acquisition; that is why Tier C carries an abandonment rule rather than an assumption. M-bias is dropped on an is_dag parse technicality with no written argument and it is the textbook structure in which a consistent-looking adjustment choice opens a collider path, which is the exact failure being priced. The transfer statistic is separation because O* = pa(cn(X,Y)) \ forb(X,Y) is a LOCAL functional (Henckel, Perkovic & Maathuis, arXiv:1907.02435) and the radius equalled the separation in 792 of 792 designed instances; density and size are not the right unit, since within Erdos-Renyi separation >=2 swings 3.6% dense / 14.7% medium / 24.1% sparse, a factor of 6.7 on density against 1.75 across a fivefold size change. The undefined-status rate must travel because it differs 2.6-fold between the arms and cuts against the real side (44.3%, 368 of 831, versus 17.1%, 327 of 1,914). Sortability profiles are mandatory because standard ANM and linear-SEM sampling leak the causal order through marginal variance and through R^2, which survives z-standardisation (Reisach et al. NeurIPS 2021 arXiv:2102.13647; NeurIPS 2023 arXiv:2303.18211), and neither has ever been computed on this corpus; iSCM removes the variance leak but shows reversed R^2-sortability on denser graphs (Ormaniec arXiv:2406.11601; Herman CLeaR 2025 arXiv:2503.17037), so any retained synthetic cell carries a second parameterisation. The control must be rebuilt rather than inherited because no committed script writes results/axisa2/random_control.jsonl, so the existing arm's K-selection rule, gate choice and coverage setting are unverifiable from the tree — and because A6-3 has no power without it. One ledger claim is corrected here rather than repeated: the ledger states real admissible records carry no method field; all 831 carry one, distributed {local_up_fast: 811, e1_ladder: 20}, so the real arm has its own unreported two-method provenance split that must be broken out.
axes.falsifiable_check: The matched-ER separation test, unchanged in shape and sharpened in denominator. Run the matched control through the identical pipeline and compare the FULL separation distribution against the real corpus's, on the 5,032-pair observables-only population and not on the 831-row true-DAG-gated one, at a level pre-registered before the control is looked at, reporting each arm's undefined-status rate as its own number rather than conditioning it away. DECISION RULE: if the matched control is not distinguishable from the real corpus on that distribution, the substrate argument is dead — the finding narrows in writing from 'ER is not exchangeable with real structure' to 'the edge probability was set wrong', Zé's Decision 2 declining structure-matched synthetic generators is formally reopened rather than inherited, and A6-3 loses its positive control, so every non-rejection in A6-1 becomes uninterpretable and must be reported as such. This check is likely to bite: at the sparse setting the unmatched ER arm already reaches 24.1% against real 45.4%, under a factor of two.
axes.cost: Compute: 1 to 2 days wall-clock for the matched control once the gate is the polynomial GAC predicate and the extension scope is dependency-closed. Sortability profiles are minutes. Agent-hours: ~12, most of it the committed generator script that does not exist and the M-bias derivation. Human-hours: ~6 for the bnRep post-cutoff filtering decision and the written M-bias argument. Nothing on the critical path except Tier C acquisition, which now has an abandonment rule so it cannot silently become one.

axes.axis: A2 QUERY POLICY — how (X,Y) is drawn, non-adaptively, and what the admissibility filters do to the population
axes.decision: A two-stage frame, filter surgery, and a measured population expansion that the draft under-counted by an order of magnitude. STAGE 1, a census stratum: every documented (exposure, outcome) pair recovered from the dagitty attrs group, taken as-is and never filtered out of the report. Restoring it costs one field on ParsedNetwork; the regex at dagitty.py:44 captures attrs and the string 'attrs' occurs exactly once in the whole source tree, so every applied author's declared exposure, outcome, adjustment set and latent marker is matched and discarded at parse time. STAGE 2, the declared observables-only sampling frame replacing 'screen all n(n-1)': draw X from chain components of Chat of size >= 2 or nodes adjacent to one, draw Y from possde(X, G0), then a seeded deterministic stride, with total_ordered_pairs, sampled_pairs, sampling_rate, sampling_seed and the REALISED INTEGER COUNT on a per-network _meta row (the two currently disagree by up to 23%). MEASURED CONSEQUENCE, recomputed for this protocol: the frame admits 5,045 distinct candidate (X,Y) pairs over 33 networks, against 543 distinct admissible pairs over 25 networks today, and the old set is a STRICT SUBSET of the new one with zero losses. FILTER SURGERY, stated exactly. Keep treatment_not_in_or_adjacent_to_component (reads Chat), knowledge_inconsistent (Meek Algorithm 1 on Chat and K), o_g0_not_identified and z_invalid_at_g0 (both at G0), and o_g0_extensions_intractable (a measurement limit with its own status). Replace no_causal_path with the observables-only test Y in possde(X, G0). DELETE from the deployment path the three filters that read the true DAG — no_valid_adjustment_set, empty_set_trivially_valid, no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity — and convert them into post-hoc audit LABELS. QUESTIONNAIRE CUT, derived not chosen: the frame implies 551 load-bearing undirected edges; a network earns questionnaire space only if it buys at least one candidate pair per question asked, which cuts munin, munin2, munin3 and munin4 (127 questions for 13 pairs) and keeps everything else including link at 5 questions for 9 pairs. Final questionnaire: 424 questions over 29 networks and 5,032 candidate pairs, with the cut published rather than silent. Additionally: record per (X,Y) the number of valid adjustment sets; run H4, the naive |K|-count baseline, pre-registered and unrun for six sessions; report every aggregate pair-weighted AND network-weighted, per network first, zero-yield networks in the denominator; keep the adaptivity ban, defended rather than assumed.
axes.justification: Verified in the repo on 2026-09-10 and re-verified 2026-09-11: of the 12 documented (exposure, outcome) pairs, exactly ONE is admissible — the toy mediator graph, and only at coverage 1.0 — and all eight applied papers' own queries are rejected by a filter that reads the true DAG. Six of the eight (Acid_1996, Didelez_2010, Kampen_2014, Polzer_2012, Sebastiani_2005, Shrier_2008) fall to no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity, Schipf_2010 to no_causal_path, Thoemmes_2013 to empty_set_trivially_valid; confounding falls to a filter that survives and M-bias is never screened at all. fast_gate reads dag.descendants(x), computes o = optimal_adjustment_set_dag from the TRUE DAG, tests is_valid_adjustment_set_dag twice, and builds k_true = knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag) before looping the atomic perturbations. Two facts recomputed here change what the surgery costs and what it buys. FIRST, the reject-reason census over all 115,974 screened rows is {treatment_not_in_or_adjacent 66,330; no_causal_path 42,618; empty_set_trivially_valid 3,738; no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity 1,659; ok 831; o_g0_not_identified 518; o_g0_extensions_intractable 280} and NOTHING ELSE: no_valid_adjustment_set, z_invalid_at_g0 and knowledge_inconsistent each fire ZERO times. So deleting no_valid_adjustment_set is free, and the Meek consistency filter — one of A6-1's feature-vector components — has never once fired, because oracle K is consistent by construction; it becomes a live variable only under elicitation, and every published Meek-rejection rate in this lineage is identically zero for that reason. SECOND, and this is the finding the draft missed: no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity is precisely what MANUFACTURES the real arm's 'unreached = 0 of 831'. It certifies that some single retraction of k_true already breaks validity. Delete it, as the invariant requires, and UNREACHED becomes possible on the real side for the first time, so the redesign must PRE-REGISTER a non-zero real-side UNREACHED rate as an expected outcome and a headline, not as a defect. It also means the comparison between the real arm's zero infinite radii and any synthetic arm's rate was never a comparison of populations; it was a comparison of gates. The frame replacement is forced by the budget sitting on the wrong side of the filter (115,974 ordered pairs screened to keep 831, treatment_not_in_or_adjacent alone burning 66,330, pathfinder spending its entire 1,200 s wall cap on screening and producing no radius). Recording the count of valid adjustment sets is required because it decides whether the incumbent RoCA test has power on that instance (Su & Henckel UAI 2022, arXiv:2206.07533, verified CONFIRMED); pairs with exactly one valid set are where testing is unavailable and pricing is the only instrument. Dual weighting is mandatory because the weights differ materially (separation >=2 at 45.4% pair-weighted versus 35.6% network-weighted; r=1 at 61.1% versus 71.3%). The adaptivity ban is load-bearing rather than stylistic: an answerer who has seen a computed radius contaminates the exchangeability test A6-1 runs.
axes.falsifiable_check: The documented-pair recovery check, pre-registered before the surgery runs, and now with its mechanism written down so the prediction is risky rather than tautological. PREDICTION: under the observables-only filter set at least 6 of the 12 documented (exposure, outcome) pairs become measurable, against 1 of 12 today. The mechanism is that fast_gate short-circuits, so the six pairs rejected by no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity were never tested against the knowledge-dependent filters that remain live — o_g0_not_identified and z_invalid_at_g0 at an ELICITED G0 — and any of them may still fall there. That is exactly why 6 is a prediction and not an arithmetic identity. DECISION RULE: if fewer than 4 of 12 survive, the applied tier cannot carry the domain-documented stratum, that stratum is declared dead in writing rather than quietly dropped, A6-2's referent falls back to harvested-prose K on the sampled pairs only, and the power of every A6-2 comparison is recomputed and reprinted at the smaller n. The full before/after table — which filter rejected which documented pair at which coverage — is published either way, as the population-shaping report the pre-registration promised and never delivered.
axes.cost: Compute: the frame itself is graph-only (component membership plus a possibly-directed reachability pass) and ran over all 38,658 distinct screened pairs in under a minute on this machine, so the draft's 'one day to rescreen' is wrong by two orders of magnitude and is corrected to under an hour. What costs is the DOWNSTREAM evaluation of 5,032 rather than 543 pairs, priced under A5. Agent-hours: ~10 — one dataclass field, the possde test, the frame sampler, the _meta schema fix, the H4 baseline, the questionnaire cut script. Human-hours: ~3 for the pre-registered prediction and the population-shaping table. Still the cheapest high-yield change on the board.

axes.axis: A3 KNOWLEDGE MODEL — source, coverage, granularity, and above all the error process
axes.decision: select_knowledge is DELETED from the deployment path and reborn as the post-hoc yardstick; on the deployment path K comes only from an answerer on the frozen questionnaire. THE QUESTIONNAIRE IS RE-DERIVED FROM OBSERVABLES, which is the draft's own invariant violation corrected: one question per undirected edge of Chat lying in a chain component that contains at least one candidate treatment UNDER THE A2 FRAME — 424 questions over 29 networks, not 342 over 25, because 342 was scoped by an admissible set that a true-DAG gate produced. Response grammar three-way and multi-granular: {A->B, B->A, DECLINE}, plus optional forbidden-edge, tier and ancestral assertions from a fixed vocabulary, each with a source-reported confidence in [0,1] that is RETAINED. Query form triplet / causal-order, never pairwise. FIVE ADDITIONS the draft omits against the ledger's A3 checkable list. (i) CHECKABLE #1: the headline error quantity is named the CONSISTENT-BUT-FALSE FRACTION — assertions that survive Meek Algorithm 1 and are wrong — reported as its own column, never as 'noise' and never folded into a scalar. (ii) CHECKABLE #4: a published SCALE BRIDGE mapping our (reversed, omitted, invented) triple onto CSCD's 0.3-reversed and b-LOAD's rho and mu, so the three arms are quantitatively comparable rather than merely adjacent. (iii) CHECKABLE #7: a COMPELLED-EDGE CONTROL BLOCK — a seeded sample of edges the CPDAG already orients is put in the questionnaire, because the undirected-edges-only questionnaire has no data at all on the data-compelled half of that checkable; a correct answer there is redundant under Meek and costs the deployment path nothing, a wrong one is inconsistent, so the block is a pure commission detector for free. And the distance-stratified error rate is RECOVERED rather than abandoned: 424 questions × 3 conditions × 2 prompt variants × >=2 models is several thousand assertions, enough to estimate it on R3 and the mechanical arms; it is only R2 that cannot support it, and the pre-registration says the R2 comparison is on the pooled rate alone. (iv) CHECKABLE #11: TWO PROMPT VARIANTS per condition with mention order randomised under a stored seed, so prompt-induced variance is measured rather than assumed away, and the refinement budget is declared at zero as a reported protocol parameter. (v) CHECKABLE #13: confidence is retained AND its use is GATED — the audit arm publishes the stated-confidence-versus-measured-correctness calibration curve before the deployment arm is permitted to read confidence at all. Every assertion carries granularity, graph distance from X, confidence, provenance (answerer id, prompt hash and variant, model id, temperature 0, response-cache key, or coder id and paper DOI), pre- and post-filter Meek status, and cascade size. Error is reported on ONE scale for all answerers — fraction reversed, omitted, invented, each with its Wilson interval, realised and never intended, split by granularity AND network and never pooled. Nine arms: R1 published-author, R2 human analyst, R3 surrogate in three conditions, NULL, MISSING, and the mechanical generators (knowledge_to_recover-thinned, uniform flip, tiered misfiling). COVERAGE STOPS BEING A KNOB and becomes an observed covariate of an elicited K.
axes.justification: The invariant. select_knowledge calls knowledge_to_recover(dag, cpdag) and thins it by an even stride, so at coverage 1.0 G0 IS the true DAG exactly with zero undirected edges — 543 of 831 admissible instances, 65% of the corpus, the ball centred on the truth. It is also greedy and gain-maximising, repeatedly asserting the true orientation whose Meek closure compels the most new edges, so the K it returns is systematically smaller and more cascading than an analyst's claim set, biasing |K_G0| — the other binding term of r_val <= min(s, |K_G0|) — downward. Two further verifications sharpen this. The committed wrong_knowledge.jsonl carries g0_is_true_dag on every row, and it is TRUE in 1,388 of 2,737 rows (50.7%) even under flipping, so injecting flips is not an escape from the invariant — only elicitation is. And knowledge_inconsistent has fired zero times in 115,974 screened rows, which is the mechanical proof that the consistency filter has never been exercised by the oracle model. The questionnaire's scope is corrected because a questionnaire whose edge set was selected by which pairs a true-DAG gate admitted is itself a true-DAG functional on the deployment path; 424 over 29 networks is the observables-only answer, and the four munin networks are cut by a written rule (127 questions for 13 candidate pairs) rather than dropped. Triplet rather than pairwise because Vashishtha et al. (arXiv:2310.15117, verified CONFIRMED) measure over 3k cycles on Child and over 5k on Neuropathic under pairwise against zero under triplet, SHD falling 177 to 28, and Child, Asia, Alarm, Insurance and Sachs are all inside our own BIF corpus. Per-granularity coverage because tiered knowledge closes under Meek R1 alone while single-edge assertions cascade through R1 to R4, so the same nominal coverage buys a different closure and a different radius (Bang & Didelez). Distance from X as a distribution because placement is a measured first-class variable and locally-sampled knowledge beats globally-sampled knowledge at the same rho (b-LOAD, arXiv:2607.04447). Confidence retained but GATED because our own CSCD measurement says correct hard constraints raise accepted precision (PC 0.802 to 0.850) while noisy hard constraints hurt recall (PC 0.577 to 0.526), so an error process that only ever hardens will overstate the damage — and because stated confidence is known to be miscalibrated, which is why the calibration curve precedes its use. Pre- and post-filter reporting because consistency is purely syntactic and says nothing about truth (Perkovic, Kalisch & Maathuis UAI 2017, arXiv:1707.02171), a practitioner drops what Meek FAILs, up to two thirds of corrupted draws are rejected outright, and realised wrongness lands at 6.8% for an intended 0.10. NULL and MISSING because an expert-asserted structure cannot be assumed informative — the out-of-domain precedent is an expert-designed structure adding at most +0.01 AUC on 7 of 9 real datasets (Gervet JEDM 2020) — and without them a large radius is confounded with vacuous knowledge. Forbidden edges and tiers because b-LOAD's noise study is confined to required edges and bkrobust's operators are orientation-only, and that is the one weakness all four b-LOAD reviewers named. Coverage demoted because the three strata are non-comparable populations (543/182/106, survivors with systematically larger separation, r=1 falling 69.8 to 51.1 to 34.0% as a composition effect) — and because the corpus-wide three-stratum intersection of 105 pairs collapses to SIXTEEN on the applied tier, which the draft proposed to condition on and which cannot carry a comparison.
axes.falsifiable_check: The cascade-size test, run on the SAME questionnaire so nothing else varies. Compute the distribution of edges-compelled-per-assertion for R1, R2, R3 and knowledge_to_recover. PREDICTION, pre-registered before any answerer is scored: knowledge_to_recover's cascade-size distribution is stochastically LARGER than every human and surrogate answerer's, because it is greedy and gain-maximising by construction. DECISION RULE: if a two-sample test on the same edges fails to separate them at the pre-registered level, the claim that the incumbent knowledge model is unrealistically cascading — the stated reason the redesign was necessary — is withdrawn in writing, the incumbent's published numbers stop being labelled biased on that ground, and the redesign's justification narrows to the invariant violation alone. The statistic is cheap and has never been computed on any candidate generator. SUBORDINATE CHECK: the redesigned error process must preserve the measured direction that wrong knowledge INCREASES the radius (r=1 share 57.8 to 42.1% as flip rate rises 0 to 0.5, median 1 to 2, s>=2 share 40.6 to 49.5%, max radius 14 and max separation 7 unchanged), or state in writing why it no longer holds. SECOND SUBORDINATE CHECK, new: the compelled-edge control block must return a near-zero contradiction rate for R1 and R2 and a measurable one for R3, or the block is measuring question comprehension rather than knowledge and is reported as such.
axes.cost: Compute: negligible; cascade statistics and Meek closures are milliseconds. Agent-hours: ~22 — the whole knowledge-sourcing API is specified and entirely NotImplementedError (elicit.py, taxonomy.py, perturb.py, graphs/distances.py) and the specifications are better than anything the built code does, so this is filling a written scaffold; the additions are the consistent-but-false accounting, the scale bridge, the compelled-edge block, the prompt-variant plumbing and the confidence-calibration gate. Human-hours: the elicitation itself, priced under A6. Surrogate tokens: 424 questions plus the control block × 3 conditions × 2 prompt variants × >=2 models is roughly 5,600 to 6,600 cached calls, tens of dollars.

axes.axis: A4 PERTURBATION GEOMETRY — centre, distance, operator, and the reference measure inside a shell
axes.decision: Centre at Meek(Chat, K), never at the truth — already correct in code, since breakdown_radius takes no true DAG in its signature and local_up_covers takes (cpdag, g). Unit: d_L,pseudo (#directed + 2 × #undirected atomic moves), declared once in conventions.py and printed in every manifest as a human-readable RADIUS_CONVENTION string. Operator: RETRACTION, with a forbidden-edge retraction and a TIER retraction added, the latter costed as a block rather than one hop. THREE things the audit forces. FIRST, a reference measure inside the shell: alongside r, report phi(j), the fraction of shell-j covers at which Z fails, for j = 0 to r+2, uniform over covers, with an O*-relevance-weighted variant as a secondary column. SECOND, unify the two geometries: breakdown_radius walks the covering graph while the r_0 probe enumerates raw retraction SUBSETS of K, and its j is not the same metric as d; the covering-graph distance is the DEFINITION, the subset enumeration is an approximation labelled as such wherever it appears, with the disagreement rate measured on the instances where both run. THIRD, and new: SENTINEL DISCIPLINE MUST BE EXTENDED TO UNREACHED BEFORE THE SWEEP RUNS, because deleting no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity makes real-side UNREACHED possible for the first time; today it is 0 of 831 by gate construction. r_P = min{d(G0,G) : P fails at G} as BFS hop count; shells 0..r-1 certified clean so the safe-move count is r-1; UNREACHED = -1 never averaged or plotted on a numeric axis; DEGENERATE = 0 gated out at generation; NOT-REACHED added for elicitation time-outs; and r_0's three distinct 'infinite' cases (no zero in the hull, hull undefined, extension cap hit) given three distinct statuses instead of one Python None. Forbidden claim forms enforced here: never a continuity bound, never SHD as the unit, never rank arithmetic on the MPDAG poset.
axes.justification: SHD is refused because SHD1 <= SHD2 <= d_L,pseudo for any MPDAGs with an explicit example at d_L,pseudo = 1 while SHD = n-1, so an SHD-denominated radius OVER-certifies (Taeb, Guo & Henckel arXiv:2511.10625v3, Proposition 12, Example 2, Fig. 5). Rank arithmetic is refused because for |V| >= 4 the poset is not graded, so no rank function exists, and it is neither a semi-lattice nor semimodular, so the cheap two-sided bounds are only upper bounds (Proposition 9, Table 3, Theorem 1). The covering relation has no known graphical characterisation, stated three times in that source, so conditioning on the fixed estimated skeleton sub-poset G_Chat is necessary and whether gradedness returns there is stated as a CONJECTURE. Retraction is derived rather than assumed: failure is upward-closed because refinement shrinks the represented DAG set, so orienting one more edge can never invalidate a fixed valid adjustment set, a flip costs exactly two atomic moves, and the first failure is always reached by losing an assertion. The shell measure is forced because BFS returns the nearest failure and nothing about how much of shell j fails. HERE THE DRAFT OVER-CLAIMS AND IS CORRECTED: the committed calibration table in report.md reports coverage 1.00 with conservativeness 0.425, 0.439 and 0.465 across three scenarios, but that is measured over the WHOLE outside-radius region of a 48-element demo space, not over shell r+1 of the real corpus. It does not bracket phi(r+1) from below and must not be quoted as if it did; phi(r+1) is genuinely unmeasured and the threshold is pre-registered at the sign change alone. Weighted covering relations are named as open future work in the competing paper's own section 7, which is the slot the O*-relevance weighting fills. Continuity bounds are forbidden because damage conditional on O* moving is heavy-tailed — median 0.59, up to 128× — so the object is a breakdown radius. Every exact radius inherits an open assumption chain (Anti-Exchange Case B => Lemma R => Property S => Lemma L => Conjecture 2), Case A proved and Case B open at 0 violations in 36,094 applicable triples, whose failure direction is one-sided and FAVOURABLE to the hypothesis (radii too large, optimistic about robustness); that caveat and the counter-directed MPDAG-GAC-forbidden-set caveat travel with every number.
axes.falsifiable_check: The shell-measure calibration check, pre-registered before phi is computed, with the threshold now anchored on the sign change ALONE because no prior estimate legitimately bounds it. Report phi(r) and phi(r+1). DECISION RULE: if phi(r+1) < 0.5 — fewer than half the graphs one hop beyond the certified radius actually break — the certificate is advertised as a LOWER BOUND WITH MEASURED SLACK and never as a tolerance, the verb 'tolerates' is struck from the paper, and the slack figure travels in the abstract beside r. SECOND PRE-REGISTERED CHECK, forced by the filter surgery: the real-side UNREACHED rate, which is 0 of 831 today purely because no_atomic_perturbation_changes_validity certified a one-hop failure before any radius was computed. The redesign predicts it becomes non-zero. If it does NOT — if UNREACHED stays at zero across all 5,032 candidate pairs with the gate removed — then that filter was never load-bearing, the population expansion bought no new geometry, and the sentence about gate-manufactured headlines is withdrawn. SUBORDINATE OBLIGATION: the forbidden-edge and tier retraction moves must return radii identical to the current ones on required-edge-only instances; disagreement there means the new moves are wrong, not that the geometry changed.
axes.cost: Compute: phi(j) rides on covers already generated for the BFS, so the marginal cost is roughly one extra shell on top of a radius search that runs at 0.02 to 0.16 s per instance. The tier-retraction move is new enumeration, bounded by the same cap. Agent-hours: ~15, including the sentinel extension (UNREACHED, NOT-REACHED, the three r_0 statuses) and the two-geometry disagreement report. Human-hours: ~15, and least optional here, because three prior-art items must close before the differentiation paragraph is written: Appendix F.3 of arXiv:2511.10625v3 (three failed retrievals, and the section-6 readings CONFLICT across passes), the identity of arXiv:2010.08611 (two different titles across three passes, all abstract-level), and the entirely unsearched stability-radius family (stability radius = r_opt, radius of robust feasibility = r_val, Renegar's distance to ill-posedness, AGM contraction, MUS/MCS minimal correction sets — zero corpus hits and zero queries run), which is a prior-art risk on the one part of the geometry claimed as unshared.

axes.axis: A5 STATISTICAL LAYER — oracle CPDAG against a CPDAG estimated at finite n, and how the two are kept separate
axes.decision: Fix the gate first with a THEOREM STATED AT THE RIGHT SCOPE, then run two panels, then cut what does not fit. THE GATE. (1) is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag is NEVER called on the deployment path; is_gac_valid_mpdag is, measured at 8.2× (20.22 s to 2.47 s over 2,240 pairs across child, insurance, asia, sachs and water, 2,240 of 2,240 identical verdicts, 0 disagreements) and 1.07 ms per call at n = 20. (2) The one enumeration that REMAINS on the deployment path is optimal_adjustment_set_mpdag inside evaluate, which calls enumerate_dag_extensions on the WHOLE G0; it is restricted to the DEPENDENCY-CLOSED COMPONENT SET — the union of chain components meeting cn(X,Y) together with their parents and neighbours — and NOT, as the draft states, to X's chain component alone. That narrower statement is false as written, because O* = pa(cn(X,Y)) \ forb(X,Y) reads parents of the whole causal-node set, which can lie in other components; shipping it would make the differential fire and, under the draft's own decision rule, kill a substitution that is correct at the right scope. (3) The cap is DERIVED from a measured cost curve, not chosen: enumerate_dag_extensions timed on this machine gives asia 2 undirected edges 0.000 s, child 12 edges 0.048 s, sachs 14 edges 0.149 s (whole-graph 17 edges 1.375 s, so the restriction is 9.2× there), insurance 18 edges 2.789 s (whole-graph 7.289 s, 2.6×), against the known ecoli70 wall of 1,839.78 s at 25 edges — a factor of 657 over seven edges, about 2.6× per additional edge. MAX_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS is therefore set to 17, where the worst call is about one second, and everything above it is a STATUS (o_g0_extensions_intractable) with its wall recorded, never a rejection. (4) WHAT THAT ACTUALLY BUYS, measured over the 5,032-pair population at K = empty, the worst case: global enumeration at cap 12 (today's rule) covers 44.8%; the dependency-closed restriction at the same cap covers 53.3%; at cap 14, 64.7%; at cap 17, 75.1%; at cap 20, 83.6%; at cap 25, 89.8%. So the restriction buys 8.5 points at fixed cap and the leverage is the cap raise it licenses. The draft's claim that this opens the corpus by orders of magnitude is refuted by this curve and is withdrawn. THE TWO PANELS: an oracle-CI panel beside a finite-n panel sampling from the fitted linear-Gaussian SEM at a declared n grid, running a CPDAG-EMITTING discovery method, comparing recovered component structure and separation against the already-committed descriptive_structure.csv, with the generator held fixed across panels. Reporting axis Pi = n / (|V| × d_exp/2). Estimator: the Frisch-Waugh-Lovell standard error from a covariance matrix alone, the same formula for population Sigma and sample Sigma-hat, with the true DAG entering only to generate the sample. THE BAND, NOT THE POINT HULL. Coverage reported CONDITIONAL ON r. Two reported quantities and never one interval: the perturbation layer prices structural error, the sampling layer prices sampling error. Stated once, early: the certificate is a DETERMINISTIC COMBINATORIAL certificate, a functional of (Chat, K, X, Y, Sigma-hat, n) — not a Bayesian credible bound, not a conformal set. Until the finite-n panel runs, the claim form 'robust under an ESTIMATED CPDAG' stays forbidden. THE CUT, made explicitly: the finite-n panel runs on SIX networks, not the corpus, selected by a written rule — at least 20 pairs in Arm 0's bridge stratum AND dependency-closed component inside cap 17 — because a CPDAG-emitting discovery run per (network, n, seed) times the full radius pipeline times the seed-dispersion requirement does not fit any budget a person will actually run.
axes.justification: The wall is measured, not estimated: one is_valid_adjustment_set_mpdag call took 1,839.78 s on ecoli70, 46 nodes with 25 undirected edges and a 2^25 global enumeration, against 0.02 to 0.04 s for an entire r_0 on the same network; the earlier '>120 s' was the author's waiting limit rather than a measurement. A protocol that calls that once per graph in a ball is not a protocol, and the answer is three-part and each part is measured rather than hoped for: substitute the predicate (Theorem 14 says back-door and GAC coincide on Z = O(.), so it is a cost substitution and not a change of predicate, and gate_predicate_swap.json records 2,240 of 2,240 identical verdicts), restrict the one remaining enumeration to the dependency-closed components, and cap on the measured cost curve rather than on a round number. The component restriction needs a theorem plus a differential and not a commit, because the rejected one-level-cover optimisation was 746× faster on pathfinder and WRONG — retracting a knowledge edge and re-closing can land strictly above a cover — and only the differential caught it. A CPDAG-emitting method is required because a skeleton-times-order factorisation commits to a single topological order and destroys the undirected chain component the radius is defined on (Thompson et al. Arrow arXiv:2605.07204). The generator is held fixed because post-hoc-standardised SCMs' near-determinism breaks CI tests and PC/GES do better on large iSCMs for that reason (Ormaniec arXiv:2406.11601). The band is chosen on a measurement rather than a preference, using three-bucket scoring because agreement is the wrong metric for a deliberately conservative estimator and hides the sign: the point hull errs DANGEROUS 24.7% at n = 200 and still 18.1% at n = 20,000, while the 95% band errs dangerous at most 1.7% at every n even though its raw agreement looks worse (7.8% versus 57.0% on magic-irri at n = 200), and a danger rate that barely improves over a hundredfold n increase is the argument that this is a coverage problem and not a sample-size problem. Conditional coverage because a degenerate small-radius corner otherwise averages into a healthy-looking number. Two quantities because if the graph knowledge is wrong the ESTIMAND itself moves, which is outside any covariate-shift correction (Lei & Candès JRSS-B 83(5)). And the compute bar is external: the sensitivity family is now amortised with orders-of-magnitude speedups (Javurek arXiv:2605.10590), so either the gate is made cheap or the protocol must argue why an exact combinatorial certificate is worth several orders of magnitude more compute than an amortised bound. The measurement limit stays a status: MAX_G0_UNDIRECTED_FOR_EXTENSIONS = 12 produced 280 o_g0_extensions_intractable rows, three network runs are censored at wall_until_timeout_s = 1200.0 and are never counted as measurements, and the 280 are re-reported once the restriction lands.
axes.falsifiable_check: The component-restriction differential, now stated at the scope the theorem can actually carry. PRE-REGISTERED CLAIM: enumeration restricted to the dependency-closed component set returns verdicts identical to the global enumeration on every instance where the global version terminates. DECISION RULE: ANY disagreement kills the substitution outright — this is a claimed theorem, not a tuning parameter, so one disagreement means the theorem is false, the global enumeration stays, the tractability wall is reported as a scope limit, and the corpus is narrowed in writing to the networks where the global version terminates. THE DIFFERENTIAL'S OWN BUDGET IS BOUNDED BY A WRITTEN RULE, because it must call the slow path wherever it terminates: it runs only on pairs whose whole-graph undirected count is at most 18, where the measured worst case is 7.3 s, and every network carries its own wall cap and censoring record; networks where the global version does not terminate contribute nothing and are reported as censored rather than as agreement. The disagreement rate is published WITH ITS SIGN whatever it is, following the fast_gate precedent, where the author predicted the substitution was strictly weaker and the differential showed it was strictly stricter — 16 disagreements in 46,800 cases, 0.034%, all one-directional, and the exclusion biased AGAINST our own hypothesis.
axes.cost: Wall-clock. The deployment sweep is now costable rather than hand-waved: 75.1% of 5,032 candidate pairs sit inside cap 17, about 3,779 pairs; at roughly 1.2 s per pair (Meek closure plus component-restricted enumeration plus the polynomial GAC predicate plus a radius search measured at 0.02 to 0.16 s) that is about 75 minutes per arm-run, and with six deterministic arms plus three stochastic arms at ten seeds each, 36 arm-runs, about 45 hours, call it 2 days. The differential is the binding item at 3 days under the at-most-18-undirected bound and per-network caps. The finite-n panel, CUT to six networks × five n values × ten seeds, is 2 to 3 days; the uncut corpus version was 3 to 4 weeks and is the scope this axis explicitly abandons. Agent-hours: ~22, split between the dependency-closed restriction plus its theorem and test, the discovery front-end, the cap-17 status plumbing and the Pi axis. Human-hours: ~8 for the theorem statement and the assumption-status wording that travels with every number.

axes.axis: A6 REALISM AUDIT — the external referent the simulated knowledge distribution is judged against, and how the certificate's calibration is checked
axes.decision: BUILD the referent as one frozen questionnaire answered by four suppliers, then run six audit stages. THE QUESTIONNAIRE (A3's 424-question artefact, observables-scoped) is frozen and hashed before any answerer sees it. THE FOUR ANSWERERS. R1 PUBLISHED-AUTHOR: the restored dagitty attrs annotations, plus the prose of the eight source papers (Shrier & Platt 2008, Schipf 2010, Sebastiani 2005, Didelez 2010, Thoemmes 2013, Kampen 2014, Polzer 2012, Acid 1996) fetched and read, with two independent coders converting every causal assertion into the response grammar, blind to the DAG file; pre-adjudication Cohen's kappa reported with a floor at the conventional substantial-agreement boundary 0.61. Load: 41 load-bearing questions across the eight applied networks, now covering 595 candidate pairs rather than 117. R2 HUMAN ANALYST — REQUIRED, because without it the surrogate's number is a measurement of a language model and nothing licenses the word 'expert' anywhere in the paper. THE ROUND, resized on the Wilson curve: 82 domain-legible questions (the eight applied networks' 41 plus asia 3, child 12, hepar2 9, sachs 17), one sitting capped at 100 minutes, no feedback, no revision, unanswered items recorded NOT-REACHED. RECRUIT TO FIVE, FLOOR THREE, by a derived stopping rule: at a per-edge rate near 0.30 the Wilson 95% half-width is ±0.097 at m = 82, ±0.070 at 164 (28.6% narrower), ±0.057 at 246 (18.1%), ±0.049 at 328 (13.3%), ±0.044 at 410 (10.5%) — stop when the marginal analyst buys less than a tenth of the width, which is at five. Who: causal-inference-trained researchers who did not build the questionnaire and have not seen the true DAGs, so the licensed claim is about ANALYSTS specifying DAGs from a data dictionary, which is the deployed case. Because the ledger records no literature at all on elicitation time per edge, the round's own median seconds-per-question is published as a first measurement rather than assumed. R3 LLM SURROGATE: all 424 questions plus the compelled-edge control block, one pass, temperature 0, cached, in three conditions (named / scrambled / cold recall) × two prompt variants × at least two models. G MECHANICAL GENERATORS: knowledge_to_recover-thinned, uniform flip, tiered misfiling — arms to be judged, never deployment sources. THE SIX STAGES. A6-0 INVARIANT AUDIT: a machine-checkable manifest field per reported quantity, arm in {deployment, post_hoc} and true_dag_on_path in {true, false}; the seed exists as g0_is_true_dag in wrong_knowledge.jsonl; any row with arm=deployment and true_dag_on_path=true FAILS THE BUILD — and the check is run against the QUESTIONNAIRE's provenance too, since that is where the draft's own violation sat. A6-0b BRIDGE AUDIT, new: every legacy headline recomputed on the 543-pair intersection inside the new pipeline, since the old admissible set is a verified strict subset of the new candidate set. A6-1 DISCRIMINATOR: the ledger's feature vector (coverage per granularity; distance-from-X distribution; commission and omission separately; pairwise graph distance among the WRONG assertions; Meek Algorithm-1 rejection rate, which is identically zero in every published number and becomes live only here; cascade size; cycles before repair; consistent-but-false fraction), permutation two-sample test at the K level. A6-2 RADIUS TRANSFER: fixed instance set, paired. A6-3 POSITIVE CONTROL on the matched ER arm — with its scope limit printed, that only the mechanical arms and R3-scrambled can answer on a synthetic substrate, so it tests substrate exchangeability for MECHANICAL knowledge and is silent about R1 and R2. A6-4 CONTAMINATION SCREEN: named-minus-scrambled gap plus cold recall, with the correction written into the reporting — that gap BOUNDS memorisation above and domain knowledge below and does NOT separate them. PRE-REGISTERED FALLBACKS: fewer than 3 analysts completing means the human anchor is reported ABSENT and 'expert' is struck everywhere; pre-adjudication kappa below 0.61 means the harvested arm is reported as failed; no post-cutoff Tier C network in hand by elicitation start means Tier C is reported ABSENT and A6-4's limitation moves into the abstract. Scoring is mechanical, against the true DAG, in the post-hoc arm only; a second LLM never validates elicited knowledge and pairwise LLM comparison is never used.
axes.justification: The referent must be built because no published study measures a domain expert's per-edge error, separating omission from commission, on expert-specified DAGs scored against a known-true DAG — surviving a 1,100-note corpus grep, a seven-dimension web sweep, and a gap-fill that exhausted a 200-call budget and was blocked by HTTP 403 at Reliability Engineering & System Safety, Risk Analysis, IJAR and Knowledge-Based Systems. Adjacent things HAVE been measured and are not denied: expert calibration on probability estimates (Cooke, never instantiated for structure), expert accuracy on bivariate statements without ground truth, domain-varying expert accuracy on the Tübingen pairs (arXiv:2502.13132), unassisted expert accuracy 60.8% on a hidden gold standard (arXiv:2603.02678). R1 is the only answerer whose knowledge was produced by a real domain expert unaware of this study, and its data DOES NOT YET EXIST: over the 12 dagitty files, 12 of 12 carry one exposure and one outcome, only 2 carry any adjusted node (Didelez_2010: Age, Smo; Thoemmes_2013: s2 — three nodes in total), and the one file with latent nodes marks SEM error terms rather than substantive assertions, so exactly ONE file yields a published expert's own adjustment set. The knowledge is in the paper texts, and those eight papers were named in one sweep and fetched in none. On this tier truth is the published author's own diagram, so the score is DISAGREEMENT WITH THE AUTHOR — the CSCD/Sachs precedent, where a domain-accepted graph is used as an evaluation referent with precision and recall against it explicitly refused. The human round is required because a realism audit is an explicit two-sample comparison on a named statistic and a one-sample surrogate number is an assertion of resemblance, the form the ledger forbids. Its size is derived from the Wilson curve above rather than chosen. Contamination control is mandatory because ASIA, ALARM, CHILD, INSURANCE and SACHS sit in both our BIF corpus and the published evaluation sets of LLM-plus-SCM work, LLMs systematically override imposed causal facts with pretraining priors (CausalSynth arXiv:2605.17528), and a surrogate asked about them may be reciting; the two-model requirement comes from the flagging method itself (arXiv:2605.21543). A6-3 is rebuilt rather than inherited because its premise — that session 6 already shows the populations differ on the statistic the radius equals — is exactly what the A1 audit puts in question. A second LLM may never validate: judges and domain experts reach opposite conclusions on the same pairs, and the bias is WORSE in the comparative setting that is the standard remedy (arXiv:2606.12071). Two things are added against the draft. A6-0b exists because the old population is a verified strict subset of the new one (543 of 543 carried over, zero losses), so the draft's resignation that no result may be compared across the filter change is over-pessimistic and the bridge is cheap and obligatory. And A6-1's Meek-rejection feature is flagged as new-in-this-protocol, because knowledge_inconsistent has fired zero times in 115,974 screened rows and every published value of that feature is a construction artefact rather than a measurement.
axes.falsifiable_check: A6-2, the radius transfer test on the applied tier, which has teeth because the reported quantity is r and not K, and which now has real power because the frame change grew the tier. On the applied-tier instance set — 595 candidate pairs under the A2 frame, re-derived BEFORE the referent is looked at, against 117 under the old gate — compare the r=1 share under R3 (surrogate) against R1 (published-author), paired, same networks, same pairs, same gate, same estimator. DECISION RULE, in this order: (1) report the number of discordant pairs D FIRST, before any p-value; (2) if D < 17 the comparison is declared UNDERPOWERED and reported as a descriptive difference with its interval, never as a null and never as a rejection — the arithmetic fixing 17 is that below it a two-sided exact p < 0.05 needs more than 76% of discordant pairs to move one way (verified: D = 17 needs 13 of 17, D = 12 needs 10 of 12, D = 9 needs 8 of 9); (3) otherwise McNemar two-sided at alpha = 0.05, and REPORT THE SIGN. If the surrogate's r=1 share is significantly HIGHER than the referent's, the surrogate produces systematically LARGER radii, which is optimistic about robustness and therefore the dangerous direction: the surrogate arm becomes a separately reported stratum, never pooled, and no sentence about practice may be written from it. POWER AT THE DESIGN POINT, recomputed at the new n: with 595 paired instances the detectable marginal shift in the r=1 share at 80% power is 5.5 points at 25% discordance (E[D] = 149), 4.2 points at 15% (E[D] = 89) and 3.4 points at 10% (E[D] = 60), against 12.0 / 9.1 / 7.2 points on the draft's 117. The same test is run R3-versus-R2 on the 82-question subset and R3-versus-G-oracle on the whole 5,032-pair corpus, where the detectable shift falls to about 1.5 points, and the three signs are reported together.
axes.cost: Human-hours, and this axis is where they all are. R1: fetching and reading the eight applied papers 8 to 12 h with a real paywall risk (the gap-fill pass hit 403 at four journals), plus two independent coders over 41 load-bearing questions and free-text assertions, ~12 to 16 h across two people. R2: instrument build 6 to 8 h, recruiting to five 6 to 9 h, five sittings at up to 1.7 h each, scoring 3 h, so ~25 h. Pre-registration, the CFP-style section checklist and the two-stage commitment discipline: ~15 h. Total human on A6: ~55 to 70 h. Compute: R3's three conditions × two prompt variants × at least two models is roughly 5,600 to 6,600 cached calls, under a day and tens of dollars; A6-1's permutation tests, A6-0b's bridge recomputation and A6-4's recall probe are minutes. Agent-hours: ~28, for the questionnaire builder, the four answerer adapters against the elicit.py scaffold, the manifest invariant field with its build-failing assertion (extended to cover questionnaire provenance), the bridge-audit script and the four analysis scripts. Everything else in this protocol can be run by one person and a machine; the referent cannot, and that is the design's honest bottleneck.

known_weaknesses: My lens still spends the budget on the referent, but the imbalance is smaller than the draft admitted, because the frame change grew the corpus for free: 5,032 candidate pairs over 29 networks against 543 over 25. A substrate-first lens would still run the finite-n panel over the whole corpus rather than the six networks I cut it to, and if the referee's objection is 'n is small on the finite-n leg', that design answers it better than mine.

The tractability-first ordering is now partly vindicated and partly refuted, and I refuted my own draft's version of it. The dependency-closed restriction buys 8.5 percentage points at fixed cap (44.8% to 53.3% of candidate pairs), not orders of magnitude; the leverage is the cap raise it licenses, which takes coverage to 75.1% at cap 17 and 83.6% at cap 20 with the per-call cost rising about 2.6-fold per additional undirected edge. If the differential fires and the restriction dies, the protocol is left paying for elicitation on a corpus that grew from the A2 frame alone — which is still 9.3-fold, so the downside is bounded, but the cap stays at 12 and 55% of the population becomes a censoring record rather than a measurement.

The human round measures ANALYSTS, not domain experts, and I chose that deliberately. The recruitable population here is causal-inference-trained researchers reading a data dictionary. That is the deployed case and it is honest, but it is NOT the population the A6 gap sentence is about, which says no published study measures a DOMAIN EXPERT's per-edge error. An elicitation-methodology lens would insist on real domain experts with a Delphi or SHELF instrument, would take months, and would earn the stronger claim.

Five analysts is still a thin sample and the interval is printed rather than hidden: pooled m = 410 gives ±0.044 on a rate near 0.30. I have recovered the distance-stratified error rate on R3 and the mechanical arms, where several thousand assertions support it, but on R2 it remains out of reach, so the one quantity the ledger calls the most load-bearing unmeasured thing in the design is measured for a language model and not for a human. The human-versus-surrogate comparison is therefore on the pooled rate only, and that is pre-registered rather than discovered.

On the applied tier, truth is the published author's own diagram, so R1's score is disagreement with an author and not error. I keep the tier because it is the only one with a real expert in the loop, but every claim it supports is weaker than Tier B's, and the two are never pooled — the same non-pooling rule the ledger applies to the designed backdoor family, where pooling moved a headline from 79.6% to 65.3%.

A6-4 cannot separate memorisation from knowledge and I do not pretend it can. The named-minus-scrambled gap bounds one above and the other below. Tier C, a post-cutoff network, is the only clean control, and it is still the tier I specify least concretely, because bnRep's post-cutoff subset has not been enumerated; I have added an abandonment rule so its absence is declared rather than discovered, which converts a soft spot into a printed limitation but does not fill it.

A6-3 is a positive control for a narrower claim than its name suggests, and I have printed the limit rather than fixed it: a matched Erdos-Renyi graph has no publication and no domain semantics, so only the mechanical generators and R3-scrambled can supply K on it. The audit's power check therefore covers substrate exchangeability for mechanical knowledge and says nothing at all about whether the machinery could distinguish a human answerer from a generator on a synthetic substrate.

Deleting three filters enlarges the population in a direction I have measured on one axis and not on others. The 543-pair bridge stratum lets every legacy headline be recomputed inside the new pipeline, which is a real repair of the draft's weakness here, but the 4,502 net-new pairs are a population nobody has ever looked at, and I predict without evidence which way their separation distribution and their newly-possible UNREACHED rate will fall. The pre-registration commits me to publishing both whatever they are.

Prior art is unresolved on the axis I touch least. Stability radius, radius of robust feasibility, Renegar's distance to ill-posedness, AGM contraction and the MUS/MCS minimal-correction-set literature are all entirely unsearched — zero corpus hits, zero queries run — and the retraction operator claimed as the unshared differentiator against Taeb, Guo & Henckel may be contraction under another name. That must close before A4's differentiation paragraph is written, along with Appendix F.3 (three failed retrievals, conflicting section-6 readings) and the disputed identity of arXiv:2010.08611.

The protocol has no interventional or effect-level leg. It validates a certificate about adjustment-set validity, not about a realised intervention, and the field is measurably moving from structure-level to effect-level validation. That is deliberate — no real dataset carries both a domain-accepted graph and ground-truth interventional effects — but a reviewer from that direction will read it as a gap, and the answer must be written rather than left to be discovered.

The protocol still has no decision-relevant quantity beyond calibration, and that is the failure mode that sank our own restrained paper, where both reviewers read 'stability not correctness' as a ceiling rather than a strength. EVPPI is the off-the-shelf answer and it needs a loss function this project has not written; I have not written one either, and a decision-analysis lens would put it on the critical path instead of the referent.

The cost curve behind the cap-17 decision rests on four timed points plus the known ecoli70 wall, all on one machine, and the extrapolation between 18 and 25 undirected edges is a two-point geometric fit. If enumeration cost is not smooth in that range — and extension counts are not smooth, since sachs has 336 extensions at 17 edges while insurance has 41 at 18 — the cap is set from a curve that is really a scatter, and the honest fallback is to raise or lower it after the first arm-run rather than to defend the number.
name: Four Answerers, One Observable Frame
one_sentence: Nothing generates the knowledge and nothing chooses the questions: the question set itself is re-derived from analyst-observable quantities alone — 424 load-bearing edges over 29 networks and 5,032 candidate treatment-outcome pairs, against a questionnaire the draft had scoped by which pairs a true-DAG gate happened to admit — and then four suppliers, the published authors of the applied DAGs, a small round of analysts, an LLM surrogate and the repository's own mechanical operators, each answer that frozen questionnaire, so the framework's claim about practice becomes a paired two-sample gap on a fixed instance set with a bridge back to every number already in circulation.
primary_table: THE ANSWERER TABLE. One table, one fixed instance set, one questionnaire, two printed blocks that are never pooled. ROWS, one per knowledge supplier: R1 published-author; R2 human analyst; R3 surrogate (named); R3 surrogate (scrambled); G-oracle (knowledge_to_recover at coverage 1.0); G-flip at 0.25; G-tiered; NULL; MISSING. COLUMNS in two groups. Group one, what the knowledge looks like: n instances; n assertions; coverage per granularity (required / forbidden / tier / ancestral, never pooled); median graph distance from X to an assertion; commission rate with Wilson 95%; omission rate with Wilson 95%; CONSISTENT-BUT-FALSE fraction (the headline error quantity, named rather than folded into 'noise'); Meek Algorithm-1 rejection rate pre- and post-filter (identically zero in every number published so far, live for the first time here); median cascade size; cycles before repair; compelled-edge contradiction rate. Group two, what the radius does: share at r = 1; median r; max r; UNREACHED rate (zero in every published real-side number purely because the deleted gate certified a one-hop failure, and predicted non-zero here); shell failure fraction phi(r+1); agreement with the bound r_val <= min(s, |K_G0|); share the post-hoc audit calls DANGEROUS; share on which the incumbent RoCA test would have fired. Every row carries true_dag_on_path and every cell carries seed dispersion wherever a seed exists; rates without a seed say so rather than implying stability. The header states the instance count and the discordant-pair count D, so an underpowered comparison is visible before any p-value. A ROW MEANS: this is what the breakdown radius looks like when THIS is where the knowledge came from, on the same questions, pairs, gate and estimator. TWO BLOCKS: Tier A (8 applied networks, 595 pairs, truth is a published author's diagram) and Tier B (benchmark, truth is a curated network), printed separately because they are different objects. ONE APPENDED BLOCK, the bridge stratum: the same nine rows restricted to the 543 pairs the legacy true-DAG gate admitted, so every figure in the six committed reports has a recomputed twin beside it and no reader has to guess whether a change came from the redesign or from the population. The referee reads down the r=1 column and sees whether the surrogate sits with the humans or with the oracle-derived generator; that single comparison is the paper's entire claim about practice.
total_budget: WALL-CLOCK, roughly 9 to 13 days of machine time, most of it idle. Under 1 hour to re-screen the 38,658 already-enumerated distinct pairs under the observables-only frame, since the frame is graph-only and was executed end to end in seconds while designing this protocol — the draft's 'one day' was wrong by two orders of magnitude. About 2 days for the deployment sweep: 75.1% of 5,032 candidate pairs sit inside the derived cap of 17, roughly 3,779 pairs, at about 1.2 s per pair, over 36 arm-runs (six deterministic arms plus three stochastic arms at ten seeds each), about 45 hours. 3 days for the component-restriction differential, bounded by a written rule (only pairs whose whole-graph undirected count is at most 18, where the measured worst case is 7.3 s) with per-network caps and its own censoring record. 1 to 2 days for the matched-Erdős-Rényi control. 2 to 3 days for the finite-n panel, CUT to six networks selected by a written rule; the uncut corpus version was 3 to 4 weeks and is the scope this protocol explicitly abandons. Under 1 day for surrogate elicitation, roughly 5,600 to 6,600 cached calls, tens of dollars. AGENT-HOURS, roughly 100 to 115: the filter surgery, possde frame and questionnaire-cut script (~10); the questionnaire builder and four answerer adapters against the fully specified but entirely NotImplementedError elicit.py / taxonomy.py / perturb.py / distances.py scaffold (~28); the knowledge record schema, cascade statistic, consistent-but-false accounting, scale bridge, compelled-edge block, prompt-variant plumbing and confidence-calibration gate (~22); the shell measure, forbidden-edge and tier retraction moves and the sentinel extension to UNREACHED, NOT-REACHED and the three r_0 statuses (~15); the dependency-closed restriction, its theorem and its differential harness (~22); the manifest invariant field with its build-failing assertion extended over questionnaire provenance, the bridge-audit script, and the committed generator script the control arm has never had (~15). HUMAN-HOURS, roughly 60 to 80, and they are Zé's plus one second coder plus up to five analysts: fetching and reading the eight applied source papers 8 to 12 h with a real paywall risk (the gap-fill pass hit 403 at four journals); two independent coders converting prose to the response grammar, 12 to 16 h across two people; the elicitation round — instrument 6 to 8 h, recruiting to five 6 to 9 h, five sittings at up to 1.7 h, scoring 3 h, about 25 h; pre-registration, the CFP-style section checklist, and prior-art closure on Appendix F.3, arXiv:2010.08611's identity and the entirely unsearched stability-radius family, 15 to 20 h. THE BINDING CONSTRAINT IS NOT COMPUTE AND NOT AGENT TIME. It is the second coder and the analyst round. Every other line can be run by one person and a machine; the referent cannot, which is why the recruitment fallback (fewer than 3 analysts completing means the human anchor is reported ABSENT and the word 'expert' is struck everywhere), the harvest fallback (pre-adjudication kappa below 0.61 means the harvested arm is reported as failed) and the Tier C abandonment rule are pre-registered rather than improvised. There is no deadline pressure on any of it, which is the one condition under which building a referent instead of citing one is the right trade.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_r: The surrogate and human rows sit close on the A6-1 feature vector (exchangeability not rejected), and BOTH sit far from G-oracle on cascade size and on the radius distribution, with G-oracle's r=1 share the highest of the three — meaning every headline published so far is optimistic and the honest radius on elicited knowledge is larger, in the same direction the wrong-knowledge sweep already measured (r=1 share falling 57.8 to 42.1% as error rises, median 1 to 2, s>=2 share 40.6 to 49.5%). A2's documented-pair recovery check returns at least 6 of 12, so applied authors' own queries become measurable for the first time and the domain-documented stratum the pre-registration promised finally has rows in it. The observables-only frame delivers its measured expansion — 5,032 candidate pairs over 29 networks against 543 over 25 — and the 543-pair bridge stratum shows the legacy headlines reproduce inside the new pipeline, so the redesign is a superset rather than a replacement and six committed reports stay usable. The real-side UNREACHED rate becomes non-zero once the gate that manufactured its zero is removed, and is reported as a finding rather than hidden as a defect. A5's dependency-closed differential returns zero disagreements, the cap rises from 12 to 17, tractable coverage of the candidate population goes from 44.8% to 75.1%, the 280 intractable pairs and 3 censored runs are recovered, and r_val and r_0 become measurable on the SAME instances for the first time. phi(r+1) is reported alongside r so the certificate is stated as a bound with measured slack rather than as a tolerance. A6-3 rejects on the matched control, so the audit demonstrably has power for mechanical knowledge and A6-1's non-rejections mean something. And the audit arm shows DANGEROUS at a low single-digit percentage under the 95% band, conditional on r, on instances where the incumbent RoCA test would NOT have fired — the only form in which pricing beats testing, measured on the same data rather than asserted.
what_it_would_show_if_the_framework_is_w: Seven concrete, pre-registered ways this protocol kills the framework, each reachable inside the stated budget. (1) THE SURROGATE IS A MEMORISER. A6-4 shows the named-minus-scrambled gap above the pre-registered threshold AND cold recall reproducing the published adjacency above chance on the Tier B networks carrying most of the instances. The LLM-as-expert-surrogate decision then fails on the tier where the data is, and the paper is left with the applied tier and an 82-question human anchor, which is a workshop paper. (2) THE REFERENT AND THE GENERATOR ARE INDISTINGUISHABLE. A6-1 fails to reject AND A3's cascade test fails to separate knowledge_to_recover from the human and surrogate answerers on the same edges.
